author: koki-ishikawa-aforce
body:
## Summary
This PR implements comprehensive API endpoints for transaction management, expense settlement, and master data operations. It adds support for manual transaction creation/editing, bulk classification sessions, retroactive rule application, monthly expense cycles, CSV imports, and master data management for categories and expense types.

## Key Changes

### New Route Handlers
- **Classification Routes** (`classification.ts`): Retroactive rule application, bulk classification sessions, merchant/Amazon learning rules management
- **Transaction Routes** (enhanced): Manual transaction creation, editing, deletion, and classification
- **Expense Settlement Routes** (enhanced): Monthly expense cycle management, CSV confirmation, finalization with deposit matching, prorated child transaction generation
- **Imports Routes** (enhanced): CSV upload/parsing, transaction candidate confirmation, daily mail batch management
- **Categories Routes** (`categories.ts`): CRUD operations for custom categories with rename/delete restrictions
- **Expense Types Routes** (`expense_types.ts`): CRUD operations for custom expense types with rename/delete restrictions
- **Monthly Limits Routes** (`monthly_limits.ts`): Monthly spending cap management per expense type

### Core Utilities
- **CSV Parser** (`parse-statement-csv.ts`): Robust statement CSV parsing with date/amount validation, header detection, and detailed error reporting
- **Role Mapping** (`role_mapping.ts`): Maps user roles to personal expense classes for unclassified transactions

### Repository & Domain Enhancements
- Added `deleteById` methods to `CategoryMasterRepository` and `ExpenseTypeMasterRepository`
- Added `renameCustomExpenseType` domain function for expense type renaming
- Enhanced `TransactionCandidateRepository` with sorting support
- Enhanced `AmazonProductKeyLearningRuleRepository` with sorting support

### Dependency Injection
- Updated `composition-root.ts` to wire all new repositories and queries
- Added mock repository implementations for testing
- Updated route registration in `app.ts` with new endpoints and dependency injection

### Error Handling
- Enhanced error handler middleware to support `InvariantViolationError`
- Consistent permission and ownership validation across all routes

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Ownership Validation**: All routes enforce user ownership checks (e.g., `assertOwnedByViewer`, `assertCycleOwnedByViewer`)
- **State Machine Enforcement**: Bulk classification and expense settlement routes validate state transitions (e.g., `assertInProgress`)
- **CSV Parsing**: Handles multiple date formats (YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY-MM-DD), normalizes merchant names (NFKC), supports quoted fields and comma-separated amounts
- **Retroactive Application**: Validates that merchant learning rules are fully learned before retroactive application
- **Bulk Operations**: Supports filtering and selective application of transactions in bulk classification and settlement workflows
- **Master Data Restrictions**: Custom categories/expense types can only be renamed/deleted by their creator; default items are immutable

author: michalmoronga-alt
body:
## Čo sa mení z pohľadu používateľa

Pri výbere ABS hrany **dielca** aj **dosky** sa zoznam pások teraz rozdelí na dve skupiny:

- **„Odporúčané k dekoru"** navrchu — pásky s rovnakým dekorom ako výsledný materiál dielca/dosky (zoradené hrúbkou vzostupne: 1,0 → 2,0),
- **„Ostatné"** pod tým — zvyšok katalógu.

V drvivej väčšine prípadov sa k danému dekoru používa jedna konkrétna páska — používateľ ju teraz nájde okamžite hore, nemusí ju loviť v celom zozname. Keď sa v karte zmení materiál, skupiny sa prepočítajú hneď (netreba čakať na prekreslenie z modelu).

**Nič sa nemení automaticky** — je to čisto zoradenie/zoskupenie ponuky. Žiadna ABS hodnota sa sama neprepíše (filozofia D-32: nič sa nedeje ticho). Jednoklikové olepenie k dekoru rieši naďalej existujúca ikona (D-35).

## Rozhodnutia

- **B2 (owner decision):** skupina „Odporúčané" = **všetky** ABS pásky, ktorých dekor sa **presne** zhoduje s dekorom výsledného materiálu, zoradené **hrúbkou vzostupne**. Bez per-hrana pravidiel. Dekor sa porovnáva case-sensitívne, presne ako ho drží katalóg (žiadne fuzzy); porovnanie znáša len orezanie okrajových medzier.
- **B1:** odporúčanie sa počíta v JS **pri renderi** zo živého katalógu `MATERIALS` (sync cez `NX.setMaterials`), nie z uloženého per-card payloadu — po zmene katalógu za behu je ponuka vždy aktuálna. Žiadne nové polia v payloadoch dielca/dosky.
- **F4:** materiál s prázdnym/legacy dekorom → skupina „Odporúčané" sa vôbec nezobrazí, ponuka je plochý zoznam bez optgroup. To isté platí, keď dekor nemá v katalógu žiadnu zhodnú pásku.
- **F5:** aktuálne vybraná ABS hodnota, ktorá už nie je v katalógu (legacy/zmazaná), sa zachová ako položka v „Ostatné" — nikdy ju neprebije prvá odporúčaná páska.
- **F3:** po zmene materiálu v karte sa selecty pregrupujú lokálne z `MATERIALS`. Pri zrušení override dielca (návrat na dedenie) sa lokálne neráta — počká sa na resolved payload z Ruby (JS nový zdedený materiál nepozná).
- **N7:** zmena je čisto prezentačná — žiadne umelé `change` eventy, žiadny extra `NX.loadBoard`, žiadny zásah do echo-guardov ani `boardPending`.

Grouping je napísaný ako čistá funkcia (`groupAbsEdges` + `absOptionsHtml` + `normDecor`) v `core.js` a zdieľaný medzi kartou dielca aj dosky — jeden zdroj pravdy.

## Ako testované

- **JS unit testy (nové):** `tests/js/test_abs_groups.js` — 32 assertov: zhoda dekoru + zoradenie hrúbkou, case-sensitivita, F4 (prázdny/nil/whitespace dekor + žiadna zhoda), F5 (preserve), stavba HTML (optgroupy vs plochý zoznam, poradie, escapovanie). Pridaný krok do `.github/workflows/tests.yml`.
- **JS regresie:** `test_expr.js` 46/0, `test_insert_state.js` 42/0, `test_usage.js` 35/0.
- **Ruby headless:** `ruby tests/run_all.rb` → **317/0** (Ruby sa zmena nedotýka, overené že nič nerozbila).
- **Kvalita:** `git diff --check` čistý; všetky menené súbory UTF-8 bez BOM; panel.html cache-bust jednotne `0.4.7y`; žiadny nový hex mimo tokenov (zmena sa CSS/farieb netýka).

## Čo vedome nespravené / na ručné overenie

- **In-SketchUp vizuálne overenie** (otvorenie panela, optgroupy v selecte hrany dielca a dosky, správanie po zmene materiálu) — VBO SkAgent bridge počas prípravy PR nebežal (0 inštancií), preto to treba prekliknúť lokálne. Logika je pokrytá unit testami, zmena je izolovaná do options builderov.
- **Bez per-hrana odporúčaní** — vedome (B2). Odporúčanie je len podľa dekoru výsledného materiálu, rovnaké pre všetky štyri hrany.

author: agstttt
body:
то сделано
Новая модель CategoryBanner в схеме Prisma — баннер-слайд для главной страницы: изображение (R2), ссылка на Category, порядок сортировки, статус активности. Без переводимых полей — баннер только изображение + ссылка на категорию.
Публичный эндпоинт GET /api/category-banners — только активные баннеры, отсортированы по sortOrder, с slug и трёхъязычным названием связанной категории (для alt-текста и ссылки в каталог).
Админ-эндпоинты GET/POST /api/admin/category-banners и PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/category-banners/[id] — по образцу существующих product-images (multipart-загрузка в R2, те же лимиты 5 МБ/jpeg-png-webp). PATCH всегда multipart, файл необязателен — если передан новый файл, старый объект в R2 удаляется после успешного обновления БД.
Админ-панель — новый раздел «Баннеры категорий» в сайдбаре: таблица со списком (превью, категория, порядок, статус) + форма создания/редактирования (выбор категории, загрузка изображения через новый компонент SingleImageUpload, порядок, переключатель активности).
Секция на главной странице — карусель с ручным управлением (стрелки + полоски-индикаторы, зацикливание), без автопрокрутки (по DESIGN §10). Располагается сразу после Hero, перед «Новинки». Каждый слайд ведёт на /catalog?category=<slug>. При отсутствии активных баннеров секция не рендерится вообще (без пустого отступа).
Высота слайда — фиксированная по брейкпоинтам (180px моб. / 320px планшет / 480px десктоп), не пропорция aspect-ratio. Решение принято вживую вместе с вами после сравнения обрезки на тестовом фото: оказалось, что при чистой пропорции 3:1 баннер слишком тонкий на мобильных, а единая фиксированная высота на всех экранах — наоборot, доминирует на мобильном. Итоговая обрезка: ~18% на мобильном, ~26% на планшете, ~41% на десктопе (десктоп обрезает больше всего, хоть и самый высокий — потому что 1440/480=3:1 самое широкое соотношение из трёх). Рекомендация для фотографа: держать главный объект в центральных ~60% кадра по вертикали.
Чего НЕ касался
src/middleware.ts — не редактировался. Новые админ-маршруты уже покрыты существующим паттерном /api/admin/:path*.
prisma/migrations — по-прежнему отсутствуют (известный пробел проекта, не мой).
DESIGN.md — не редактировался (файл только для вас). Отмечу: фиксированная высота по брейкпоинтам — новый паттерн геометрии, которого нет в таблице соотношений §8. Возможно, стоит добавить туда явно.
На что обратить внимание при ревью
Точный финальный блок схемы — скопируйте себе для db push (применялось через db push, не migrate, как и весь проект):

model CategoryBanner {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  imageUrl   String   @map("image_url")
  imageKey   String   @map("image_key")
  categoryId String   @map("category_id")
  sortOrder  Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  isActive   Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  category Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([sortOrder])
  @@index([categoryId])
  @@map("category_banners")
}
Плюс одна строка в модель Category:

categoryBanners CategoryBanner[]
Удаление категории каскадно удаляет связанные с ней баннеры (по вашему решению) — но R2-объект баннера в этом случае НЕ удаляется автоматически (та же особенность, что у Product→Brand, не новая проблема).
Проверено сквозным тестированием через реальные загрузки в R2 (без моков): создание/редактирование/замена изображения/удаление, каскад категории, авторизация, публичный эндпоинт, рендер на /ru и /en, фильтрация каталога по ссылке баннера, пустое состояние.
tsc --noEmit и eslint чисты, только 2 старых предупреждения (не мои).

author: secherkasov
body:
Six reviewers went over everything merged into `main` today (#36, #38–#42) — nothing in that batch had been reviewed before merging. This fixes all ten findings plus three minor ones. Every claim was verified against the code before it was acted on.

## Blockers

- **Recording had two writers.** `startRecording`/`stopRecording` ran on the UI thread while the PTY collector wrote chunks into the same `SessionRecorder` on `Dispatchers.Default`. Stopping a recording on a busy session (`tail -f`, build logs) could corrupt the `.cast`. The recorder now lives on the command loop that already owns the emulator; stop waits for it, so every chunk queued before the stop is in the file.
- **Playback ran on the main dispatcher.** `CastPlayerOverlay` fed the ANSI parser from `Dispatchers.Main` while live sessions use `Default`. Seeking near the end of a long take froze the UI — ANR-class on Android.
- **The size cap counted the wrong thing.** `bytes += chunk.length` counted source UTF-16 units while the buffer holds the JSON-escaped form (an `ESC` is 1 character and 6 escaped; a CJK glyph is 3 bytes). On TUI-heavy output the buffer grew several times past the intended 32 MB.

## The rest

- Exported `.cast` files were written at the default umask (`-rw-r--r--`). They hold whatever the server printed; they now get the same 0600 as every other private file Skerry writes.
- Broadcast reported "sent to N" from a queue write that never fails, so a host whose transport had just dropped counted as reached. Delivery is judged on `TerminalState` now, and `broadcastTargets` — the function deciding which shells a broadcast reaches — has tests for the first time.
- `Ctrl+Shift+S/R/P` became reserved by the shell in #42, silently killing any snippet already bound to them. The editor now warns.
- A category chip showed multi-tagged snippets twice, once under each of their other tags.
- Both command palettes laid out up to 200 rows eagerly on every keystroke; they are lazy now, and the fuzzy matcher's match positions — computed, carried to the UI, then dropped — highlight the match.
- `historyKey` kept pointing at a disconnected host; the desktop chip row was unkeyed.

## Tests

Nine new tests, written before the fixes: escape/UTF-8 accounting and a backwards clock step in the recorder, undelivered broadcast targets, `broadcastTargets` coverage (split panes in, unconnected and VNC out), multi-tag chip grouping, reserved-chord matching.

`:composeApp:desktopTest` and `:shared:desktopTest` pass; desktop and Android targets both compile.

**Not verified by eye yet** — worth a look before merging: match highlighting in the palette, the reserved-chord warning in the snippet editor, and the mobile palette, whose list structure changed when it became a `LazyColumn`.

author: michaelqee
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a Windows desktop boot failure loop: when a messaging platform with a
heavy SDK (e.g. Feishu/`lark_oapi`) is configured, the desktop never gets
past "Waiting for Hermes backend to become ready" — the backend announces
its port, the readiness probe times out at 15s, the desktop kills the
backend and retries forever.

**Root cause:** the first `/api/status` request after startup lazily
imports the configured platform's adapter module, which imports its SDK at
module level. `lark_oapi` alone is ~11k generated modules (~98 MB); with
Windows Defender (or any real-time AV) scanning each file, that import
blocks the asyncio event loop for 15-60s. The desktop's readiness fetch
times out at 15s (`DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`), aborts the request (which
cancels the in-flight import mid-tree), retries — each attempt re-pays the
cost — declares boot failure, kills the backend, and starts over. Because
the backend is killed before ever finishing, the loop never converges.

**Fix:** pay the import cost *before* announcing readiness. Between the
uvicorn socket bind and the `HERMES_(BACKEND|DASHBOARD)_READY` print, the
server now resolves every *connected* platform through the platform
registry (`_warm_configured_platform_sdks()`), which triggers the deferred
platform-module import — the same lazy path the first request would take.
The desktop's port-announce window is 90s (`backend-ready.ts`), so the
announcement still arrives comfortably in time, and the first readiness
probe then answers in milliseconds. The helper is best-effort: any failure
is logged at debug level and ignored, so a broken config can never block
server startup (the lazy request-time path remains as fallback).

This follows the precedent already in the codebase for the same Windows
cold-import problem: `hermes_cli.gateway`'s first import is offloaded to a
thread in `/api/status` (see the comment there about 15-30s cold-import
stalls), and `_lifespan` warms it via `run_in_executor` for the same reason.

## Related Issue

Related to #50209.
Note: #50209 addressed a different root cause for the same symptom; this PR fixes the same Windows cold-import boot-loop issue when the configured messaging platform SDK is lazily imported at the first `/api/status` request.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/web_server.py`: add `_warm_configured_platform_sdks()` helper
  and call it in `_serve()` between `_read_bound_port()` and the
  `HERMES_(BACKEND|DASHBOARD)_READY` announcement (both `serve` and
  `dashboard` paths share `_serve()`).
- `tests/test_web_server_platform_warmup.py`: new tests — resolves exactly
  the connected platforms through the registry, no-op when none are
  connected, and swallows config/registry failures.

## How to Test

Reproduction (Windows, Feishu configured in `config.yaml`, cold venv):

1. `python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`
2. Immediately `curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/status` on the announced
   port.

Before the fix: the first request hangs 15-60s (py-spy shows the main
thread importing `lark_oapi\api\...\__init__.py`), so the desktop's 15s
readiness fetch times out and boot loops. After the fix:

1. Same `serve` command — the `HERMES_BACKEND_READY` announcement is
   delayed (~23s here) while the SDK import happens *before* it.
2. First `/api/status` probe after the announcement: **HTTP 200 in ~0.2s**.

Desktop end-to-end (`hermes desktop --source`): boot reaches
"Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup" instead of the
timeout/respawn loop.

Unit tests: `pytest tests/test_web_server_platform_warmup.py -v` (4 passed),
plus existing `pytest tests/test_web_server.py -q` (4 passed, no
regressions). `ruff check` clean.

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (Python 3.11.15, Electron 40.10.2)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before (desktop.log, repeating forever):

```
[hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=59538
[hermes] [boot] Waiting for Hermes backend to become ready
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend did not become ready:
Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
```

py-spy during the hang (main thread = event loop):

```
<module> (lark_oapi\api\corehr\v2\model\__init__.py:703)
<module> (lark_oapi\api\corehr\v2\__init__.py:1)
<module> (lark_oapi\ws\client.py:21)
...
```

After:

```
HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=53801        # announced after ~23s warm-up
GET /api/status -> HTTP 200 in 0.21s   # first probe, previously 15-60s
[hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
```

## Summary
- `sw.js`'s `fetch` handler applied its cache-first strategy to every GET request with no origin check, so cross-origin API calls (GG.deals price checks, Steam lookups) fell into the same path meant for static assets. A repeat request with an identical URL — e.g. the same wishlist App IDs on the next "Check Live Prices" run — could be served straight from a stale cache entry instead of hitting the network, which is why a check could show no price movement even hours after the real price had changed.
- Cross-origin GET requests now always go straight to the network and are never written into the service worker cache.
- Added a cache-busting timestamp (`&_=${Date.now()}`) to the GG.deals and Steam worker fetch URLs as defense in depth, matching the convention already used for every Apps Script request in this codebase.
- Bumped the service worker cache version so any previously-cached cross-origin responses get purged on next activation.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified in a headless browser: the service worker installs/activates cleanly, same-origin assets (`app.js`, `style.css`) still get cache-first served and populate the cache as before.
- [x] Verified a cross-origin fetch (Steam worker URL) is never written into any service worker cache bucket, confirming the new routing bypasses caching entirely for cross-origin requests.
- [x] Verified the routing logic against the full set of request shapes the app makes (same-origin assets, `btb-url.js`, navigation requests, GG.deals worker, Steam worker) — each resolves to the intended strategy.

author: brazilofmux
body:
## Summary
Step 1 of #996 (found by Kagura's review — thanks, this was the class neither the wrapper audit nor any corpus could see): `%q` SUBST slots are 256 bytes, so register values >255 bytes silently truncated on the JIT route (`setq(0,repeat(x,300))` + a `%q0` read → 258 instead of 303, `eval_handled=1`, verified on macOS matching the Linux report).

- **Entry-side decline:** `marshal_qregs_to_slots` reports a masked register exceeding `SUBST_SLOT-1`; both entry-marshal sites decline to the AST evaluator (side-effect-free — nothing has executed). New `bail_longreg` jitstats counter.
- **Mid-program resync still truncates** (cannot decline after side effects) — that's step 2, **designed for review** in the plan doc: a guest-memory long-register bitmap maintained by marshal/`ECALL_SETQ`/resync, with `%q` reads lowered to a bit-test diamond (short path = today's slot materialization at zero new cost; long path = `fun_r` ECALL to authoritative `global_regs`). Feasibility pre-checked: `OUT_SLOT` = LBUF, so long values flow intact through ECALL results/output slots/STRCAT — only the `%q` slots are narrow. Three open questions flagged (bitmap address, mask-unknown marshal cost, scope-restore interaction).
- **Corpus:** `JITDIFF_LONGREG=1` — interpreter preamble sets `%q9` straddling 256 bytes, measured expression reads it. Mid-program setq-then-read shapes deliberately excluded until step 2.
- **TC017** locks the decline via a fresh `u()` inner evaluation: 300 → decline (303), 200 → JIT path (203).

## Testing
- Repro: **303** (was 258), `eval_bailout=1 bail_longreg=1`
- Smoke: **1317/1317 both toggles** · Oracle 7/7
- Sweeps: standard, longreg ×2 seeds, longreg+utf8+brackets — all **400/0 LOGIC**

Kagura: the step-2 design section in `docs/plan-jit-evalbracket-lift.md` is the review request — particularly the three open questions at the end.

body:
## Summary

Generalizes the wallet-only `WalletMoments` delight bus into a shared `SourceMoments` bus (hue-aware: a moment names its source and the berry rain falls in that source's brand color), then uses it — plus a few row/hero/empty-state touches — to add surprise & delight across the per-source feeds, following the honesty rules already established for the Wallet pass (prd §79) and the "no streaks, no goals, no guilt mechanics" law (build-brief §10).

- **Moments (new `SourceMoments` bus, `Model/SourceMoments.swift`)**
  - A watched token crossing +25% since its watch-time anchor fires once, ever, per token (`TokenPulse`).
  - A Bitrefill balance refill fires when the cached balance rises (`BitrefillBridge`).
  - A watched Farcaster/Bluesky account posting again after a real 30+ day quiet stretch fires — self-throttling by construction, a read-only pass that never touches the ingest internals (new `SocialMoments`).
  - Pulling to refresh inside one source's own feed now rains in that source's hue instead of the app's default blue (`BerryRain`, `FeedScreen`).
- **"On this day" (new `OnThisDay.swift`)** — every habit source's calendar-heatmap card (Photos, Day One, Apple Journal, Obsidian, Notion, Apple Health, Strava, ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini, Farcaster, Bluesky, plus GitHub's own graph) now surfaces a real match from the same day in a prior year, when one exists — rides inside the SAME card rather than competing for the feed's one-hero-per-source slot. The card also gained a text `ShareLink` for the year's own stats.
- **Cross-source recognition (new `CrossSourceEcho.swift`)** — a link already saved from a different source echoes quietly on its row ("Also saved from X"). Exact-URL matches only, to avoid a wrong "you already saved this" reading as a bug.
- **Try-it chips (`FeedScreen`)** — empty Tokens/Stocktwits/RSS feeds offer a one-tap "Watch ETH" / "Watch $AAPL" / "Follow NASA's feed" chip, generalizing the Wallet screen's existing "Peek at vitalik.eth".
- **Per-source milestones (new `ThingMilestones.swift`)** — crossing a round total of things from one source flashes "N things banked from Source." once per threshold, ever.

Every moment is a fact the corpus can prove, fires at most once per occasion, and is asymmetric where a loss is possible (a drop never fires — same rule as the wallet's new-high mark).

## Environment note

This session ran in a Linux sandbox with no Xcode/simulator toolchain, so I could not run `xcodebuild`, `scripts/verify.sh`, or the simulator screen sweep. I reviewed every change line-by-line for correctness (types, signatures, actor isolation, brace balance) against existing precedents in the codebase, and `scripts/catalog-sync.sh` passes, but **please run the full build + `scripts/verify.sh` + a simulator pass before merging** — this diff has not been compiled.

- [ ] Confirm a link saved from two different sources shows "Also saved from X" on the later row

## The reimagining (operator-directed)

- **The 2³ ladder amortized:** `CausalMask`'s 8 rungs become **8 canonical `NamedView` masks over ONE `SpoFacet` register** — the register is written once, the Pearl rungs are projections. Counterfactual (rung `SPO`) = `distance(spo(), witness())` — the semantic triple contrasted against the AriGraph episodic-witness triple, each pair one palette256² table read (`contract::distance`, generalizes to larger codebooks).
- **Self-awareness on the better substrate:** the CE64 signed inference mantissa (direction × NARS rule) + truth are **consumed from M20 A6 (`DirectionInferenceFacet`) / A3 (`NarsTruthFacet`)** at full width — not re-planned, not crammed into 64 bits.
- **The standing wave:** Markov superposition of per-version rung readings over the `temporal.rs` sorted stream (`E-MARKOV-TEMPORAL-STREAM-1` — C-K exact by stream order). The "orientation for free" claim (what observational causal discovery pays super-exponential compute for) is stated **falsifiably** in §4 and gated on probe **D-CSW-1** (real text stream as temporal updates, registered margin vs single-cycle + the p64 3-bit-mask baseline).
- **Endgame — the graph reasoning about itself:** AriGraph basins promoted to causality-edge candidates carrying rung decomposition (D-CSW-2); entropy work driven by the rung-content ladder (144 verb atoms / the 34 NARS tactic recipes / frozen·learned·explore triangle); qualia texture → gestalt → `MulAssessment` (MetaCognition / MUL).

Everything is **CONJECTURE until probes D-CSW-1..3 report**; the probe is the next deliverable, not code. No bytes land before the M20 auditor + mint gates. No byte-sniffing — readings are ClassView-elected (le-contract §2; the #776 carving-verification finding). Metric only via `contract::distance`. No "wiring/replaces" claims without a caller.

author: luciferlive112116
body:
Closes #7634

## Summary

Extends the cross-repo evaluation harness (#4788) from **readiness-only** to a **full-execution** dry-run mode, so it answers not just "can the miner form a plan for this repo?" but "does the miner actually produce working, correct code?" — the real signal behind the #4810 launch-readiness bar.

A new `--full-execution` flag on the existing `packages/loopover-miner/scripts/cross-repo-evaluation.mjs` runs the discover → plan → code → test loop against the benchmark repos: it drives the configured coding-agent driver to generate a **real diff** in the local clone, builds the result, runs the target repo's **own test suite** locally, and checks the diff isn't a no-op. **Dry-run only** — it edits the clone and hard-resets it afterward; it never opens a PR, never pushes, and needs nothing beyond a local clone + a configured driver (the same safety posture the readiness harness already has).

### What's added
- **Execution taxonomy** (`CROSS_REPO_EXECUTION_CATEGORY`), extending the readiness taxonomy per the issue: `plan_not_formed`, `code_build_failed`, `tests_failed`, `no_op_diff` (tests passed but the diff was empty), plus the shared `clone_setup` / `other`.
- **`evaluateRepoFullExecution` / `runFullCrossRepoExecution`** — reuse `evaluateRepoReadiness` for the plan stage, then delegate the code/build/test steps to injectable seams (`runAgentAttempt`, `buildRepo`, `runRepoTests`) so the orchestration + taxonomy are unit-testable without a live agent.
- **`summarizeCrossRepoExecution` / `formatCrossRepoExecutionReport`** — an execution report in the same shape the readiness report already produces.
- **CLI `--full-execution` mode** wiring real dry-run seams: build/test spawn the repo's own commands in the clone; the agent seam runs the configured driver via `runCodingAgentAttempt` and captures `git diff`, then resets.
- **Docs** — `docs/cross-repo-evaluation.md` documents the new mode, taxonomy, and operator prerequisites.

## Scope

- [x] `--full-execution` mode on the *existing* CLI + lib module (no new script; no live PR submission against benchmark repos)
- [x] In scope (`packages/loopover-miner/**`, `test/**`), no `blockedPaths`; no secrets
- [x] No changelog / `site/` / `CNAME` / `lovable` edits

## Test Coverage

`packages/loopover-miner/**` is outside Codecov's `coverage.include` (`src/**` only), so no patch-coverage gate applies — but the new logic has real unit tests (`test/unit/miner-cross-repo-full-execution.test.ts`) following this package's conventions: every execution category and the pass path are exercised with injected fake seams, plus `runFullCrossRepoExecution`, the summary, the report, and the CLI arg/dispatch wiring.

## Validation

- [x] `tsc -p packages/loopover-miner/tsconfig.json` — new module compiles clean; emitted `.js`/`.d.ts` committed
- [x] `node --check` on the emitted `.js` and the CLI script
- [x] Readiness mode unchanged (`--full-execution` is additive); CLI `--help` documents the new flag
- [x] `vitest run` on the new test suite — green
- [x] Branch current with `main`

## Safety

- [x] Dry-run only — edits the local clone and hard-resets; never opens a PR, pushes, or writes to any benchmark repo
- [x] No forge API calls, no credentials beyond a local clone + a configured coding-agent driver

author: cornerblue
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw security audit` **silently skipped** workspace skill scanning when `workspace/skills` was a **directory symlink** (or Windows junction).

Why that is dangerous:
1. Operators often symlink `skills/` to a shared skills store.
2. A nested skill directory symlink can point **outside** the trusted skills root (malicious or accidental).
3. The audit used `lstat()` + `isDirectory()` on the skills root. For a dir symlink, `isDirectory()` is **false**, so the scan returned **zero** SKILL.md files and never emitted `skills.workspace.symlink_escape`.
4. Result: **fail-open security tooling** - the guard that is supposed to catch skill-path escapes was blind exactly when shared/symlinked skill roots are used.

## Fix

- Follow the top-level `workspace/skills` path with `fs.stat()` so directory symlinks/junctions are traversed
- Resolve and remember the skills root realpath
- Align containment with the skill loader: resolved skills root **or** `skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets`
- Require each `SKILL.md` realpath to stay inside its skill directory
- Regression tests for the symlinked-root blind spot and trusted allowlist targets

## Evidence

```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/skills/security/workspace-audit.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Key new coverage:
- nested escapes when `workspace/skills` itself is a symlink/junction
- no false positive when a nested skill is explicitly trusted via `skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets`

## Security notes

This restores a security-audit control-plane signal (not a remote unauth RCE). Without it, operators relying on `security audit` for workspace hygiene can miss skill symlink escapes on the common shared-skills layout.

Closes #111797

author: wingoblin
body:
## What & why

Reshape the Telegram deal-alert so the `@airpick` channel only pings on genuine steals (to lure people to the app), instead of on every `deals.json` refresh. Also cleans up the card and message.

## Selection

- **Round-trip only.**
- **Discount-gated:** discount ≥ **25%** off its own baseline (not just "cheap anyway"), AND price ≤ **500,000 KRW**.
- **Long-haul override:** a big enough drop (≥ **35%**) ignores the price ceiling, so half-off long-haul steals still get through.
- **Flexible count** (up to 6) — however many qualify, not a fixed 3.
- Trigger stays on `deals.json` updates + 24h per-deal dedupe → fires only when a standout deal actually appears; no spam, no cron. On current data this yields just Clark −38%.

All thresholds are env vars (`TELEGRAM_MIN_DISCOUNT`, `TELEGRAM_MAX_PRICE`, `TELEGRAM_PRICE_OVERRIDE_DISCOUNT`) — tune without code changes.

## Message & card

- Caption trimmed to one line: **`✈️ 실시간 특가알람`**.
- Per-deal booking-link buttons removed; replaced with fixed app-market buttons — **아이폰** (App Store) / **안드로이드** (Play Store).
- Card is more compact (width 440→360, tighter padding/fonts) and rendered at **3×** so it stays sharp instead of being upscaled/blurred by Telegram.
- Date line no longer bold (price is the only bold emphasis).

## Ops

- New `resend` workflow_dispatch input drops the dedupe window to 0 for a single manual test post.

## Verification

Ran live dispatches end-to-end: sends succeed, selection matches the rules (Clark/Da Nang/Kota Kinabalu under the earlier ≥20% bar; Clark only under the final ≥25% bar), synthetic tests confirm the ≥35% price override and round-trip/one-way gating. `py_compile` clean.

author: levi-qiao
body:
## Why

The supervisor was too low-power — it largely took the ledger's word for "done". You wanted it to actually **re-verify acceptance** from its outside context: catch where the executor drifted or concealed a shortcut, judged against the shared standards (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, ops.md) both nodes obey, and own commits + pending decisions + plan changes.

## What changed

The supervisor is now an **independent acceptance auditor**, while keeping the single-writer ledger invariant (it still never edits the ledger — plan changes flow through directives):

- **New step 3 — Independent acceptance audit.** Take the item(s) the ledger marks done since last tick and reproduce acceptance itself: re-run the gate/eval and inspect the real diff/artifact/call-site against the North Star acceptance criteria and the shared standards. Hunts for **drift** (scope narrowed, bar lowered, TODO left), **fake-done** (gate not actually run, test with no call site, metric from wrong set), **concealment** (skipped test, `--no-verify`, swallowed error, silently violated AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md).
- **Commit only what passes the audit** (step 4).
- **Steer the plan** (step 5): add/reprioritize/split items, insert acceptance checks, order redos of audit-failed work — via directives; executor applies to the ledger.
- **ops.md** gains a "Standards / conventions" section — the canonical shared yardstick.
- Reframed across SKILL.md, README(.zh-CN), and methodology §8.

Docs/prompts only. Preserves clean-context separation and single-writer ledger.

author: garycoding
body:
## What & why

Makes the **main process the single authority over task data**, so the GUI today and an in-app MCP server later share **one write path** over the same model. This is the foundation PR from the settled MCP design (`docs/mcp_ideas.md`), split out so it stands on its own and de-risks the server that follows. **No user-visible behaviour change.**

Before: the renderer parsed `forest.json5`, applied mutations, validated, and handed opaque text to main, which only wrote bytes. After: the pure model moves to a shared location; main owns a task service over the store's atomic reads/writes; the renderer is reduced to a caller.

## Changes

- **Relocate the pure model** `src/renderer/src/model/` → `src/shared/model/` verbatim (five sources, their tests, the fixtures — all 100% renames), so both the main and renderer builds import it. Importers repointed.
- **Shared task-authority core** `src/shared/taskOps.js`: `runTaskOp` and `readForest` own the one write path (load text → parse → migrate → apply one pure mutation → re-validate → persist), parameterised by synchronous storage callbacks. **Synchronous by design**, so a per-op run never yields the event loop between load and save; concurrent callers (the GUI, and later MCP) serialise with no lock.
- **Main task service** `src/main/taskService.js` over `store.js`, exposing `readForest` and an **allowlisted** `taskOp`. Two new IPC channels (`pensagrex:read-forest`, `pensagrex:task-op`) plus the preload methods. The coarse `load/save-forest` handlers stay for seeding and one-time migration writes; `store.js` is unchanged.
- **Renderer reduced to a caller**: `openDomain` reads via `api.readForest`; every edit is `applyOp(name, ...args)` → `api.taskOp` instead of a local mutation + debounced save. The forest debounce (`saveForestDebounced` / `cancelPendingSave` / `flushSaves`) is retired; notes keep their own autosave. The in-memory **fallback runs the same shared core** over its Map, so a no-Electron edit behaves identically.
- **Single-instance lock**: one process is one authority (and, for the coming MCP server, one binder of the fixed loopback port); the window reference is hoisted so `second-instance` focuses it.

## Tests & verification

- New `src/main/taskService.test.js` drives the authority against a real temp library: each op loads/mutates/validates/persists; an invariant-breaking op and an unknown op each return an error and **write nothing**; `readForest` migrates a schema-1 forest and persists once; `pasteAsTree` writes the note files. Relocated model tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run lint` clean · `npm test` **189 passing** · `npm run build` OK (the shared core bundles into **both** `out/main` and `out/renderer`) · `reuse lint` compliant.
- **Running renderer** over its fallback: opened a domain (renders through `api.readForest`), added a task via the context menu (through `api.taskOp`); the map re-rendered in place with no console errors.

## Not in this PR

The MCP server itself (SDK, loopback Streamable-HTTP endpoint on 35899, scope tiers, tool surface) is PR 2; live view updates and note-editor reconciliation are PR 3. The 2.0.0 milestone question is a release-time decision.

author: cykatherine
body:
## Summary

The `build.yml` "Deploy to Maven Central" step runs `./gradlew publish` on every push to `main`. The project is configured with `SONATYPE_HOST=CENTRAL_PORTAL` (`gradle.properties`), which routes publishes to `central.sonatype.com`. The Sonatype Central Portal **does not support SNAPSHOT publishing** — with the current `VERSION_NAME=2.2.0-SNAPSHOT`, the step fails with a `403 Forbidden` on every push to `main`.

## Change

- Added a `Read version name` step that extracts `VERSION_NAME` from `gradle.properties` into a step output.
- Gated the publish step with `!endsWith(steps.version.outputs.name, '-SNAPSHOT')` so it only runs for release (non-SNAPSHOT) versions.
- Renamed the step from "Deploy SNAPSHOT to Maven Central" to "Deploy to Maven Central" to reflect that it now only publishes releases.

- [x] Pushes to `main` no longer fail due to the SNAPSHOT publish step (step is now skipped for `-SNAPSHOT`)

body:
Close backlog #1047 (repo-creation 422 swallow / unique repo names) as obsoleted by codegen_orchestrator-646.

The collision premise is structurally impossible: repo name is `org/{project.slug}` and `generate_project_slug` (`shared/project_slug.py`) appends the full `project_id.hex`, so two distinct projects can never share a repo name even with identical titles — the exact fix #1047 proposed, delivered stronger (full UUID vs short hash). Docs-only, no code change.

author: eugenelim
body:
## Summary

- **P0 routing robustness**: `_astar_route` returns `None` on failure; callers retry via `_route_perimeter` at 4 margins (16/32/64/128px); if all fail, edge is silently omitted rather than drawn through obstacles (fixes overlap bleed)
- **P1 IR types**: `LabelPlacement(box, reroute_required)` frozen dataclass replaces bare tuple return from `_best_label_pos`; geometry IR types (`Point`, `Port`, `PortAllocation`, `GroupLayout`, `RoutedEdge`, `LayoutResult`, `ValidationResult`) added to `_geometry.py`
- **P2 port allocation & predicates**: `allocate_face_ports` replaces ad-hoc offset arithmetic; `_fan_offset` clamped to `[0, node_w]`; `node_rect(n)` accessor uses `_node_render_w/h` instead of fixed `NODE_W`; back-edge and reverse-edge predicates use center-based geometry
- **P2 cycle-breaking**: `_break_cycles` replaced with iterative DFS (avoids Python recursion limit; greedy Eades FAS was prototyped but caused `statediagram-complex` regression — wrong edge reversed, 4 ranks vs 6)
- **P0 gallery validation**: `validate(src)` stub wired into `compare_gallery.py`; `_build_gallery` returns `(path, has_failures)`; `main()` exits 1 on invalid/error status; gallery moved `scripts/ → tools/`
- **Spec/plan**: `renderer-hardening-2026-07` spec status → Shipped, all ACs checked; plan status → Done

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_routing_astar.py` — 23 tests: A* None return, perimeter retry, route_edges edge-omit, port allocation, node_rect, iterative DFS invariants
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_compare_gallery.py` — 3 tests: `_build_gallery` has_failures, `main()` SystemExit(1)

author: justinpeterman-droid
body:
## Summary

Two related refinements to the report-writing flow, from officer feedback.

### 1 — Auto-add checklist confirmation lines to the narrative

Officers no longer type routine follow-through into their notes. Confirming an item on the checklist adds a plain sentence to the **first-person report** and **supervisor summary**:

| Checklist answer | Sentence added |
|---|---|
| Medical → **Seen by Infirmary staff** | "The inmate was seen by medical staff (refer to the Infirmary Report)." |
| Medical → **Refused** | "The inmate refused medical attention and the Refuse box was checked (refer to the Infirmary Report)." |
| Medical → **Sent by ambulance** | "The inmate was transported by ambulance to an outside facility for medical treatment (refer to the Infirmary Report)." |
| Photo/video obtained → **Yes** | "Photographs were taken." |
| Drug test → **Conducted** | "A drug test was conducted on the inmate." |
| Drug test → **Refused** | "The inmate refused a drug test and the Refuse box was checked." |
| Witness statements → **Yes** | "Witness statements were collected." |

New checklist-level `universal_auto_content` block, resolved by the existing deterministic path (no LLM, no raw notes). A line fires only when its condition is met; **N/A / No produce nothing**, and a line whose slot doesn't exist for a category never fires.

### 2 — Smarter Missing-Information step

Three fixes from direct feedback ("charges still asked," "medical won't clear / can't continue without Unknown," "a blank shouldn't stop generation"):

- **Charges dropped from Missing Information** — they're picked from the disciplinary handbook and confirmed in the charges panel, so re-asking was redundant (`validate.COLLECTED_ELSEWHERE`).
- **Medical disposition pre-selects a sensible, changeable default** — "Seen by Infirmary staff" for medical-involving incidents (fight, staff assault, forced cell move, PREA), "N/A - no injuries reported" otherwise. Drug test keeps its N/A default. Defaults ride on the gap and stay fully editable.
- **A blank never blocks generation** — Continue is always enabled; whatever's left open is flagged on the report as `[TO BE SUPPLEMENTED]` instead of trapping the officer behind the Unknown button. The progress line is informational only.

## Verification (deterministic, in-sandbox)

- `find_gaps`: universal lines fire on confirm / stay absent on N/A·No; charges never emitted as a gap; medical/drug defaults applied per category.
- Playwright against stubbed classify/extract/generate: charges absent from Missing Info, medical pre-selected "Seen by Infirmary staff", Continue enabled with fields left blank, changing medical registers, generation runs with blanks carrying medical + drug + charges through; zero JS console errors.

### Notes
- The medical narrative line uses "The inmate" rather than a specific name, to stay correct for multi-inmate incidents and never emit a `[NEEDED: …]` placeholder. Say the word if you'd rather it name the inmate.
- Narrative reads best on a live GCP-credentialed run; the deterministic insertion/gap logic is verified here.

author: mraszyk
body:
When a canister is deleted, its per-use-case consumption is added both to the `consumed_cycles_by_deleted_canisters` scalar and to the `consumed_cycles_by_use_case` map. `SubnetMetrics::consumed_cycles_total()` summed both, double counting the cycles consumed by deleted canisters.

Fix `consumed_cycles_total()` to skip the canister-level use cases (which only ever enter the map via deleted canisters and are already covered by the deleted canisters scalar), summing only the subnet-level use cases (SchnorrOutcalls, VetKd, DroppedMessages) that are not covered by any scalar.

Since this changes the certified state, the legacy behavior is preserved in `consumed_cycles_total_v27()`, which the canonical state consumer keeps using for all certification versions up to and including V27. A future certification version can switch the consumer over to the fixed `consumed_cycles_total()`.

author: quietcode-org
body:
### Description

Follow-up to #28490.

The `linux_native_test` environment uses `build_src_filter` to add the Marlin unit-test source files to the native test build.

Marlin sets:

```ini
src_dir = Marlin
```

Therefore this filter:

```ini
+<test>
```

refers to `Marlin/test`, which does not exist.

The project-level `test/` directory remains PlatformIO's test harness and contains the unit-test runner and configuration files. The C++ unit-test sources are stored separately in `Marlin/tests/`.

This PR changes only the source filter:

```diff
- build_src_filter = ${env:linux_native.build_src_filter} +<test>
+ build_src_filter = ${env:linux_native.build_src_filter} +<tests>
```

### Requirements

No printer hardware or board-specific environment is required.

The existing native unit-test command is sufficient:

```sh
make unit-test-all-local
```

### Benefits

The final CI run for #28490, with `+<test>`, completed successfully while executing zero registered Marlin test cases for all three configurations:

```text
marlin_default:             0 test cases, 0 succeeded
marlin_extruders_1_runout:  0 test cases, 0 succeeded
marlin_extruders_3_runout:  0 test cases, 0 succeeded
```

Each run reported `Collected 1 tests`, then skipped the test entry and finished with `0 test cases: 0 succeeded`.

With this one-line source-filter correction, the existing suites execute their registered Marlin tests:

```text
marlin_default:             145 test cases, 145 succeeded
marlin_extruders_1_runout:  146 test cases, 146 succeeded
marlin_extruders_3_runout:  146 test cases, 146 succeeded
```

### Configurations

Tested with the existing unit-test configurations:

- `test/001-default.ini`
- `test/002-extruders_1_runout.ini`
- `test/003-extruders_3_runout.ini`

### Scope

- One changed line
- One changed file: `ini/native.ini`
- No production firmware code changes
- No test-content changes

### Related Issues

- Follow-up to #28490

body:
## Summary

Pins the artifact and release GitHub Actions in `.github/workflows/release.yml` to immutable commit SHAs for supply-chain safety. Tag refs (`@v7`, `@v8`, `@v3`) are mutable and can be repointed by an upstream maintainer or attacker; pinning to a full commit SHA guarantees the exact reviewed code runs on every workflow invocation. Each SHA is annotated with a trailing version comment so Dependabot can continue to propose updates.

## Changes

| Action | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `actions/upload-artifact` | `@v7` | `@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1` |
| `actions/download-artifact` | `@v8` | `@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1` |
| `softprops/action-gh-release` | `@v3` | `@3d0d9888cb7fd7b750713d6e236d1fcb99157228 # v3.0.2` |

All three commit SHAs were verified to exist and correspond to the noted release tags (upload-artifact v7.0.1, download-artifact v8.0.1, action-gh-release v3.0.2).

No other actions were touched — `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-go`, and `actions/setup-node` are left exactly as they were.

author: mithun-svasamm
body:
Second remediation pass from the 2026-07-20 SEO audit. Stacked on #87 (Phase 1) — merge #87 first.

## Phase 4 — technical hygiene (nginx.conf, verified in a live nginx container)
- **Trailing-slash 301**: extensionless non-slash paths (`/in/locations` → `/in/locations/`) now canonicalise, so both URL forms stop returning 200 and splitting crawl budget. Files/assets (sitemap, robots, llms) are untouched.
- **Legacy `/in/solutions-*`**: real **one-hop** 301 → `/in/solutions/{clinics,hospitals}/`, replacing the meta-refresh+noindex stubs that robots.txt (contradictorily) Disallowed. Dropped the Disallow, removed the Astro redirect stubs, pointed the footer at the canonical pages.
- **Content-Security-Policy** header (enumerates gtag/GA/Plausible/admin-API origins; `'unsafe-inline'` until nonces) + `server_tokens off`.
- **Homepage `SoftwareApplication`** JSON-LD (mirrors `/pricing`, no fabricated rating).
- **Demo video** `preload` metadata→none. (The audit's "autoplay hero video" was wrong — it's a click-to-open modal that never loaded on homepage render.)

Redirect behaviour was tested in a real `nginx:alpine` container, not just `nginx -t`:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `/in/locations` | 301 → `/in/locations/` |
| `/in/locations/` | 200 (no loop) |
| `/in/solutions-clinics` | 301 → `/in/solutions/clinics/` (one hop) |
| `/sitemap-index.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt` | 200 (not redirected) |

## Phase 3 — content depth
- **All 8 specialty pages** expanded from ~380–500w to ~600–800w with genuinely specialty-specific workflow/compliance detail (dental lab-tracking, dermatology cosmetic/retail, diagnostics sample-lifecycle, IVF cycle/couple, multispecialty referrals, nursing-home IPD billing, polyclinic per-doctor settlement, small-hospital TPA/casualty).
- **Every addition was reviewed for accuracy.** I softened claims that reached past Lucoze's confirmed modules (IVF embryology, small-hospital TPA claim-lifecycle) and **restored two original team FAQs I'd initially over-edited** (diagnostics zone-routes + NABL bundle — those are the team's own consistent claims, not mine to rewrite).
- **6 thinnest location pages** deepened append-only (extended `localContext` + a point + a FAQ each) with safe local context. West Bengal (home wedge) made strongest.

## Blog — mostly already fine (audit over-flagged)
Disclaimers already present on the DPDP/GST posts; the billing posts cite-by-reference to the fully-sourced GST pillar. Per-post H2 question-form rewrite **deferred** — low value, high churn across 16 posts. Happy to do it as a fast follow if you want it.

## Verified
build 71pp · jest 90/90 · prettier · `nginx -t` + live-container redirect/header tests · mobile (360px) render check on the most-changed specialty page (no overflow).

⚠️ **CSP note for the manual pass:** GA/Plausible only load on prod (empty on UAT), so those CSP origins can only be verified live — after the prod deploy, check the browser console shows no beacon/form request blocked by CSP.

author: g761007
body:
Last piece before v0.8.0. **776 lines → 399**, restructured to answer *how do I
use this* before *how does this work*.

## What changed structurally

The old README opened with a pain/answer table, prerequisites, and a
concept-first tour. The new one is:

1. **What it is** — two sentences.
2. **Install** — one block.
3. **60-second start** — shortest path ending in a skill that works.
4. **"I want to…"** — the heart of the document. One runnable recipe each:
   recommend skills for a project · not reinstall what you have globally · see
   what you actually have · install globally · turn a skill off · update global
   skills · switch your whole setup · use a machine-local skill.
5. **Command reference** — one line each.
6. **`skillfile.yml` reference** — moved down.
7. **How it works** — moved to the end.

Concepts (the four-layer paths, adapters, cache immutability) appear only where
a task forces them.

## Every snippet was run before it was written

That rule paid for itself immediately. The most obvious first command anyone
would try —

```bash
skillpod add anthropics/skills --skill pdf
```

— did not work. Those skills live under `skills/`, and the manifest writer
discarded that. It is fixed in #17, merged before this PR, rather than writing
the README around a bug or shipping a first-run instruction that fails.

Verified end-to-end for this rewrite: `init`, `add` (project and `-g`),
`add --list`, `install`, `status`, `list`, `doctor`, `global list`,
`global link`, `global unlink`, `global update --dry-run`, `profile create`,
`profile save`, `switch --scope global --dry-run`, `--version`.

## Content the rewrite forced

- **Every `skillfile.lock` mention is gone** except the roadmap line noting its
  retirement. The old "Lockfile integrity" section became "what gets recorded",
  which says plainly that install records describe *your machine* and do not
  constrain a teammate's.
- **The positioning is stated up front**: a project recommends, you decide.
- **New material** for `prefer_global`, `global update`, the `status`
  dashboard, and the `LAYER` column.
- **Two surprises are now documented** rather than left to be discovered:
  `add -g` deliberately does *not* fan out, and a personal skill outranks a
  project one in Claude Code — with the docs link, because it is the reverse of
  the usual convention.
- **Roadmap corrected** — it previously listed 0.7.0 and 0.8.0 as things they
  are not.

`skillpod init` now mentions `prefer_global` in its commented `install:` block.

## Verification

```
513 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed
ruff check src tests   clean
mypy src/skillpod      clean (strict)
```

author: studio-18
body:
## Summary

Makes logging a result **from a league** open the exact same experience as the global **Log a Score** flow, and tightens the Log a Score set rows for mobile. Two related changes to score entry:

### 1. Log a Score — mobile set rows (`Scoreboard.tsx`)
Restructured each set into a **two-line stacked layout**: a header (SET label + winner trophy) then two side-by-side cells, each with an avatar and a −/+ stepper. This keeps score entry from overflowing on narrow screens. Layout/CSS only — no changes to scoring math, validation, winner calc, or the submitted payload.

### 2. League score entry now mirrors Log a Score
Previously the league page's **Add Score** opened a bespoke drawer (opponent-based: `GET /leagues/:id/result-opponents` → `POST /leagues/:id/results`), which looked and behaved differently from the polished `/log-result` flow.

Now both the league page's **Add Score** and the dashboard's **Log a Score** navigate to the shared **`/log-result`** page with the league preselected:
- `LogResultPage` reads nav-state (`{ matchType: "league", leagueId }`) to open straight into **League mode** with the league chosen.
- The bespoke Add-Score drawer in `LeagueDetailPage` is **retired** — its state, handlers, JSX, and `.league-score-*` CSS removed.
- This realigns league scoring with the **fixture-based** model (`POST /leagues/:id/matches/:fixtureId/result`) that `/log-result` already uses.
- Body-scroll-lock + overscroll containment are kept for the remaining Need-a-Match drawer.

## Behavioral note
League scoring now requires a **scheduled fixture** to exist for the user — you pick a fixture (`/leagues/:id/fixtures?mine=true`) rather than an arbitrary opponent. If the fixture dropdown is empty on Add Score, that league has no fixtures wired for the current user. `createLeagueResult` / `getLeagueResultOpponents` remain exported in `api/leagues.ts` but are now unused.

## Testing
- `npm run build` — green.

author: darksession
body:
## What

The `id64 → PG name` decoder only ever produced the **procedural** sector name, so any system physically inside a hand-authored (HA) nebula/cluster sector — Pleiades, Coalsack, NGC/IC/M/Col, etc. — was named wrongly in the app.

An HA overlay sector changes **both** the sector name *and* the letter/N1 suffix (only the final N2 index is shared), so it can't be a prefix swap. Concretely:

| | |
|---|---|
| in-game / EDDN | `Pleiades Sector HR-W d1-79` |
| id64 | `2724879894859` |
| old app output | `Synuefai XU-M d8-79` ← wrong |

## How

- **`PGHASectors.ts`** (new): the canonical EDTS `ha_regions` as light-year spheres (sorted smallest-radius-first for ED's overlap priority, with a `needsPermit` flag; 458 regions). `regionForCoords(x,y,z)` does first-match sphere containment against galaxy coordinates.
- **`PGSystem.ts`**: `fromSystemAddress` / `fromModSystemAddress` now accept optional galaxy coords; when a system falls in an HA region, `applyHASectorName` overrides the sector name **and** recomputes the letter/N1 suffix relative to the HA region origin (the exact inverse of the existing, tested `absoluteBoxel`). Mass code and N2 are origin-independent and stay as decoded. Adds `isHASector` / `needsPermit` fields.
- **`home.component.ts`**: `getPGName(id64, coords)` threads through `data.system.coords` and renders HA names verbatim (title-casing would mangle `NGC`/`IC`/`Col`, and in-game spellings like the lower-case `Blue planetary Sector` must be preserved).

Attribution: the `ha_regions` data is ported from the canonical EDTS source, https://bitbucket.org/Esvandiary/edts/.

## Testing

- `PGHASectors.spec.ts` (new): 5 real `(id64, coords, name)` triples pulled from Spansh across mass codes b/c/d/e all reproduce their exact in-game names; membership, priority ordering, permit flag, procedural fallback, and the mod-address path are covered.
- Existing `pgnames.spec.ts`: 26/26, unchanged.
- `ng build` (strict template/type check): clean.

## Known limitation

`NGC 2392 Sector` (Eskimo Nebula) is the one HA region with no origin in `PGRegion`, so its systems fall through to the procedural name (no corruption — same as the pre-existing baseline). Adding it needs an origin sourced/verified the same way `PGRegion`'s others were; worth an in-game check of what ED actually calls those systems first.

author: abrichr
body:
Rebases the paper disclosures onto the corrected, independently judged lending evidence from #219. The paper keeps the target-state product architecture intact while making the scientific scope and release boundary exact.

## What changed

- Preserves the corrected MockLoan three-arm result: screen-only `24/36`, single-surface `3/36`, complete-read-path `0/36`; complete verification detects `18/36` wrong actions and over-halts `3/36`.
- Describes the write, system-under-test readback, and benchmark judge as operationally separate paths: HTTP write, REST verification, and direct read-only SQLite ground truth with independent classifier code. It no longer falsely says verifier and judge share no state; both necessarily inspect the same persisted system of record, and neither provides specification independence.
- Reframes deterministic fault repetitions as a scripted coverage matrix. Repeated outcomes were invariant within each released arm-scenario cell, but they are not independent samples from a production population and do not support inferential confidence intervals.
- States that the computer-use-agent comparison measures only the exact baseline configuration; it does not predict what additional scaffolding would cost or recover.
- Preserves the closed-world disclosure: the complete-read-path zero covers the audited database surfaces, not undefined external side effects or an incomplete business specification.
- Clarifies EffectBench's current reference scope and labels the positioning table as design intent, not an empirical head-to-head.
- Aligns the paper with the open-core source boundary: each public constant binds to a permitted raw artifact or bounded aggregate, while grown corpora, tuned/deployment-derived data, raw private rows, and target recipes remain private.
- Corrects public-web availability: the public repository releases the bounded 29-application aggregate, not raw per-target rows or curated target recipes.
- Adds precise data/privacy and package-license language: no customer-derived hardening corpus is in this paper release; approved sanitized derivatives remain hash-bound and defense-in-depth; repository-only third-party reference environments remain outside the MIT wheel and sdist.
- Adds partial-oracle context from the software-testing literature and keeps both bibliography copies byte-identical.

## Verification

- `python paper/check_artifacts.py`
- `make -C paper` (full report and workshop PDF)
- `python scripts/validate_claims.py --check`
- committed verification-report regeneration produced no diff
- `python scripts/check_consistency.py`

No benchmark row, production provider, GUI/input, release, or deployment was executed by this PR.

author: siri-ray
body:
## Why

The 0.15.1 reliability review found that some runs recorded as execution failures were actually explicit user cancellations. When a user canceled an active Claude run, the CLI could flush a final assistant/result error while shutting down. That late frame raced the cancel route, latched a stream error, and let the close handler finish the run as failed before the existing cancel-aware classifier ran.

This caused a canceled run to be returned and telemetered as failed, could surface a false execution error in chat, and could make retry policy evaluate a run that the user had already stopped.

## What users will see

Canceling an active agent run now remains canceled even if the agent CLI emits a final error while reacting to SIGTERM. The run no longer surfaces a false execution error, retries because of the shutdown frame, or reports a `stream_error` failure classification.

## Surface area

- [ ] UI
- [ ] CLI / agent surface
- [ ] API / data contracts
- [ ] Design system / design tokens
- [ ] Extension points (`skills/`, `design-systems/`, `design-templates/`, `craft/`)
- [ ] Root dependencies
- [ ] Env vars
- [ ] i18n keys
- [x] Default behavior change
- [ ] None

## Screenshots

Not applicable — this is a daemon-only lifecycle fix with no UI surface change.

## Bug fix verification

- Red spec: `apps/daemon/tests/server-startup-smoke.test.ts` — `[P0] keeps a user-canceled Claude run canceled when a late error frame arrives`.
- Red on `main`: confirmed. The cancel API returned `status: failed` after the fake Claude process emitted canceled assistant/result error frames and exited with code 1.
- Green on this branch: confirmed. The cancel response and final run stay `canceled`; SSE contains no `error` event, no retry, exactly one terminal `end`, and no `stream_error` classification.
- The source change preserves non-cancel failure and retry paths; only events arriving after `cancelRequested` are treated as cancellation shutdown noise.

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon exec vitest run -c vitest.config.ts tests/server-startup-smoke.test.ts tests/claude-sidechain-assistant-error-false-failure.test.ts tests/chat-run-artifact-quiet-period.test.ts tests/runtimes/runs.test.ts` — 4 files, 83 tests passed.
- Full `tests/server-startup-smoke.test.ts` — 11 tests passed.
- `corepack pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon typecheck` — passed.
- `corepack pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon build` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `corepack pnpm guard` — blocked by the current-main repository baseline because `apps/telemetry-worker/package.json` is missing; the guard checks reported before that manifest load all passed.

author: greenheadhq
body:
## Summary

- 계획/PRD의 명시적 제외 범위와 가정을 존중하면서도 구체적 위험 완화 누락은 지적할 수 있도록 Arbiter 기준을 보강합니다.
- hook/test hard-fail 시 local diff 격리부터 merged PR 조회, 정상 재검증, 승인된 임시 bypass까지의 순서를 기존 decision-regression SSOT에 추가합니다.
- `for_plan`의 빈 diff 오판과 PR 코멘트 예시의 pinning-guard 충돌을 방지합니다.

Closes #794
Closes #796
Closes #1128
Closes #1145

## 기존 문제/배경

`run-da` 문서에는 서로 다른 네 가지 마찰이 남아 있었습니다.

1. Arbiter가 `Non-Goals`, `Assumptions`, `Out of Scope` 같은 의도적 결정을 누락 요구사항으로 오해할 수 있었습니다.
2. hook/test hard-fail 시 local diff 문제와 main에 이미 수정된 회귀를 구분하는 재사용 가능한 조회 절차가 없었습니다.
3. `for_plan` reviewer가 아직 구현되지 않은 계획을 현재 코드와 비교해, 빈 diff 자체를 기각 근거로 삼을 수 있었습니다.
4. PR 코멘트 예시의 상세 헤딩이 pinning-guard의 진행 카운터 패턴과 충돌했습니다.

이 문제들은 실제 결함보다 리뷰 형식과 실행 시점의 차이를 문제로 보고하게 만들거나, 문서 예시를 그대로 사용할 수 없게 했습니다.

## CIR (Change Intent Record)

- Issue #794: 명시적 제외 범위는 보호하되, 그 결정이 구체적인 새 위험을 만들면 `missing risk mitigation`으로만 escape hatch를 허용하도록 정리했습니다.
- Issue #796: 새 reference 파일을 추가하는 대신 이미 절차 SSOT 역할을 하는 `decision-regression-audit.md`를 확장했습니다. 중복 문서와 링크 분산을 피하기 위한 선택입니다.
- Issue #1128: Arbiter에만 있던 `for_plan` 해석 규칙을 reviewer 공통 프롬프트와 SKILL 핵심 invariant에도 반영해 최초 finding 생성 단계부터 빈 diff 오판을 차단했습니다.
- Issue #1145: pinning 정책을 완화하지 않고 문서 예시를 기존 요약 표의 `R1`/`R2` 표기와 통일했습니다.

Trade-off: 공통 프롬프트와 SKILL에 핵심 규칙이 한 번씩 재서술되지만, reviewer 프롬프트의 자기완결성과 preflight 가시성을 위해 의도적으로 허용했습니다. 상세 판정 기준의 정본은 기존 reference에 유지됩니다.

## ADR

| 대안 | 설명 | 장점 | 단점 | 결정 |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| 별도 main-regression reference 추가 | hook 회귀 조회 전용 문서를 새로 생성 | 주제별 탐색이 직접적 | decision-regression 절차와 중복, SSOT 분산 | 기각 |
| 기존 decision-regression SSOT 확장 | 시계열 게이트 인접에 main PR lookup 절차 추가 | 기존 소스 계층과 역할 분담 재사용, 링크 최소화 | 문서가 조금 길어짐 | 채택 |
| pinning-guard 패턴 완화 | 기존 상세 헤딩을 허용하도록 검사 변경 | 예시 수정 불필요 | 휘발성 진행 카운터 차단 의도를 약화 | 기각 |
| 예시를 `R1`/`R2`로 변경 | 요약 표와 상세 헤딩을 같은 축약 표기로 통일 | 정책 유지, 변경 최소 | 축약 표기 의미를 문맥에 의존 | 채택 |

## 구현 상세

| 파일 | 변경 | 내용 |
|------|------|------|
| `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/skills/run-da/SKILL.md` | 수정 | main 회귀 lookup lazy-load 항목과 `for_plan` 미구현 계획 invariant 추가 |
| `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/skills/run-da/references/arbiter-prompt.md` | 수정 | 명시적 scope-out/assumption 보호 및 risk mitigation escape hatch 추가 |
| `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/skills/run-da/references/decision-regression-audit.md` | 수정 | local-diff 격리, merged PR 검색, main 대조, 승인된 bypass 후 재검증 절차 추가 |
| `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/skills/run-da/references/da-domains.md` | 수정 | reviewer 공통 프롬프트에 `for_plan` 빈 diff 비기각 규칙 추가 |
| `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/skills/run-da/references/protocol.md` | 수정 | PR 코멘트 상세 헤딩을 `R1`/`R2`로 통일 |
| `scripts/ai/verify-ai-compat.sh` | 수정 | 허용 헤딩 존재와 차단 대상 헤딩 부재를 검증하는 회귀 계약 추가 |

### 핵심 규칙

```text
리뷰 모드가 for_plan이면 현재 코드에 변경이 없거나 git diff가 비어 있는 것은 finding의 기각 근거가 아니다.
```

```markdown
### R1
...
### R2
```

### 자동 검증

- deterministic pinning-guard fixtures: 통과
- run-da/analyzing-da-sessions 연동 테스트 45개: 통과
- skill consistency, stale identifier, noise 검사: 통과
- `verify-ai-compat`의 신규 run-da 계약 검사: 통과
- 전체 `verify-ai-compat` 실행은 저장소 밖 user-scope 설정의 기존 TOML 중복 키 때문에 최종 실패했으며, 이번 변경 영역 이전과 신규 계약 검사는 모두 통과했습니다.

## 참고 레퍼런스

- Issue #794 — Arbiter의 Non-Goals/Assumptions anti-bias 규칙
- Issue #796 — main 회귀 PR lookup 절차
- Issue #1128 — `for_plan` 빈 diff 오판
- Issue #1145 — PR 코멘트 예시와 pinning-guard 충돌

## Human Test Plan

### 정상 동작 검증

1. `arbiter-prompt.md`의 scope-out 보호 절을 읽고, Non-Goal 하나와 그 결정으로 생기는 구체적 위험 하나를 가정합니다.
   - 기대: 단순 미구현은 finding이 아니며, 근거가 있는 위험만 `missing risk mitigation`으로 표현됩니다.
   - 실패 시: 보호 절에 escape hatch의 메커니즘·근거·완화 누락 조건이 모두 있는지 확인합니다.

2. hook/test hard-fail 상황을 가정하고 `decision-regression-audit.md`의 절차를 따라갑니다.
   - 기대: local diff 격리, stable token 기반 merged PR 조회, main 포함 여부 대조, 정상 재검증 순서가 유지되고 `--no-verify`는 사용자 승인 뒤에만 등장합니다.
   - 실패 시: `SKILL.md` lazy-load 표가 같은 reference를 가리키는지 확인합니다.

3. 변경 전 코드가 그대로인 계획을 `for_plan` reviewer 프롬프트에 넣습니다.
   - 기대: reviewer는 빈 diff를 이유로 기각하지 않고, 기술적 메커니즘의 실재와 계획 실행 후 문제 도입 여부를 검토합니다.
   - 실패 시: `da-domains.md` 공통 프롬프트와 `SKILL.md` 핵심 invariant가 함께 포함되는지 확인합니다.

### pinning 회귀 검증

4. `protocol.md`의 PR 코멘트 예시를 일반 임시 파일에 복사해 pinning-guard 검사에 통과시키고, 차단 대상 상세 헤딩이 남아 있지 않은지 확인합니다.
   - 기대: `### R1`과 `### R2`는 허용되고 차단 대상 진행 카운터 헤딩은 검색되지 않습니다.
   - 실패 시: `scripts/ai/verify-ai-compat.sh`의 run-da PR comment contract 결과와 `pinning-patterns.sh`의 Pattern A를 비교합니다.

body:
## Summary

Low-risk cleanup pass covering dead code, safer admin destructive actions, and a real enrichment cache TTL.

### Dead code removed (each justified by a repo-wide grep)
- **`app/webhooks/models.py`** (`PaymentRecord`, `OrderRecord`, `CrossReferenceLog`) — deleted.
  - `grep -rn "PaymentRecord|OrderRecord|CrossReferenceLog" app/ tests/` matched only the file's own definitions.
  - The module is shadowed by the `app/webhooks/models/` **package** (package wins on import); all `webhooks.models.*` imports resolve to `webhooks.models.rich_notification`.
  - No webhooks migrations exist (`app/webhooks/migrations/` has only `__init__.py`), so nothing depended on these tables.
- **`app/webhooks/services/message_builder.py`** + **`tests/test_message_builder.py`** — deleted.
  - `grep -rn "message_builder|MessageBuilder" app/ tests/` showed the only importer was `tests/test_message_builder.py`. No `app/` code references it (superseded by the `RichNotification` / `notification_builder` path). The test file only tested `message_builder`, so it was removed too.

### Safer admin destructive actions (`app/core/admin.py`)
- Removed the custom one-click `delete_selected_companies` action, which bypassed Django's delete confirmation page. Django's built-in `delete_selected` (with its confirmation page) covers this.
- `purge_enrichment_data` now shows an **intermediate confirmation page** (`admin/core/company/purge_enrichment_confirmation.html`); the irreversible purge only runs after the confirmation form is submitted.

### Honor enrichment cache TTL
- `CACHE_DURATION_DAYS` was defined but unused, giving an indefinite cache. Both services now set `CACHE_DURATION_DAYS = 30` and treat enrichment older than that (via the existing `_blended_at` / `_enriched_at` timestamps) as stale so it gets refreshed.
- Added shared `core.utils.is_timestamp_fresh` (timezone-aware; missing/unparseable timestamp = stale) to avoid duplicating the check across `DomainEnrichmentService._has_enrichment` and `EmailEnrichmentService._is_fresh`.

## Test plan
- New `tests/test_enrichment_cache_ttl.py` proves stale (older than TTL) enrichment needs refresh while fresh does not, for both services and the shared helper.
- Updated `tests/core/tests_services.py` and `tests/core/tests_admin.py` for the new TTL and confirmation behavior; removed the obsolete custom-delete test.
- `uv run ruff check .` — passed
- `uv run ruff format --check .` — passed
- `uv run mypy app/` — Success, no issues in 115 source files
- `uv run pytest -q` — **1475 passed**, 20 subtests passed

author: an9xyz
body:
## Summary

The contributor avatar stack on the Changelog page fanned out on hover by animating `margin`, which changed the group's layout width and re-flowed/wrapped the parent flex row **under the cursor** — producing a hover flicker loop. With many contributors the fanned stack also overflowed past the card's rounded corner.

This PR reworks the interaction so it is flicker-free and overflow-safe, on both desktop and touch.

## Changes

- **No flicker**: fan the stack with `transform: translateX()` (per-avatar index) instead of `margin`, so hover never triggers layout reflow. Fanned step (20px) stays below the avatar width (24px), so avatars remain gapless and the cursor never falls into a gap.
- **No overflow**: the group reserves its *fanned* width up front (via a CSS var), so the fan fills that box exactly and the whole group wraps as one unit instead of spilling over the card.
- **Bounded for large lists**: show at most 10 avatars plus a `+N` overflow badge; the badge's `title` lists the remaining contributor names.
- **Mobile**: under `@media (hover: none)` the fan/lift/name-tooltip are disabled and the reserved width falls back to `auto`, so a sticky tap-triggered `:hover` can't shift avatars or cause horizontal overflow.

Scope is limited to `src/pages/Changelog/index.tsx`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `vitest run` — 49/49 tests pass
- [x] Verified in a real browser (Playwright) against the test backend:
  - [x] Desktop: hover fans avatars out with no flicker; rightmost avatar stops at the content edge (no overflow past the card)
  - [x] Desktop: no page horizontal scrollbar
  - [x] Mobile (390px, touch): contributor group stays within the viewport (no overflow)

## Notes

- A pre-existing, unrelated horizontal overflow on mobile comes from the platform filter `Tabs` (6 icon tabs on narrow screens), not from the contributor avatars. Left out of this PR — happy to address separately.
