author: kyle-sexton
body:
## Summary

Standing operator principle: what needs no reasoning gets a script. Every `/loop`
lane currently hand-assembles two pure-mechanics artifacts every session — the
MACHINE-BEHAVIOR telemetry block and the "maintain ONE telemetry comment, edit in
place" upsert. This PR extracts both into scripts the lane prompt references, so
the outputs are deterministic and testable and the lane prompt shrinks (context
minimalism — long prompts micromanage; Fable-class models need fewer steers).

Both scripts live under `plugins/claude-ops/skills/lanes/scripts/` and follow the
existing `lane-launcher.sh` conventions (jq CRLF wrapper for native-Windows jq,
the `--help` header as the full contract, explicit exit codes, per-field graceful
degradation for telemetry).

## Fix

**Part 1 — `machine-behavior.sh` (issue item 1).** Emits the MACHINE-BEHAVIOR
block as a verbatim-printable text block: gh identity (`gh api user`), clone path
+ worktree inventory (root, count, per-worktree branch, detached-HEAD flag, from
`git worktree list --porcelain`), and installed plugin versions.

- **Determinism contract:** the script emits ONLY mechanically unambiguous facts.
  It deliberately does **not** compute "deviations from standing rules" — the
  standing rules are prose the script cannot read, so a deviation is a model
  judgment made by reading these facts against those rules. Emitting a fabricated
  deviations verdict would put guessing inside the "deterministic" script; the
  block ends with a one-line pointer reminding the lane to make that assessment.
  For the same reason there is no heuristic "worktree pattern" field — the
  worktrees legitimately span different parents, so the raw path list *is* the
  pattern.
- **Installed, not repo-HEAD, versions.** The block describes the environment the
  lane is actually running in. Per the lanes skill's `context/refresh.md`, a
  running lane's installed plugin version can lag repo HEAD mid-session — the
  installed record (`installed_plugins.json`) is the honest number, the checkout
  is not. `--plugin <id>` (repeatable) scopes the block to the plugins a lane runs.

**Part 2 — `telemetry-upsert.sh` (issue item 2; interim home of the #502 contract).**
`--issue N --marker STR --body-file PATH` maintains exactly ONE marker-identified
comment on a tracking issue, editing it in place instead of posting a second.

- **Marker / detection convention (reusable across lanes and issues):** the script
  writes a machine-detectable sentinel as the comment's first line —
  `<!-- claude-ops:lane-telemetry marker=STR -->`. `STR` is constrained to
  `[A-Za-z0-9:._-]+` so it can never contain the `>` that would close the HTML
  comment early. The sentinel is invisible in the rendered issue and distinct per
  marker, so N lanes can each own one comment on the *same* issue without
  colliding.
- **Two-tier detection (mirrors the issue spec):** (1) primary — the newest comment
  carrying the exact sentinel; (2) fallback — on first migration off a
  hand-authored comment, the most recent comment **by the authenticated user**
  carrying the raw marker text (PATCHing it adopts it, so the next cycle takes the
  primary path). The comment list is fetched with `gh api --paginate` and slurped;
  without pagination an existing comment on page 2 of a busy tracking issue is
  invisible and the script would POST a duplicate — the exact bug it exists to
  prevent. REST numeric comment ids are used for the `PATCH` (the GraphQL
  `gh issue view --json comments` node ids the read-side uses are not accepted by
  the REST `issues/comments/{id}` endpoint).

**Part 3 — wire `re-anchor:script-the-deterministic-work` into the prompt-authoring
ritual (issue item 3): DEFERRED — blocked on #480.** The issue scopes this to
"#480's future skill." #480 (a loop-prompt-authoring skill) does **not** exist yet
as an implemented skill — it is an open, unimplemented issue — so there is no
ritual to hook into, and building #480's skill is out of scope for this PR. A repo
grep for an existing prompt-versioning ritual/checklist (`prompt-version`,
`prompt-authoring`, `script-the-deterministic`) found only the `re-anchor` skill
itself and the existing `#480` *prompt-storage* forward-dependency note in the
lanes SKILL.md / `context/config.md` — which is about storage, not the authoring
ritual, so wiring the re-anchor step there would be a stretch. Per the task's
stated scope boundary, no new ritual/checklist file is invented; Part 3 lands when
#480 does.

## Verification

Tests follow this repo's convention (a sibling `.test.sh` per script, PATH-stubbed
external commands + JSON fixtures, hermetic — no network/real CLI), discovered by
`scripts/run-plugin-tests.sh` (`plugins/**/*.test.sh`).

```
$ bash plugins/claude-ops/skills/lanes/scripts/machine-behavior.test.sh
machine-behavior.test: PASS — 22 cases

$ bash plugins/claude-ops/skills/lanes/scripts/telemetry-upsert.test.sh
telemetry-upsert.test: PASS — 21 cases

$ bash plugins/claude-ops/skills/lanes/scripts/lane-launcher.test.sh   # regression, unbroken
lane-launcher.test: PASS — 88 cases
```

`machine-behavior.test.sh` covers: gh identity rendering + degradation to
`unavailable` when gh is missing/unauthenticated; worktree count, per-worktree
branch, detached-HEAD flag, and clone-path from the common git dir; installed
plugin versions filtered by `--plugin`, with the scope-divergent marker when a
name has >1 installed version; missing/malformed `installed_plugins.json`
degradation; a `--plugin` naming no installed plugin reported (not silently empty);
argument/repo exit codes.

`telemetry-upsert.test.sh` covers: create when no match (POST); update-in-place on
the sentinel (PATCH to that id); fallback adoption of the user's raw-marker comment;
fallback refusing another user's marker comment (creates instead); **pagination —
a sentinel comment on a second page is found (no duplicate POST)**; marker
`>`-injection rejection; non-numeric issue + missing body-file rejection; `--dry-run`
performs no write; `-` reads the body from stdin.

Repo quality gates run locally (all clean):

```
shellcheck -x --rcfile .shellcheckrc  <all four scripts>   → clean (0 findings)
shfmt -d  <all four scripts>                                → clean (no diff)
scripts/check-changelog-parity.sh --check-bump origin/main → PASS
scripts/validate-plugins.sh                                → PASS
scripts/check-orphaned-fixtures.sh                         → PASS
scripts/check-changed-skills.sh origin/main                → PASS (7 trigger phrases preserved; 3 script tests pass)
markdownlint-cli2 CHANGELOG.md SKILL.md                    → 0 errors
```

Closes #538

## Related

- **#538** — the umbrella this PR closes (script the deterministic lane mechanics).
- **#502** — the telemetry contract whose "one comment, edit in place, never
  double-post" rule `telemetry-upsert.sh` is the interim scripted home of.
- **#480** — loop-prompt-authoring skill; **Part 3 is blocked on this landing
  first** (see the Fix section). Also the forward owner of durable prompt storage
  referenced by the lanes skill today.
- **#496** — context economy / restart discipline; scripting these mechanics
  shrinks the per-cycle lane prompt.
- **#477–#479** — absorption umbrellas; these extractions are the script-shaped
  subset of that work.

author: kagura-agent
body:
## Summary

The in-sandbox guard for `openclaw channels add/remove` printed a generic hint with literal `<sandbox>` and `<channel>` placeholders. Users and CI automation could not determine the correct host-side command from these generic tokens.

## Changes

- Render the validated sandbox name through the existing `_nemoclaw_policy_denial_hint_label()` helper.
- Render only the supported `add` or `remove` operation; other values become `<operation>`.
- Render only built-in channel names (`discord`, `slack`, `teams`, `telegram`, `wechat`, or `whatsapp`); missing or hostile values become `<channel>`.
- Add valid add/remove coverage plus quote, newline, and command-separator cases proving attacker-controlled text never reaches the copyable host command.
### Before
```
Error: 'openclaw channels add' cannot modify channels inside the sandbox.
Changes inside the sandbox do not persist across rebuilds.

To add or remove messaging channels, exit the sandbox and run:
  nemoclaw <sandbox> channels add <channel>
  nemoclaw <sandbox> channels remove <channel>

These stage the change and rebuild the sandbox to apply it.
WhatsApp pairs entirely inside the sandbox; complete pairing via:
  openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp
WeChat captures its token via a host-side QR during the host-side
'channels add wechat' flow — no in-sandbox login step.
```

### After
```
Error: 'openclaw channels add' cannot modify channels inside the sandbox.
Changes inside the sandbox do not persist across rebuilds.
Run 'nemoclaw my-assistant channels add telegram' on the host.
```

- Vitest project membership is exact

- `npm run check:diff` passed

Traces whether a Karate 2 scenario emitted `SCENARIO_ENTER`. Scenarios that return before entering are not finished or retried.

# Motivation

With `abortSuiteOnFailure` enabled, `ScenarioRuntime.call()` can return before the scenario starts. The retry advice previously attempted to finish a test that did not exist.

Fixes the repo-fixable causes behind the failing `test`-branch CI jobs, diagnosed per failing job group.

## Workflow config (caused 4 red jobs by itself)
`.github/workflows/main.yaml` lists 14 suites in the matrix but only had `include` (path/timeout) entries for 10. **`benchmark`, `pipeline_3.0_v1`, `pipeline_designer`, `pipeline_create`** had empty `matrix.path`/`matrix.timeout`, so those jobs ran bare `python -m pytest` over the whole tree with an invalid `timeout-minutes` template — and never ran their intended suites. Added the 4 missing entries.

## SDK fix
- `aixplain/v2/model.py`: serialize the `functions` search filter as plain strings. Backend now rejects the old `[{"id": ...}]` shape with `400: each value in functions must be a string` (the Inspector search path already sends strings).

## Test fixes
- Slack action code renamed upstream (Composio): `SLACK_SENDS_A_MESSAGE_TO_A_SLACK_CHANNEL` → `SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE` across v1 agent, team_agent, and v2 test files. The stale name silently produced empty action scopes.
- `test_rlm.py::test_create_rlm_missing_orchestrator`: pass `mode="recursive"` — auto mode falls back to worker-only parallel/rag and never raises.
- `test_snake_case_e2e.py::test_execution_params`: accept any `APIError`; backend now returns a generic message for token-limit failures.
- `run_connect_model_test.py`: unique script-tool names + `try/finally` delete, so a mid-test failure can't poison later runs with `Name already exists` (current cause of 2 red tests — the orphaned "My Test Tool" connection on the CI account still needs a one-time manual delete).

## Verified
- `pytest tests/unit`: 1388 passed, 4 skipped
- `pytest --collect-only`: 1808 tests, 0 errors
- Matrix validated: every suite has an include entry

Remaining red tests are backend/platform issues (metrics 500s, API-key quota, Tavily 404, web-search asset, utility-model runtime, Vectara creds, AIR filtered search, dead public MCP host) — not fixable in this repo.

author: jgarcialr
body:
Supersedes #3126 — re-sent with a bnd version bump so the corrected build can be published as a new artifact.

Adds a JDK 17 build guard to the two Apache CXF patcher modules (`org-apache-cxf-core-3.6.11` and `org-apache-cxf-rt-rs-security-oauth2-3.6.11`), matching the precedent on `org-primefaces` and `jakarta-faces` (LPD-86469), and bumps their bnd version from `3.6.11.LIFERAY-PATCHED-1` to `3.6.11.LIFERAY-PATCHED-2`.

JDK 21's `javac` ([JDK-8292275](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8292275)) emits a `MethodParameters` attribute with empty parameter names for the synthetic and mandated constructor parameters of anonymous inner classes (for example `OAuthRequestFilter$1` and `W3CMultiSchemaFactory$RecursiveAllowedXMLSchemaReader$1$1`). The Jakarta transformer (bnd 6.4.0) throws an NPE writing that nameless attribute, so those classes fail to transform and are copied through still referencing `javax.*`. JDK 17's `javac` does not emit it.

The guard fails the build up front on any non-JDK-17 JVM, and the version bump lets the corrected JDK 17 build publish as `LIFERAY-PATCHED-2` rather than overwriting the existing artifacts.

author: gtauzin
body:
## Template update: v0.27.3 → v0.28.1

Updates this project from python-package-copier **v0.28.0 → v0.28.1**, folded into
the existing v0.28.0 update on this branch. Two commits, one per release.

**v0.28.0** gave docstring sections real headings via mkdocstrings template
overrides. The fan-out across the fleet found five defects in it; **v0.28.1** fixes
all five, and this PR now carries the corrected result.

### What changed in this commit

| # | Fix | Effect here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rendered overrides no longer end in a blank line | `end-of-file-fixer` stops rewriting them on every commit |
| 2 | `exclude_docs` gains `*.jinja` and `material/overrides/*.html` | 4 `.jinja` + 3 override HTML files no longer published |
| 3 | `Methods` heading gated on rendered methods, not `obj.members` | `Sampler` and `Storage` lose an empty heading + dead ToC entry |
| 4 | `_dedupe_heading_ids` added; section-title strip ungated | inert here (no multi-object page) |
| 5 | `theme.css` uses a descendant selector | the class sits in an inner span, so the old selector matched nothing |

### Verification

Files touched by the update: **5** (`.copier-answers.yml`, `docs/hooks.py`,
`class.html.jinja`, `theme.css`, `mkdocs.yml`). **Zero `.rej` files.**

- **Nav intact.** `mkdocs.yml` is not copier-protected and this release edits it, so
  the nav was checked leaf-by-leaf from parsed YAML: **17 leaves before → 17 after**,
  per-section counts identical (Tutorials 2, How-to 8, Examples 1, Explanation 2,
  Reference 3, root 1), order unchanged, `Reference` last. `exclude_docs` correctly
  went 4 → 6 patterns. No clobber.
- **`docs/assets` untouched** — empty diff, all 7 file hashes identical.
- **`.claude/skills/` intact** — 36 files across 15 skills, none modified.
- Tracked-file inventory identical at 119 files; nothing added or deleted.
- All six template-owned files are **byte-identical to a pristine `copier copy` at
  v0.28.1**, including `docs/hooks.py` (Tier 1, no fork).
- `nox -s check_docs` — passes, **0 warnings**.
- All 14 prek hooks pass, including `fix end of files`.

### Measured effect on the built docs

Anchor parity over `(page, id, level, order)` across a real build: 26 pages before
and after, **210 → 208 anchors**, and exactly two deltas — both intended:

```
pages/api/generated/…optuna.Sampler/  - REMOVED  h3 #methods
pages/api/generated/…optuna.Storage/  - REMOVED  h3 #methods
```

Fix 3 in both directions — `Sampler` and `Storage` had `#methods` headings with no
method under them (their only member is `__init__`, which mkdocstrings filters out);
both are now gone. `Callback` (whose `__call__` survives filtering) and
`OptunaSearchCV` (`fit`, `__sklearn_tags__`) **keep** theirs. The guard does not
over-fire: 4 pages with `#methods` → 2, and the 2 that remain are the 2 that should.

Fix 5, measured in the built HTML: elements carrying `doc-section-heading` **on** an
`h5` = **0**; carrying it in a span **under** an `h5` = **8`**. The old
`h5.doc-section-heading` selector matched nothing; the shipped rule now matches both
forms, so the 8 real headings are styled.

Fix 2, measured in `site/`: `.jinja` files **4 → 0**, files under `site/material/`
**7 → 0**. The leak was live — `…/material/templates/python/material/class.html.jinja`
served **200** from this PR's docs preview before this commit.

Fix 4 is present and unit-tested correct but **inert in this repo**: every page here
has exactly one `:::` directive, so no duplicate ids arise. 0 duplicate heading ids
and 0 leftover `doc-section-title` spans, before and after.

body:
## What?
Backport of the #1863 container-build gate wiring to `release/1.4.0`, both files identical to `main`:

리드 스코어링 검토에서 확정한 2건입니다.

## 1. hot 경계 60 → 65
참석 25 + 시청 만점 35 = **정확히 60 = 기존 hot 경계**. 창만 끝까지 띄워두고 아무 행동도 안 한 시청자가 영업 콜 우선순위(hot)에 들어갔습니다. 65로 올리면 풀시청이어도 **최소 행동 하나(투표 4·질문 6…) 또는 마케팅 동의(10)** 가 있어야 hot이 됩니다 — "접속 ≠ 관여" 원칙과 일치. 임계값만 변경이라 데이터 재계산이 필요 없습니다.

## 2. CTA 클릭 점수 dedupe

author: maores
body:
## What

Messages sent within 2 seconds of each other now buffer per chat and run as a single Claude turn with one combined reply. A lone message behaves exactly as before, just 2s later. `DEBOUNCE_MS` env overrides the window; `POLL_SERIAL=1` rollback mode bypasses the whole thing.

## Origin

Designed and approved in Telegram chat on 2026-07-20 (Maor picked the 2s window), then implemented by the agent on the droplet itself as `4e881bc`. The droplet cannot push, so this branch is the rescue: the agent's commit is preserved as-is, my review fixes sit on top (same flow as PRs #40/#42).

## Review findings fixed in the second commit

1. **Shutdown drain missed the buffer.** The offset is saved at fetch time, so a deploy restart landing inside a 2s window silently lost the buffered messages, the exact bug class the graceful drain exists to prevent. `flushAll()` now runs before the drain awaits the queues.
2. **/stop could not see the buffer.** A message still in its window resurrected as a fresh turn seconds after the stop. The stop path now clears the chat's buffer and counts it in the "cancelled" reply.
3. **Quiz commands leaked to Claude in batches.** `/hint` sent within 2s of another message would have ridden the combined prompt past the poller's code handler. Quiz commands now bypass the debounce (flushing the buffer first so order holds).
4. **Allowlist was first-sender-only.** In a group chat a mixed burst either smuggled a stranger's text in or dropped an authorized user's. Now filtered per message.
5. **Voice echo parity.** Low-confidence transcripts keep their mic echo in batch turns.

Also extracted the timer bookkeeping into a `Debouncer` class in dispatch.ts (where ChatQueues/SerialChain live) so it's unit-testable.

## Verification

- Suite: 575 -> 583, all green (8 new Debouncer tests: burst batching, window restart, per-chat isolation, clear-on-stop, flush-on-shutdown, throw safety).
- Verified against the live paths: usage logging and the review loop are inherited via `streamClaude`; serial rollback mode still routes straight to `handleMessage`.

Not deployed yet; the droplet still runs main.

author: rtimesc
body:
## Summary

- Reorganize the previously flat navigation scripts into explicit `data`, `training`, `evaluation`, `pipelines`, `policies`, and `legacy` packages.
- Keep `habitat_vln/habitat_vln_nav.py` as the primary runtime entrypoint while updating internal imports and documented CLI commands to the new module paths.
- Encode generated MP4 artifacts as browser/VS Code-compatible H.264 when FFmpeg is available, with the existing `mp4v` output retained as a safe fallback.
- Update architecture documentation and interface tests so the new boundaries and supported entrypoints are directly inspectable.

## Why

The navigation code had grown as a collection of top-level Python files. That made it difficult to tell which modules prepare data, train a model, evaluate results, orchestrate a workflow, or run the online controller. This change gives each responsibility a stable package boundary before more navigation features are added.

The generated MP4 files also used the OpenCV `mp4v` codec. Those files could be valid but still fail to play in VS Code's embedded video viewer. The runtime now attempts an FFmpeg/libx264 transcode to H.264 (`yuv420p` plus `faststart`), which is much more broadly supported.

## Package layout

- `habitat_vln/data/`: VLN data checks, HM3D smoke generation, oracle collection, training-record schemas, coverage analysis, and NaVIDA dataset building.
- `habitat_vln/training/`: Qwen and NaVIDA QLoRA training entrypoints.
- `habitat_vln/evaluation/`: offline NaVIDA output scoring and PointNav policy comparison.
- `habitat_vln/pipelines/`: multi-stage HM3D/NaVIDA workflow orchestration.
- `habitat_vln/policies/`: policy interfaces and concrete VLM/NaVIDA policies.
- `habitat_vln/legacy/`: older direct Habitat-Sim and standalone PointNav examples kept out of the main workflow.
- `habitat_vln/runtime/`: runtime artifact production, including H.264 video conversion.

## Interface and behavior changes

- The main online entrypoint remains `python habitat_vln/habitat_vln_nav.py`.
- Moved workflow scripts are now run as modules, for example:
  - `python -m habitat_vln.data.check_vln_data`
  - `python -m habitat_vln.training.train_navida_qlora`
  - `python -m habitat_vln.evaluation.evaluate_pointnav_policies`
  - `python -m habitat_vln.pipelines.hm3d_navida_pipeline`
- Old top-level forwarding files are intentionally removed after interface and smoke validation, so new work has one canonical import/command path instead of maintaining two parallel layouts.
- Policy input/output and controller data flow are not intentionally changed by the package move.
- Video writing first creates a temporary OpenCV MP4, then attempts H.264 conversion. If FFmpeg or conversion fails, the original MP4 is preserved instead of losing the episode artifact.

## Validation

- `conda run -n habitat_vlm python -m unittest discover -v -s test -p 'test_habitat_vln_*.py'` — 16/16 tests passed.
- `conda run -n habitat_vlm python -m habitat_vln.training.train_qwen_qlora --self-test` — passed.
- `conda run -n habitat_vlm python -m habitat_vln.training.train_navida_qlora --self-test` — passed.
- All 11 reorganized module entrypoints accepted `--help`.
- Structured-package import checks passed.
- `conda run -n habitat_vlm python -m compileall -q ...` passed for the changed Python scope.
- `git diff --check` and the staged whitespace check passed.
- A 2-step, 64x64 Mock plumbing smoke run completed.
- A 20-step, 320x240 Mock PointNav smoke run completed with `Success=1.0`, `SPL≈0.99946`, and zero collisions.
- The generated 320x240 episode video was inspected with `ffprobe` and reported H.264 High profile, `yuv420p`, 4 seconds, and 165,465 bytes.
- Generated outputs remain ignored and are not included in this PR.

## Experiment boundary

The short closed-loop runs above validate package wiring, controller/runtime plumbing, and artifact generation. They use the Mock/privileged PointNav path and are not evidence of Qwen or NaVIDA model quality, nor a language-conditioned VLN benchmark result.

## Review notes

The most important review points are:

1. Whether the new package ownership matches the intended long-term framework.
2. Whether any external scripts still depend on the removed top-level module paths.
3. Whether the FFmpeg fallback behavior is appropriate for machines without `libx264`.

This PR is intentionally opened as a draft so the structure and public entrypoints can be reviewed before merging.

body:
## Related issues

- Related to code scanning alerts [#207](https://github.com/Automattic/studio/security/code-scanning/207) and [#208](https://github.com/Automattic/studio/security/code-scanning/208)

## How AI was used in this PR

Claude Code fetched both CodeQL alerts, traced the taint flow, proposed the "confine to a safe root" mitigation, wrote the helper and tests, and ran lint/typecheck/tests. I reviewed the approach and the diff.

## Proposed Changes

Two high-severity CodeQL `js/path-injection` alerts flagged the unauthenticated, loopback-only `POST /api/paths/compare` endpoint in the local server: it passed request-body `path1`/`path2` straight into `arePathsEqual`, which calls `fs.statSync(path.resolve(...))`. A crafted `../` payload could probe arbitrary filesystem paths outside the sites directory.

This confines both operands to the server's `sitesRoot` before they reach any filesystem call. Anything outside `sitesRoot` cannot be a Studio site, so a non-match is the correct answer and the untrusted value never reaches `statSync` unguarded. The shared `arePathsEqual` helper is intentionally left untouched, since its other callers (CLI, desktop IPC) legitimately compare arbitrary absolute site paths that come from trusted local config.

No user-visible behavior change for legitimate use: the UI only ever compares real site paths under `sitesRoot`.

## Testing Instructions

- `npm test -- packages/common/lib/tests/fs-utils.test.ts` — new `isPathWithin` tests cover the root itself, descendants, `../` escapes, and the sibling-prefix edge case (`sites-other` must not count as inside `sites`).
- `npm run typecheck` passes across all workspaces.
- Manual: `POST /api/paths/compare` with two real site paths under the sites root returns `{ equal: true }` when they match; a body with a `../` traversal path returns `{ equal: false }`.

## Pre-merge Checklist

- [x] Have you checked for TypeScript, React or other console errors?

author: kdroidfilter
body:
## What

Stop driving the render loop while a tao window is minimized, instead of continuing to record + present frames into a surface the user cannot see.

Each platform scene host gets a `if (window.isMinimized) return` guard at the top of its frame body, placed **before the frame-clock tick**:

- `TaoComposeSceneHost.kt` (macOS) — `renderFrameSuspending`
- `TaoComposeSceneHostWindows.kt` — `onRedrawRequested`
- `TaoComposeSceneHostLinux.kt` — `onRedrawRequested`

`TaoWindow` re-kicks the loop with `requestRedraw()` on the `MINIMIZED`-off (restore) event.

## Why

The loop is `invalidate`-driven, so a *static* minimized window already renders nothing. The gap is *animated* content: Compose animations keep invalidating and the loop keeps doing full record + GPU work into a hidden surface.

- **Windows is the real case**: ANGLE uses a flip-model swapchain, which never returns `DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED`, so there is no vsync back-pressure while minimized — the loop can spin at full rate.
- **Linux** already throttles via swap-in-flight back-pressure (Wayland withholds frame callbacks when occluded); the guard is belt-and-suspenders there and additionally covers the app-synthesised minimize (Wayland reports no iconified state).
- **macOS** has no such back-pressure on the Metal present path.

## Mechanism

Gating **before** `sendFrame` means the frame clock never advances while minimized, so `withFrameNanos`-driven animations re-suspend without emitting new invalidations. The `FrameDispatcher` then parks on its own — only the frame(s) already in flight at minimize time hit the early return. Restore's `requestRedraw` advances the clock again and resumes normal rendering.

This mirrors the standard practice of Flutter (`AppLifecycleState.hidden` stops `onBeginFrame`/`onDrawFrame`), Qt (`isExposed()` → stop rendering), Electron (`backgroundThrottling`) and browser rAF throttling — a pure render-pause, no forced GC.

## Test

`./gradlew :decorated-window-tao:compileKotlin` passes. Behavioural check: run a demo with a running animation, minimize, confirm CPU/GPU drops to idle and rendering resumes cleanly on restore.

author: btgaskin
body:
## What changed

- adds an explicitly Experimental `:shoal_forage` task built around 16 moving Falandays reservoirs, two persistent material needs, and an optional association need
- adds observer-aware sector vision for resources and conspecifics, blind and deterministic bearing-sham controls, proximity-based need restoration, and a three-output variable-speed turning actuator
- adds separate analysis contracts for material satisfaction, demand-normalized material regulation, association satisfaction, grouped movement, perceptual-graph structure, contacts, speed, and wall occupancy
- adds a resumable 44-job sight-range pilot and a separate 70-job one-factor operating-point screen covering input gain/shape, resource demand/feedback, association demand/feedback, association radius/normalization, and resource sight range
- records provenance and atomic job outputs, and provides paired descriptive contrasts and figure scripts without promoting the local run bundles to package evidence
- adds a production-safe documentation draft state: the shoal study remains available locally but is omitted from production routes, search, sitemap, navigation, and generated social-preview images
- documents the protocol, evidence boundary, platform limitations, and Core-versus-Experimental distinction; updates the bundled BrainlessLab skill accordingly

## Why

This provides a small first experiment for asking whether social perceptual opportunity changes task success and collective motion in a mobile ensemble of Falandays-controlled agents. Material regulation is kept separate from social satisfaction, coherence, proximity connectivity, and perceptual-graph structure, so grouped motion is not treated as successful foraging.

The design is motivated by visual-social work in fish and by cross-scale interaction-range sweeps, but it is not a fish model and makes no criticality claim. The task, components, protocol, and evidence remain explicitly Experimental. The study page is a repository draft and will not appear on the live site.

## Pilot evidence

The sight profile completed all 44 planned jobs: two matched blocks across blind, veridical, and bearing-sham conditions; association need on/off; and conspecific sight ranges 2, 3.5, 5, 7, and 10.

The operating-point profile completed 70 jobs: a matched baseline plus low/high one-factor settings for 17 operational axes in two blocks. It includes every exposed operational association control (drift, restoration, radius, neighbor normalization, feedback gain/exponent/probability) and conspecific sensory gain/shape. Structural construct choices such as the setpoint and deficit direction remain fixed.

Both screens are intentionally underpowered. Sight range changed the perceptual graph but did not yield a monotonic material-regulation benefit. Veridical social sight changed movement coherence, while association settings changed social satisfaction, resource encounters, and coherence in non-monotonic and sometimes opposing directions. High wall occupancy and near-floor material regulation make these pipeline diagnostics, not evidence of shoaling or a social-performance advantage. Generated run artifacts remain git-ignored and unpublished.

## Validation

- full `Pkg.test()` passed
- focused shoal task, analysis, control, component-catalog, and draft-publication tests passed
- the registered experiment CLI lists both workflows
- production Astro build passed with 80 pages; the draft study route, search entry, sitemap entry, and OG image are absent
- sight pilot completed 44/44 jobs; operating-point screen completed 70/70 jobs; figure scripts completed
- `git diff --check` passed

author: umbralcalc
body:
The distribution layer for the agent-usability arc — turns "we built a validated skill" into "an agent anywhere can install and use it".

## What's here
- **Plugin + marketplace.** The repo is now a Claude Code plugin marketplace (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` + `plugin.json`). The plugin's `skills` field points at the existing `.claude/skills/` dir, so the `stochadex-model` skill and its four drift-tested recipes ship **without a duplicated copy**.
  ```
  claude plugin marketplace add umbralcalc/stochadex
  claude plugin install stochadex@stochadex
  ```
- **Prebuilt binaries (no Go toolchain).** The CLI is pure Go (CGO off) and cross-compiles for macOS/Linux/Windows × amd64/arm64. **v0.5.3's binaries are already attached to its [Release](https://github.com/umbralcalc/stochadex/releases/tag/v0.5.3)**, so the documented install works today:
  ```
  curl -L ".../releases/latest/download/stochadex-$(uname -s|tr A-Z a-z)-$(uname -m|sed s/x86_64/amd64/)" -o stochadex
  # or: go install github.com/umbralcalc/stochadex/cmd/stochadex@latest
  ```
- **Release automation.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` cross-compiles and attaches binaries on every `v*` tag, so future releases need no manual step. It creates the Release from the tag annotation if one doesn't exist (a manual `gh release create` with richer notes wins if it ran first) and uploads with `--clobber` so re-runs are idempotent.
- **Onramp docs.** A top-level `README.md` (the repo had none) covering all three entry paths — plugin, CLI, Go library — with a no-toolchain example verified to run with `go` absent from PATH. Plus a CLI-install prerequisite in the skill.

## Verification
- Install one-liner resolves against the live release (HTTP 200) and the downloaded binary runs a config with `go` absent from `$PATH`.
- Cross-compilation confirmed for all five targets (CGO off).
- Both JSON manifests parse; `release.yml` is valid YAML.

author: wei18
body:
Implements the six confirmed findings from a design audit of three screens (Home, Completion, Daily hub). All six were reviewed as before/after previews and signed off before implementation.

Each phase is its own commit, ordered lowest-risk first.

| | Change | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| **D2** | exhausted-state `Practice` button gets `.tint(accent.primary)` — it had none, and there is no app-root tint fallback, so it rendered system blue | Sudoku |
| **C2** | `design-system.md` CompletionView row synced to as-built (no Liquid Glass, no rank delta — the latter removed in #698) | docs |
| **H2** | Home nav-card icons normalized to outline weight (`trophy.fill`→`trophy`, `chart.bar.fill`→`chart.bar`) | both apps |
| **H1** | Leaderboard card gets `arrow.up.forward` instead of `chevron.right` — it presents the system Game Center modal, not an in-app push | both apps |
| **D1** | new `accent.celebratory` token; both apps' streak flame repointed off `status.warning` | both apps |
| **C1** | Completion hero border raised to full opacity to clear the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 floor for non-text boundaries | both apps |

### Why D1 needed a new token

The streak flame was borrowing `status.warning`, so a celebratory indicator and a failure warning rendered in the same ink on the same screen — the same misuse class as #767. `AccentTokens` is a struct, so the new field required updating all three construction sites (built-in/neutral theme, Sudoku, Minesweeper). The neutral theme deliberately reuses a gray rather than inventing a hue, so an un-injected subtree cannot imply a "neutral celebratory brand color" exists.

Per-app values differ on purpose: Minesweeper's own `status.warning` is already orange (`#D9822B`), so reusing Sudoku's `#E0662E` would have reintroduced exactly the confusion being fixed. MS uses a redder, darker `#D4501F` (~14° hue separation), verified visually in both modes.

### Contrast measurements

- **D2** — white label on system blue `#007AFF` measured **4.02:1**, below this repo's own on-accent ink contract (≥4.5:1, #786/#797). On `accent.primary` `#5C7A4F` it is **4.81:1**, so this fix also closes a pre-existing contract violation.
- **C1** — border at `0.14` opacity measured **~1.15–1.22:1**. Intermediate values do not help (0.45 → 1.67:1, 0.80 → 2.69:1); full opacity clears 3:1 on both surfaces in both modes in both apps (worst case MS light **3.10:1**, best case MS dark **4.32:1**). Accepted tradeoff: margins now read tighter. The token-level root fix stays tracked in #846.

### Verification

- `swift test` green: **GameShellKit** (32), **MinesweeperKit** (370), **SudokuKit** (Completion 3, Home/Daily 32).
- **27 snapshot baselines re-recorded** across all six fixes — 13 Sudoku-side (Completion 3 · DailyHub 5 · Home 5) and 14 Minesweeper-side (Completion 7 · Daily 2 · Home 5). Every fix that moves pixels moves baselines: C1 the Completion sets, H1/H2 the Home sets, D1 the Daily sets.
- The Minesweeper Completion set (7) is the one worth calling out: C1 changes the *shared* `CompletionScreen`, so verifying only Sudoku would have shipped 7 red tests.
- No new user-facing strings, so the 7-locale catalogs are untouched.

### Out of scope

Two audit findings were deliberately excluded pending simulator/device verification: Home `glassEffect` empty-state borders (may be a headless-render artifact) and Completion VoiceOver not announcing the mistake count.

author: e6qu
body:
One PR. An adversarial pass over the surfaces prior sweeps under-examined — the client binaries, less-common IRC commands, and the custom queue. The `e6irc-queue` MPSC (lost-wakeups, capacity boundary, seq monotonicity, Drop/close races) and the ISUPPORT-vs-enforcement mapping both audited **clean**.

## Fixes
| Sev | Fix |
|-----|-----|
| **HIGH** | The CLI silently registered **unauthenticated** when only one of `--account`/`--password` was given (a footgun: "send as alice" would send as nobody). Now a loud error. |
| **MEDIUM** | CLI `history` **hung forever** if the server NAK'd the required caps; now fails loudly on NAK, answers PINGs while waiting, and errors on a mid-negotiation close. |
| **MEDIUM** | CLI `tail` on a **refused JOIN** hung silently; now reported like `send`/`history`. |
| **MEDIUM** | A `TOPIC` query on a `+s` channel **leaked the topic** (and the channel's existence) to non-members — the one query surface that forgot the secret-channel gate. Now returns `ERR_NOTONCHANNEL` like NAMES/WHO/WHOIS/LIST. |
| **MEDIUM** | NICK and QUIT were the only membership broadcasts hand-rolling a raw byte loop, so they **omitted the `server-time` tag** for capable clients (a logging bouncer saw `@time=` on JOIN/PART/KICK/TOPIC/MODE but not NICK/QUIT). Both now route through `send_timed` — fixing the class. |
| **LOW** | The services pseudo-client nicks (`nickserv`/`chanserv`) were **not reserved**, so a user could seize one and intercept its PRIVMSGs. One `SERVICE_NICKS` list now backs both the intercept and the NICK reservation. |
| — | `MONITOR +` at the list cap reported only the **first** over-limit nick and silently dropped the rest of the batch; it now reports them all. |
| — | `set_read_marker` was a **silent no-op** when the account name didn't resolve (in-core mirror could diverge from the DB); it now surfaces an `UnknownAccount` error the worker logs. |

## Not changed (surfaced, with reasons)
- **`bnc_buffer` orphan on account deletion** — unreachable: there is no account-deletion path anywhere in the code, and `bnc_buffer.owner` is `TEXT` for the `*` shared-network sentinel, so a FK doesn't fit. Nothing to hook cleanup into without inventing the delete feature.
- **No signal handling / unsupervised tasks** — an explicit, *logged* deferral (not a silent fallback); flagged, not silently patched.

## Tests
New: TOPIC-secret-hidden-from-nonmembers, service-nick-reserved, NICK/QUIT-carry-server-time, and CLI one-credential-flag-rejected.

## Verification
All four guards (`check-dead-code`, `check-dead-pub`, `check-duplication`, `check-noops`), `cargo fmt`/`clippy` (default + all-features), `cargo deny` clean. `cargo test` default + all-features green. PG-gated suites against a live PostgreSQL 15: **30 db / 12 http / 5 bouncer**, plus the full CLI e2e suite.

## What changed

- raise the per-instance aggregate decompressed selector-corpus ceiling from 512 MiB to 640 MiB
- retain the 64 MiB per-artifact cap, 20,000-file cap, one-million-call cap, traversal-depth cap, and discovery-entry cap

## Root cause

A healthy four-hour Superform Medusa run produced 584,398,777 and 612,564,364 bytes of valid selector artifacts across its two replicas. Both exceeded the former 512 MiB aggregate ceiling, so terminal analytics stopped early and reported `partial` plus a resource-limit warning despite every individual artifact remaining within its own safety bound.

The 640 MiB ceiling is deliberately finite and narrowly above the observed complete corpora. It lets these valid artifacts finish while preserving all independent file, call, traversal, discovery, and per-artifact limits.

author: mauricedesaxe
body:
Converges the control plane with upstream's dependency-injection refactor, the
family of seven commits ending at `3e344bd0`. Closes #84.

The point is not the shape of the wiring. It is that upstream rewrote the
landing zone every later feature arrives in — attachments, session diffs, and
everything after — and until we match it each of those ports has to be
rewritten by hand against a structure upstream no longer has. This clears that
tax once.

It also fixes a real bug. Threading a request-scoped logger (commit 3) replaced
five singleton services that captured the logger by value at construction, so
every log line from them carried the *first* request's trace id for the life of
the isolate. Production logs have been mis-attributing trace ids.

## The commits

Each is one upstream commit, applied in upstream's topological order, and each
passes the full gate on its own so the stack stays bisectable.

1. **extract `SessionMessenger`** — broadcast and send-to-sandbox behind an interface
2. **inject `SessionMessenger`** — the DO stops passing a `broadcast` closure
3. **request-scoped logger** — the trace-id fix above
4. **extract `SessionStatusService`** — status and its projections leave the DO
5. **dissolve the message-queue deps bag** — twelve positional collaborators
6. **extract a `SqlDatabase` port** — stores take a narrow query interface
7. **inject `SqlDatabase`** — routes and webhooks get an instrumented handle

## What was skipped, and why

We have not adopted session attachments (#87) or session diffs (#88), and
upstream built parts of this refactor around both. Where a hunk refactors code
we do not have, it is skipped rather than ported speculatively — when those
features land they bring upstream's post-refactor version directly. Each
commit body names its own omissions. Two upstream files have no counterpart
here and are skipped whole.

## Fork divergences preserved

Three pieces of fork-local behaviour sit inside code upstream restructured, so
a wholesale take would have deleted them while staying green:

- the pending-message and pending-sandbox-connect watchdogs, whose `broadcast`
  call sites upstream's patch had never seen
- the archive cascade, which lived *inside* the method extracted in commit 4
  (`test/integration/archive-cascade.test.ts` is what proves it survived)
- `createBoardArtifact`, the tldraw path

One deliberate naming divergence: `SessionStatusService` takes the session DO
namespace as `sessions`, not upstream's `parentSessions`, because our cascade
reaches children through it. This will conflict in a future sync; that is the
intended trade and it belongs in `docs/FORK.md`.

Upstream's new "does not schedule when the prompt is deferred for sandbox
spawn" test is not ported — we arm the connect watchdog on exactly that path,
so our existing test keeps the opposite assertion.

## Verification

Full gate per commit: typecheck, unit, integration, lint, prettier. Every
test-count delta is reconciled rather than assumed — unit went 1917 → 1935 and
integration 567 → 569, with each move traced to a test upstream added, removed,
or relocated between suites. All other packages pass unchanged.

author: vando-sketch
body:
## Summary
- Scaffolds the teams-task-agent pipeline described in the architecture doc: Graph webhook receiver → Redis (BullMQ) queue → worker → Claude Agent SDK processing → Nextcloud write.
- Node.js + TypeScript (ESM) throughout, chosen for lower resource footprint on the target homeserver and a single-language stack across receiver/worker/Claude Agent SDK.
- Built as an integration branch (`feat/repo-scaffold`) with independent pieces developed on their own branches and merged in: webhook receiver, Graph API client + subscription renewal, Claude Agent SDK processor, Nextcloud writer, Docker infra.

### Components
- `src/receiver/` — Express webhook endpoint: handles the Graph subscription validation handshake, validates `clientState`, and enqueues jobs. Responds within milliseconds, does no inline processing (per the architecture doc's #1 pitfall).
- `src/queue/` — BullMQ queue backed by Redis, shared between receiver and worker.
- `src/graph/` — Microsoft Graph client (client-credentials via `@azure/msal-node`): file download, subscription create/renew. Plus `scripts/renew-subscription.ts` for scheduled renewal (subscriptions expire in days, max 30).
- `src/claude/` — Claude Agent SDK integration that finds open tasks in a file's text content and drafts solutions, using the SDK's structured JSON output. Prompt/output shape is a first-pass default, called out as an open product decision in the architecture doc.
- `src/nextcloud/` — writes results directly into Nextcloud's data directory (same host, no network hop) and triggers a scoped `occ files:scan`; path-traversal-safe filename handling.
- `src/worker/` — wires the above into one BullMQ `Worker`: download → process → write.
- `docker-compose.yml` / `docker/` — receiver, worker, and Redis services; bind mount for Nextcloud's data directory.

### Known open items (documented in README)
- Exact Graph notification payload shape for driveId/itemId extraction is implemented defensively per documented Graph behavior, not yet verified against a live subscription.
- Claude processing prompt/output schema is a placeholder default, not a finalized product decision.
- Subscription IDs aren't persisted yet — `renew-subscription.ts` takes one via env var for now.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm test` passes (28/28 tests, no real network/Redis/Graph/Anthropic calls — all external calls mocked)

author: veronicaz41
body:
Three fixes from reviewing codex session `01KY1F0V56X9B64ZQEPC9CPPZB` ("how does codex memory work?"):

## 1. The final codex answer was dropped (`fix:`)

Codex narrates: a tool-using turn writes several assistant messages to the rollout — short preambles between tool calls, then the real reply. The pairing emitted each as its own answer; the first preamble claimed the turn row, and the double-attach guard dropped the actual final answer (attach-or-drop, so it vanished). The reviewed session kept *"I'm using the OpenAI docs skill…"* and lost the 1.9KB reply.

- `RolloutPairing` merges a turn's messages in order and re-yields the merged whole on growth — every earlier view is a strict prefix of a later one — with a per-key turn `ordinal` (repeated identical prompts share `hash(prompt)`, the only join key).
- The tailer's content-addressed dedup then works unmodified: a grown answer hashes to a fresh key → fresh emit + retry window.
- `attachOtelResponse` gains an **extend** mode (rollout answers only): grow-only upsert on the ordinal-th same-key row; equal/shorter re-emits drop as done (retry/restart idempotency); summary composes once; the stale-attach ts bound still applies. Mode B stitching is untouched.

Verified end-to-end: parser reproduces the exact 1968-char merged answer from the real rollout file, and a live-growth daemon test pins preamble-attaches-then-final-replaces on one row.

## 2. The "9 secrets" in that session are false positives (`rules:`)

All nine are config key *names* from a fetched docs page (`memories.disable_on_external_context`, …) — dotted lowercase identifiers that clear the 3.5-entropy gate (3.57–3.83 bits). The generic-api-key rule now suppresses values that are *entirely* a lowercase dotted identifier path, via a `(?-i:…)` guard (case-folded it would swallow JWTs). Verified per the rule-change protocol:

- mutation check: the suppression test fails against the old rules;
- differential probe over all 121 stored request bodies (live DB + two backups): exactly the 11 intended suppressions, **zero** new findings, nothing else lost.

## 3. Tool-call args JSON wasn't foldable in the detail view (`viewer:`)

Mode B bodies are mixed prose+JSON (`toolname\n{args}\noutput…`), which the whole-document tree path can't fold. The flat path now renders each JSON *line* as the same foldable tree, prose staying flat highlighted text, under the existing R7 guards (any leak value that wouldn't survive the split keeps the whole body flat; leak-bearing subtrees start expanded). Also widens the `Name:` head cap 40→80 — MCP tool names are 43+ chars and silently lost their fold/pretty-print.

Note: truncated JSON (codex clamps the OTel `output` attribute mid-string) still renders flat — it doesn't parse, nothing to fold.

author: sadeq-n-yazdi
body:
## Summary

Resolves the issue #54 decision: **add a named multi-credential seam** to the ACME DNS-01 solver. The seam previously handed each provider exactly one credential, which Route 53 worked around by colon-packing two values into a single string. This generalizes the seam so a provider can receive **several named credentials**, while leaving every existing single-credential provider unchanged.

## Design note

1. **Config.** `ACMEDNSConfig` gains `credentials_refs` (`map[string]secrets.Ref`) alongside the existing single `credentials_ref`. The two are **mutually exclusive** per provider — `Validate` refuses both at once so the source of a credential is never decided by hidden precedence, and refuses neither in api mode. Each named reference is enumerated (sorted) into the well-formedness sweep and the startup required-secret preflight, so a malformed or unresolvable named ref fails at startup like any other. No value is ever quoted into an error (a `secrets.Ref` renders redacted everywhere). `credentials_refs` has no flat environment binding because its keys are operator-chosen; it is YAML-configured, and the two reflection-based env test walkers skip map fields accordingly.

2. **`dns01.Credentials`.** An immutable resolved credential set. Values are `secrets.Redacted`; the plaintext map is never exposed — only `Get(name)` for one named value and `Single()` for a lone value (which succeeds only when the set holds exactly one value, else fails closed). It implements `fmt.Formatter` so a `Credentials`, or a struct holding one in an exported field, renders a constant under every verb rather than leaking via raw reflection. The named map is cloned on construction so the stored set cannot be aliased.

3. **Provider constructors.** `NewAPIProvider` and every provider constructor now take `Credentials`. Single-token providers read `Single()` and refuse an empty/ambiguous set before their existing blank check. Route 53 reads named `access_key_id` + `secret_access_key`, keeps the colon-packed single form as a documented back-compat fallback, and **refuses exactly one named half** rather than silently colon-splitting a lone value into the wrong parts. Route 53 composes its two named halves through a new `secrets.Join`, whose reveal lives in the `secrets` package, so `route53.go` keeps its single documented unwrap site (the source-scanning `Reveal()` invariant test still holds at one per provider file).

4. **Transport wiring.** `resolveDNSCredentials` resolves either the single ref or each named ref **exactly once** and threads the set down; the sources are mutually exclusive, so there is no double resolve (issue #65 property preserved).

5. **Validation.** `validateACMEDNSCredentials` stays minimal and fail-closed: `provider` required, and exactly one credential source present with every named value non-zero.

## Security invariants held

- Every credential stays `secrets.Redacted` end to end; `Credentials` redacts under all fmt/log/json paths.
- No credential value in any error, log, or the provider-name echo.
- Blank/whitespace credentials still refused at construction (each provider's `IsBlank` check is retained).
- An empty/nil `Credentials` set refuses.

## Red-then-green evidence (each security guard reverted → RED, restored → GREEN)

- **`Credentials.Format` redaction** — removing the `fmt.Formatter` made `%+v`/`%#v`/`%q` of the set (and of a struct holding it) print `SECRET-abc123-do-not-leak` in full; restored → pass.
- **Route 53 partial-named refusal** — removing the one-named-half branch let a packed pair pasted into `access_key_id` be silently accepted; restored → refused with `ErrRoute53API`.
- **`NewNamedCredentials` map clone** — dropping the clone let a post-construction mutation of the caller's map change the stored set; restored → pass.
- **Config `both sources` refusal** — neutralizing the branch let a config setting both `credentials_ref` and `credentials_refs` validate; restored → refused.

## Gates (run locally on the whole module)

- `go build ./...` — ok
- `go vet ./...` — ok
- `golangci-lint run` — `0 issues.`
- `go test ./... -race` — all 36 packages ok

## Notes

- No OpenAPI change: DNS credentials are server config, not an HTTP surface.
- This refines ADR-0015's DNS provider seam; happy to add a short ADR if the maintainers want the rationale captured there.
- `config.go` / `cmd/valletd` edits are kept to a single bounded block for the concurrent-config-PR rebase.

## Why

Daily automated refresh of the generated OpenAPI types (`src/generated/api.d.ts`)
against the live PostHog schema, so the typed client stays in sync with upstream
API changes. Triggered by drift detection on 2026-07-21.

## Spec diff size

- `src/generated/api.d.ts`: **+3,072 / −403** lines (17,571 → 20,240).
- Regenerated via `pnpm codegen` — not hand-edited.

## New operationIds added to the filter

**None.** The drift detector flags every live-spec operationId absent from the
allowlist, but `openapi-filter.yaml` is a deliberately minimal CRUD/lifecycle
allowlist. Every new operationId matching a managed family is either:

- **auxiliary/non-CRUD** (e.g. `*_activity_retrieve`, `*_sharing_*`,
  `*_bulk_*`, `dashboards_collaborators_*`, `insights_suggestions_*`,
  `experiments_stats_retrieve`) — not part of the IaC surface, or
- a **redundant `_update` (PUT) variant** of an existing managed PATCH op
  (`cohorts_update`, `experiments_update`, `experiment_holdouts_update`,
  `experiment_saved_metrics_update`, `schema_property_groups_update`,
  `event_definitions_update`, `event_schemas_update`) — the clients manage
  updates via `partial_update` (PATCH), so these add no capability.

All other new operationIds belong to unmanaged product areas (agent apps, error
tracking, warehouse, LLM analytics, etc.) that are out of scope for this tool.
No brand-new managed resource family was warranted.

## Resources touched

Upstream renamed three serializer components; patched the affected client type
aliases (minimal, cast-through-`unknown` request-body/list types — no behavior
change):

| File | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/resources/dashboard/client.ts` | `PatchedDashboard` | `PatchedPatchedDashboardOpenApi` |
| `src/resources/experiment/client.ts` | `PatchedExperiment` | `PatchedExperimentWrite` |
| `src/resources/experiment/client.ts` | `PaginatedExperimentList` | `PaginatedExperimentBasicList` |

`pnpm typecheck` passes after the fix. All 71 filtered operationIds are still
present in the live spec — nothing disappeared.

## Unresolved drift / notes

- **No removed operationIds** to flag for human deletion.
- `pnpm test`: 290/291 pass. The one failure —
  `src/pull/run.test.ts > writes files and calls tagOnServer on a non-dry run`
  (500 ms timeout) — is **pre-existing on the base branch** and unrelated to the
  schema refresh (verified by re-running on a clean checkout). Left untouched.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` / `pnpm format:check` failures are also **pre-existing**
  (68 files) and untouched, per the "don't touch unrelated files" constraint.

author: didelotk
body:
## Summary

Two type-evaluation bugs reported from the downstream data platform (issue #1799), both severe enough that the affected production functions carry `# pragma: no cover` naming sparkless as the reason:

1. **`.cast(StructType)` returns `None`.** `df.select(F.struct(a, b).cast(target))` yielded `NULL` for the whole struct, typed `STRING`.
2. **`datediff`-derived booleans return the raw integer.** `F.when(c, x).otherwise(F.datediff(a, b) >= 30)` returned the day count (`134`) instead of `True`.

They turned out to be the **same defect in five places**, and #2 is much wider than reported.

Logged as **BUG-031** and **BUG-032**; **BUG-033** is recorded as Open (see *Deferred*).

## Reproduction

```python
# BUG-031
target = StructType([StructField("urgency", DoubleType()), StructField("risk", DoubleType())])
df.select(F.struct(F.col("urgency"), F.col("risk")).cast(target).alias("scores")).collect()
# sparkless:     [Row(scores=None)]                          schema: struct<scores:string>
# PySpark 4.0.0: [Row(scores=Row(urgency=1.5, risk=2.5))]    schema: struct<scores:struct<urgency:double,risk:double>>

# BUG-032
days = F.datediff(F.lit(date(2024, 6, 1)), F.col("last_sale_date"))
aged = F.when(F.col("last_sale_date").isNull(), F.lit(False)).otherwise(days >= F.lit(90))
df.withColumn("aged_stock_flag", aged).collect()
# sparkless:     [Row(..., aged_stock_flag=134), ...]   schema: ... flag:string
# PySpark 4.0.0: [Row(..., aged_stock_flag=True), ...]  schema: ... flag:boolean
```

BUG-032 is not specific to `datediff`. **Every** non-arithmetic expression in a `when`/`otherwise` value position was silently discarded:

| Expression in `.otherwise(...)` | sparkless (before) | PySpark 4.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `F.datediff(a, b) >= F.lit(90)` | `134` | `True` |
| `F.upper(F.col("sku"))` | `'stale'` (unchanged) | `'STALE'` |
| `F.col("sku") == F.lit("stale")` | `'stale'` | `True` |
| `F.col("last_sale_date").isNull()` | `date(2024, 1, 19)` | `False` |

## Real-Spark reference

Everything below was measured on **PySpark 4.0.0 / Java 21** (the DBR 17.3 pairing), not inferred:

| Expression | Result | Field names |
|---|---|---|
| `F.struct(F.col("a"), F.col("b"))` | `Row(a=…, b=…)` | source column names |
| `F.struct("a", "b")` | `Row(a=…, b=…)` | strings are **column refs**, not literals |
| `F.struct(F.lit(1), F.col("a"))` | `Row(col1=1, a=…)` | unaliased literal → `col<position>` |
| `F.struct("a", F.lit("k"))` | `Row(a=…, col2='k')` | position, not a running count of anonymous fields |
| `F.struct(c.alias("x"))` | `Row(x=…)` | alias wins |
| `.cast(StructType)` | positional rename **and** retype | arity mismatch → `AnalysisException` |

## The shared failure shape — confirmed

Yes: the sibling agent's hypothesis holds, and `.cast(StructType) → None` is a textbook instance. **A hardcoded operation/type dispatch whose unmatched case falls through to a silent default**, making *unimplemented* indistinguishable from a genuine SQL NULL. Five instances, all reached by these two bugs:

| Site | Fall-through | Missing case |
|---|---|---|
| `ConditionEvaluator._evaluate_column_operation_value` (lazy `select`) | `return None` | `struct` |
| `SchemaManager._infer_expression_type` (`select` types) | `StringType` | `struct`, `cast`, boolean ops, `CaseWhen` |
| `TypeConverter.cast_to_type` | `return value` (no-op) | `StructType` |
| `CaseWhen._evaluate_column_operation_value` | **`return operation.column`'s value** | everything but arithmetic |
| `CaseWhen.get_result_type` | `StringType` | boolean ops, `cast` |

Two aggravating factors worth calling out:

- **Parallel tables that drifted.** `select` and `withColumn` each have their *own* dispatch for the same question. `ExpressionEvaluator` (withColumn) implemented `struct`; `ConditionEvaluator` (select) did not. `_handle_withcolumn_operation` typed `cast`; `_infer_expression_type` did not. Neither path is a subset of the other, so "it works in withColumn" was never evidence it works in select.
- **`CaseWhen`'s default is worse than `None`.** Returning the operand yields a value of a *plausible type for the column*, so it survives every downstream check. `134` where a boolean belongs is far harder to notice than `NULL`.

## Fix

- **New `sparkless/core/struct_builder.py`** — one definition of struct argument unpacking and PySpark's field-naming rules. `ConditionEvaluator` and `ExpressionEvaluator` both delegate to it, so the two projection paths can no longer drift. This removed ~125 lines of duplicated, subtly-wrong logic from `ExpressionEvaluator` and incidentally fixed `F.struct("a", "b")`, which treated every string after the first as a literal.
- **`SchemaManager`** — added `struct`, `cast`, boolean-operation and `CaseWhen` cases. The cast branch accepts any type object exposing `simpleString()`: when PySpark is installed, sparkless's type classes inherit from *PySpark's* `DataType` rather than sparkless's, so `isinstance(x, DataType)` silently fails and types the cast `STRING`. (This one only reproduces with pyspark in the venv — worth knowing.)
- **`TypeConverter.cast_to_type`** — added the `StructType` branch (positional rename + retype).
- **`CaseWhen`** — the fall-through delegates to the shared `ConditionEvaluator`; arithmetic/unary branches kept, since `ConditionEvaluator`'s arithmetic path returns `None` for the unary form.
- **`BOOLEAN_RESULT_OPERATIONS`** moved to `core/type_utils` so the several type-inference sites agree on one list.
- **`ConditionEvaluator`'s remaining fall-through now logs at debug level**, so the next gap of this shape is diagnosable rather than silent (see *Deferred* for why it does not raise).

## Relationship to #19's rounding bug

Same family, different member. #19 is a *wrong-value* bug — the scale was read from an attribute that never existed, so `getattr(..., "precision", 0)` won every time; the operation ran, with the wrong argument. Here the operation is **not dispatched at all**. Both share the underlying cause — several hand-maintained tables for the same question, no exhaustiveness check — and #19's three parallel `round` implementations are the same duplication that let `struct` diverge between the two evaluators. No overlap in the fix.

## Testing

- 20 new tests across two files, using the backend-agnostic `spark` fixture.
- **Verified under both engines**: `MOCK_SPARK_TEST_BACKEND=pyspark` with PySpark 4.0.0 on Java 21 — all 20 pass. Expectations are measured, not transcribed.
- **19 of the 20 fail on unfixed `main`** (the 20th guards the arithmetic branch that already worked).
- Full CI suite green locally: unit 1062 passed, parity 252 passed, documentation 2 passed, ruff format + check clean, mypy clean over 529 files.

## Deferred (not shipped, deliberately)

- **BUG-033 — a comparison yielding NULL returns FALSE in a `select` projection.** `ConditionEvaluator._evaluate_comparison_operation` returns `False` when an operand is NULL. `withColumn` already returns NULL correctly, so the two paths disagree. Found while fixing BUG-032, whose production shape guards the NULL row with a `when` and is unaffected. Not fixed here: NULL comparison semantics govern `filter()` library-wide, so it is a behavioural change of a different order, and it touches `_evaluate_comparison_operation`, which #19 also edits. Belongs with the Kleene-logic work of BUG-023. Logged as **Open**.
- **Making the fall-throughs raise.** Tempting, and it is the highest-leverage version of this fix — but it would convert every currently-silent gap across ~150 operations into a hard failure at once, in a compatibility shim whose value is graceful degradation. ## Gallery Integrity Audit — CLEAN

**Proof**: bezout-identity-oq026 — Iterated CRT: solvability of k simultaneous congruences
**Result**: clean (no integrity issues)

- **theoremCount 13** ✓ / **definitionCount 3** ✓ (defs: lcmList, CongSolves, Compatible; the 3 anonymous `example`s are not counted)

The generalized CRT — *a system with nonzero moduli is solvable iff pairwise compatible (gcd(mᵢ,mⱼ) ∣ aᵢ−aⱼ), with the solution unique mod lcm(m₁,…,mₖ)* — is proved from scratch by induction over the list of congruences (`solves_of_compatible`, `solutions_unique_mod_lcmList`, packaged in `iterated_crt_full`). It reuses the **parent's** two-modulus merge/uniqueness (`gcd_dvd_implies_solvable`, `crt_unique_mod_lcm`) and one genuinely new lemma `nat_gcd_lcm_distrib` (gcd distributes over lcm on ℕ, proved via prime factorizations — the overview correctly notes this is not in Mathlib). author: regularkevvv
body:
Merges upstream `astral-sh/ruff` up to `4bee0797` — the exact commit pinned by the `astral-sh/ty` `0.0.60` release tag — so `ty-extended 0.60.0` can be cut 1:1 against upstream `0.0.60`. Nothing past that tag is included; upstream ruff has 66 further commits that are deliberately left out.

## The merge

Two conflicts, both where upstream refactored code adjacent to a fork addition:

- **`types/function.rs`** — upstream replaced its `contains_unknown_or_todo` closure with `non_any_dynamic_content(..).is_absent()` in the redundant-cast check. Took upstream's predicate, kept the fork's `annotated_target.is_none()` guard.
- **`types/infer/builder.rs`** — upstream deleted the `ExpressionCache` type alias in favour of a struct of the same name. Dropped the alias (verified against the merge base that it was upstream's), kept the fork's `plugin_diagnostic_severity`.

## Pre-existing breakage fixed along the way

None of this is caused by the merge — every affected file is absent from it, and `git blame` traces each issue to `ebef5387d2` or `fa6e944b28`.

It went undetected because **nothing has ever checked**: this repository has no recorded GitHub Actions runs at all, so `ci.yaml` has never executed here. Worth deciding separately whether that is intentional.

- `ty_plugin_protocol` grew `ClassSummary::methods`, `BuildProjectIndexRequest::assignments` and `CallValueSummary::receiver`, but the example and wasm tests were never updated — 15 + 3 `E0063` errors. This blocked building *any* test target, so the merge could not be validated without fixing it.
- The `plugins` config options were never run through `cargo dev generate-all`, leaving them missing from the generated configuration reference and JSON schema entirely.
- The `ty_server` debug snapshot predated `PluginSettings`.
- Clippy had accumulated ~70 failures across the fork's crates.

## Breaking change

`PluginRequest::ValidateMutation` and `PluginResponse::Manifest` are now boxed; both variants dwarfed their siblings (752 vs 520 bytes, 464 vs 248), so every request and response paid for them. `Box` is serde-transparent, so **the wire format is unchanged** — verified by inspecting the serialized output rather than assumed, since the existing round-trip tests serialize and deserialize symmetrically and could not have caught a difference.

`CURRENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` therefore stays at `0.3`; bumping it would wrongly reject existing plugins during negotiation. The published Rust API does break, so `ty_plugin_protocol` and `ty_plugin_sdk` both go `0.0.3` → `0.0.4`.

## Verification

All local, given the absence of CI:

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p ruff_wasm -p ty_wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --workspace` — 8731 tests across 108 targets, zero failures (identical counts before and after the lint work)
- `prek` — all hooks pass

author: wayangalihpratama
body:
## What
This Pull Request introduces layout changes, security gates, and backend calculation fixes for the Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS) Explorer component:
1. **Agro-Ecological Zone Name Resolution**: Normalizes raw inputs (`zone.toLowerCase().trim()`) inside the Tinkhundla lookup in `InkhundlaHeader.js` to ensure the region's agro-ecological zone name (e.g. `"Middleveld"`) is correctly retrieved and displayed.
2. **Dynamic Reporting Consistency**: Replaced mock calculations in `IKSStatsView` with a rolling 12-month unique month count, showing the true ratio in the frontend card (e.g. `reportedMonths / 12 months reported` and `100%` when completed).
3. **Anonymized Stats Gating (TWG lock)**: Restricts access to consistency and form completion statistics for unauthenticated users, displaying a secure padlock placeholder card containing: `"🔒 - Sign in as TWG member to see data on report completness and consistency."`.
4. **Predictor Grid Realization**: Refactored Section B & C accordion panels into a responsive `2-column grid` with individual indicator cards containing a Month-Box timeline and text abbreviations underneath.
5. **Observed Status Colors**: Color-coded month status blocks inside the cards matching the design spec: active Section B blocks display in **Blue (`#3e5eb9`)** and active Section C blocks display in **Red (`#b10d0b`)**.

## Why
* **UX Mock Alignment**: The previous layout did not render a detailed breakdown timeline per-indicator or the scoring ratio, making months hard to trace.
* **Security & Role Gating**: Anonymously exposing form completion rates and reporting consistency stats breached operational guidelines; these must only be visible to authenticated Technical Working Group (TWG) members.
* **Data Correctness**: The reporting consistency must be dynamically calculated on unique submission months to display accurate progress logs.

## How

### Backend (`backend/api/v1/v1_iks/`)
* **`views.py`**:
  * Updated `IKSStatsView` to dynamically compute unique months with submissions within the rolling 12-month window.
  * Added validation in `IKSStatsView` to clear consistency and completion rates to `None` if the request is anonymous.
* **`serializers.py`**: Changed `IKSStatsSerializer` fields to accept `None` (nulls) to support anonymous lock states.
* **`tests_iks_stats_endpoint.py`**: Added assertions to verify stats are correctly returned as `None` for anonymous clients.

### Frontend (`frontend/src/components/Insights/`)
* **`IksTab.js`**: Forwarded the locked status and mapped the dynamic reported months subtitle to `KpiMetricCard`.
* **`PredictorAccordion.js`**:
  * Replaced the vertical list inside collapsed panels with a `grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 p-4`.
  * Added `Predictor observed` vs `Predictor not observed` legends at the top of Section B & C accordions.
* **`IndicatorRow.js`**:
  * Re-architected indicators to render as individual cards.
  * Mapped the `observedCount/totalMonths` scores.
  * Rendered 12 rounded month cells with centered checkmark icons for checked months.
  * Added dynamically-computed month labels underneath every cell box.
* **`KpiMetricCard.js`**: Styled the lock state flex-layout box with the custom padlock text.
* **`subcomponents.test.js`**: Updated tests to check for `rounded-[2px]` classes and separate lock node selectors.

## Verification & Testing
1. **Backend Tests**: Verified using `./manage.py test` — 446 tests pass.
2. **Frontend Tests**: Verified using Jest — 93 tests pass.

author: kohbanye
body:
Prepares the repo for public release and makes scoring a molecule a single command.

Today, running inference requires a clone of this repo, a full training environment, and two local `.ckpt` files that exist only on our cluster. `scripts/inference.py` additionally crashes before producing a score. This PR addresses both.

## What changes

**Inference no longer needs this repo's training stack.** The log-likelihood math moved into a `LogLikelihoodMixin` shared by the Lightning training modules and a new transformers-only `HFLanguageModel`. `import clamnp` no longer pulls in lightning — training entry points resolve lazily.

```python
from clamnp import NPLikenessScorer
scorer = NPLikenessScorer.from_pretrained()   # models from the HF Hub
scorer.score("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O")
```

```bash
clamnp "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"
clamnp --input molecules.smi --output scores.csv --normalized
```

**Naming now matches the paper.** `ratio` → `unstabilized` ("CLaM-NP Score (unstabilized)"), and the 3-model `stabilized` score — the CLaM-NP Score proper — becomes the default.

## Bugs fixed

- `scripts/inference.py` was unrunnable: it passed `alpha=` to `NPLikenessScorer`, which no longer accepts it, and defaulted to a `"weighted"` mode removed when gating replaced the fixed mixing parameter.
- `load_checkpoint` was duplicated between `scripts/inference.py` and `api_server.py` (the latter even carried a comment saying so); now one implementation in `clamnp/loading.py`.
- `api_server.py` re-read every checkpoint from disk on *each* request, so latency was dominated by loading hundreds of MB of weights. Models are now loaded at most once and cached; per-request options no longer mutate shared state.

## Commits

| | |
|---|---|
| `chore(repo)` | ignore job logs / generated artifacts, move 10 qsub scripts to `scripts/cluster/` |
| `refactor` | `src/` → installable `clamnp` package, Lightning-free inference core, mode rename |
| `fix` | repair the local-inference CLI, point callers at `clamnp.*` |
| `refactor(api)` | cache Hub-loaded models instead of reloading per request |
| `feat` | `clamnp` console script + `scripts/convert_to_hf.py` |
| `build` | hatchling backend, `clamnp` distribution, `[train]`/`[serve]`/`[viz]` extras |
| `docs` | real README + MIT license, current `hf auth login` command |

## Published models

`kohbanye/clamnp` is live (public), with `natural` / `synthetic` / `general` subfolders at 93 MB each:

| Model | Source checkpoint |
|---|---|
| `natural` | `checkpoints/20251023_1716/gpt2_natural/last.ckpt` |
| `synthetic` | `checkpoints/20251023_1716/gpt2_synthetic/last.ckpt` |
| `general` | `checkpoints/20260112_0125/gpt2_general/last.ckpt` |

These are the checkpoints all six paper-figure scripts reference.

## Verification

- **Conversion is lossless**: scores from the exported HF models match the original `.ckpt` bit-for-bit (max abs diff `0.00e+00` across 6 molecules).
- **End-to-end from a clean HF cache**: `clamnp "..."` downloads from the Hub and reproduces those same values — aspirin `-0.1217`, quinine `0.3580`, gefitinib `-0.9097`.
- `import clamnp` asserted free of lightning; all public + lazy entry points import; `api_server` imports; scripts compile.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean across `clamnp/`, `scripts/`, `api_server.py`.
- `uv lock` resolves (135 packages).

Training is unaffected — the `dev` dependency group keeps the full stack, so `uv run python scripts/train.py` works as before.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Notebooks and `notebooks/_render_*.py` are deliberately left uncommitted; whether to publish the paper-figure tooling (it hardcodes local `../checkpoints` paths) is a separate call.

author: hugoguitton-lucca
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2328.
Fixes #2392.

`apm audit --ci` previously had two cold-cache blind spots:
- `config-consistency` failed on valid virtual `claude_skill` deps when `apm_modules/` was absent.
- `drift` skipped on cold caches, so repos that commit deployed files could not fail CI for stale committed outputs.

## What changed

- add one lock-pinned scratch replay owner for `apm audit --ci`
  - runs a frozen manifest/lock preflight
  - materializes missing packages into a scratch-private `apm_modules/`
  - never writes the checkout, `apm.lock.yaml`, or live `apm_modules/`
- route both `config-consistency` and `drift` through that shared replay when `apm_modules/` is absent
- fail closed on replay errors instead of reporting a green drift skip in CI
- only treat missing replay outputs as drift when the path is git-tracked, so committed deployment repos fail correctly while clean gitignored deployments stay green
- tighten the manifestless virtual-skill waiver so the materialized shape and lock metadata must both identify `claude_skill`
- add the shared-owner architecture row, boundary lint, and regression coverage
- add real-CLI lifecycle proofs for tracked committed deployments, gitignored controls, and cold-cache virtual-skill allow and deny rows

## Validation

### Lifecycle suites
- `APM_E2E_TESTS=1 uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/integration/test_required_lifecycle_state_machine.py tests/integration/test_audit_cold_cache_ci_e2e.py tests/integration/test_virtual_skill_audit_e2e.py`
- `APM_E2E_TESTS=1 uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/integration/test_audit_cold_cache_ci_e2e.py::test_cold_cache_audit_fails_for_tracked_stale_deployments_and_reconciles_idempotently tests/integration/test_audit_cold_cache_ci_e2e.py::test_cold_cache_audit_stays_green_for_gitignored_clean_deployments_when_comparison_runs tests/integration/test_virtual_skill_audit_e2e.py::test_valid_manifestless_virtual_skill_audits_clean_from_cold_cache tests/integration/test_virtual_skill_audit_e2e.py::test_cold_cache_malformed_virtual_skill_bytes_fail_closed`

### Targeted regression suite
- `uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/unit/install/test_architecture_invariants.py tests/unit/install/test_drift_detection.py tests/unit/install/test_drift_phase3.py tests/unit/integration/test_mcp_config_view.py tests/unit/policy/test_ci_checks.py tests/unit/test_audit_ci_command.py tests/integration/test_virtual_skill_audit_e2e.py tests/integration/test_audit_cold_cache_ci_e2e.py tests/integration/test_architecture_authorities.py -k 'not throttle'`

### Quality and taxonomy
- `uv run --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/quality`
- `uv run --frozen python scripts/check_test_assertions.py`
- `uv run --frozen python scripts/check_exact_test_duplicates.py`

body:
## Summary

- The amber glow behind the CaseCard peek/cover frames read as a solid block with a hard edge at the top of the card (user screenshot, 2026-07-21): the glow layer's radial gradient was centered at `75% 30%` with its transparent stop at 72%, so at the layer's top boundary the falloff was only ~43% complete — ~0.11 alpha of amber cut off instantly at the cover-wrapper/card edge.
- Fix: rebalance the radial wash (`85% 80% at 70% 38%`, transparent at 78%) and mask-fade all four layer edges with Tailwind v4 mask utilities (`mask-x-from-85% mask-y-from-85%`, composited with intersect), so alpha ramps to zero before every clip boundary instead of terminating mid-falloff.
- One class change; token colors only (`--color-accent-glow`), zero JS, card layout/composition untouched.

## Scope

Behavior change: `src/components/work/CaseCard.astro` — single class attribute on the `aria-hidden` glow layer.

Not in scope: the frames' positioning/rotation and the `--color-accent-glow` token value (0.2 alpha) are unchanged; the locked "dashboard frame offset + amber glow" treatment is preserved.

## Deliberate trade-offs

- A `closest-side` gradient (zero-at-edge by construction, no mask) was tried first but shrank the ellipse so much that the frames covered virtually all of it — the amber presence the locked treatment requires disappeared. The mask-fade approach keeps the generous wash and still guarantees ~0 alpha at every edge.
- Mask fade distances are percentage-based (15% per axis), so the fade band scales with the cover wrapper (~56px on standard cards, ~88px on the wide card) rather than being pixel-identical — acceptable since both read as smooth dissipation.

## Verification

- `yarn test` → 5 files, 88/88 pass; `yarn lint` → 0 errors, 0 warnings; `yarn build` → complete.
- Built output served locally and the FeaturedWork section screenshotted at 1280 and 1920 (Playwright/Chrome): all three cards show the glow melting into the card background — no hard light edge on any card edge at either width.
- Isolated the glow layer (frames hidden, alpha boosted to 0.8) to verify mask geometry: soft fade on all four edges, no clipping against the card's `overflow-hidden` boundary.

no ticket — small real change
