author: rossiter78
body:
## What this is

`/aidsef-begin` — a one-time onboarding wizard that turns a fresh clone of the AIDSEF template into a working project. It automates getting-started **Phase D steps 4–9**, which until now lived only as chat guidance. Design recorded in [`docs/adr/007-aidsef-begin-onboarding.md`](../blob/main/docs/adr/007-aidsef-begin-onboarding.md).

## The wizard (a charter-less orchestrator, run once after cloning)

1. **Interviews** the human — project purpose, hard rules, any existing plan docs, solo/team.
2. **Cleans out** the framework-authoring files for a truly-fresh clone: `docs/playbook/`, `docs/00-getting-started.md`, **every framework `docs/adr/NNN-*.md`** (keeps `docs/adr/README.md`, so the project numbers its own ADRs from `001`), and empties `BACKLOG.md`. This closes the framework-ADR-inheritance gap left open in [ADR-005](../blob/main/docs/adr/005-project-workspace.md).
3. **Drafts** the project's own `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` from the interview; the human reviews.
4. **⏸ Pauses** to hand off the two browser-only steps (OAuth secret, GitHub App access) — which it must never do itself — *before* any PR, so the AI review can run. The handoff explains, in plain language, what each step is for, why only the human can do it, and exactly where to click.
5. **Runs** `scripts/setup-repo.sh`.
6. **Opens one setup PR** whose approval adopts the constitution (Phase 0). No separate ratification form — Git records who/when ([ADR-006](../blob/main/docs/adr/006-slim-adoption-block.md)).
7. **Points** the human at `/aidsef-1-spec`.

## Design decisions (confirmed with the human)

- **One setup PR**, not two — fewer approvals for a solo operator; adopting the rulebook is part of that one approval.
- **Wizard is kept, not self-deleted** — so setup can be re-run if someone wants to start over.
- **Truly-fresh clean-out** — including the framework's own ADRs.
- **Charter-less** — an orchestrator like `/aidsef-4-build`; no new role among the nine.

## Also

- The template `README.md` gains a findable **"Start your project"** section carrying the pre-wizard steps (Use this template → `git clone` → open in Claude Code → `/aidsef-begin`).
- `docs/00-getting-started.md` points Phase D at the wizard (keeps the manual steps as the under-the-hood record).
- The implemented item leaves `BACKLOG.md`.

`risk:standard` — a new skill + docs; touches no hooks logic, CI gates, or the traceability tool. No code changed; existing tests unaffected.

## Note for the acceptance test

When you clone AIDSEF fresh and run `/aidsef-begin`, it will pause and ask *you* to do the two browser settings and to approve the setup PR — by design, those are yours alone. The run exercises the real flow end to end, with those two human touchpoints.

body:
Closes #168. Infrastructure for the ISEF LGMEF study: ablation studies over Royal Chess mechanics evaluated with matched self-play agents.

## What's here

**Engine ablation switches** (opt-in `GameEngine` kwargs; defaults preserve the full v2 game):
- `knight_mode='legacy'` → No Knight Redesign
- `enable_boulder=False` → boulder removed from the initial position
- `enable_tiny_endgame=False` → rule never activates (all 3 activation sites guarded)
- `enable_manipulation=False` → manipulation turns not generated (no-legal-moves loss check keeps full-rules semantics; only-manipulation positions surface as empty turn lists → draw, documented)
- `extra_move_every=N` → positive-control broken mechanic (immediate second turn every Nth completed turn, latch prevents chaining)

**Trainer**: `engine_kwargs` threaded through `play_training_game`/worker tuple/`training_loop`; per-game `metrics` dict (avg/max branching, executed turn-type counts = mechanic usage, captures, tiny-endgame activation, repetition/endgame blocks) in `game_info` and the per-iteration `games/iter_*.jsonl`.

**New modules**:
- `src/experiments/variants.py` — named registry: `full`, `no_boulder`, `no_tiny_endgame`, `no_queen_manipulation`, `no_knight_redesign`, `baseline`, `control_inert` (negative control), `control_double_move` (positive control)
- `src/experiments/wellformedness.py` — random-playout gate: termination, nonempty turns, per-side ROYAL-count invariant (not king presence — a king can legitimately be captured while the royal queen survives), ablated-mechanic-never-fires
- `src/run_experiment.py` — one command per (variant, seed); gate always runs first and aborts on failure; provenance `experiment.json`; outputs under `models/experiments/<variant>/seed<k>/`

author: oimiragieo
body:
## Summary

- Adds **intra-file parallel search** to `rust_core/src/backend_cpu.rs`'s `CpuBackend::search_file_memmem` / `search_file_regex` — the functions behind the PyO3 `RustBackend.search()` FFI method that Python's `RustCoreBackend` (`src/tensor_grep/backends/rust_backend.py`) calls into. For a single file at/above **50 MiB**, the file is split into **line-aligned byte chunks** (a chunk boundary is always snapped forward to the byte right after a `\n`, so a line can never be split across a seam) and each chunk is searched **in parallel with `rayon`**, using the exact same per-line `memmem`/regex matching logic the serial path already used.
- Below the threshold, on a single-core box, or when a file has too few line breaks to usefully split, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged — same whole-buffer single-pass scan as before (now via `memchr_iter` instead of a manual byte loop for the newline scan, a behavior-preserving micro-improvement).
- This is the SAME idiom `native_search.rs::search_file_chunk_parallel` (already shipped, native_search.rs:1532-1611) uses for `--json`/`--count`/`--quiet` output — applied here to the *other* native CPU search implementation in this repo, which had **zero** intra-file parallelism before this change.

## Why `backend_cpu.rs`, not `native_search.rs`'s default text-output path

The task's benchmark reference (`docs/tool_comparison.md:58`, the 200MB single-file "tie" row: `tg search --no-ignore ERROR .../large_file_200mb.log`) exercises `native_search.rs`'s **default plain-text streaming path**, which routes through `NativeCpuBackend` per `docs/routing_policy.md`. I verified (file:line) that `native_search.rs` already has a proven chunk-parallel path — `FileChunkPlan`/`plan_file_chunks`/`search_file_chunk_parallel` (native_search.rs:645-1611) — but it is **deliberately gated off** for the default text and `--ndjson` modes:

```rust
// native_search.rs:1498-1522
fn should_use_chunk_parallel_search(config: &NativeSearchConfig, path: &Path) -> Result<bool> {
    if !config.parallel_large_files
        || !config.mmap
        || config.null_data
        || config.ndjson
        || (!config.json && !config.count && !config.quiet)   // <- excludes default text mode
        ...
```

That exclusion is not an oversight. `rust_core/tests/test_native_search.rs::test_native_search_default_output_streams_before_search_completion` (:771-796) and its `--ndjson` sibling (:798-829) assert the **first match must stream at least 25ms before the whole scan completes** — a real, tested, deliberate product contract (grep-like progressive output on huge files). A genuine multi-core speedup on that path would shrink total wall time toward `T/N`; on a fixture sized for that exact test, that plausibly collapses below the fixed 25ms margin — a foreseeable regression I can't verify without a local compile (CPU-safe: no cargo/rustc on this shared box). Reconciling true parallelism with that streaming/incremental-output guarantee needs a different design (e.g. stream an initial serial slice while parallelizing the remainder in the background) and is out of scope here — I did not touch it.

`backend_cpu.rs::search_with_paths` has no such contract: it's a synchronous call that collects every match into a `Vec` and returns it once, so there is nothing a parallel scan can disturb except *which thread* does the comparing — and it had no chunk-parallelism at all, making it a clean, correctness-first target that still delivers the requested mechanism (line-aligned rayon chunking, mirroring the existing idiom) on a real, previously-unparallelized path.

**Honesty note:** this PR does **not** claim to fix the `docs/tool_comparison.md:58` benchmark row — that row measures a different backend (`NativeCpuBackend`/`native_search.rs`) than the one this PR touches (`RustCoreBackend`/`backend_cpu.rs`). Confirmed via a documentation sweep (no doc anywhere asserts a cross-backend claim this PR would make stale).

## Design

- `LineAlignedChunk { start, end, first_line }` + `plan_line_aligned_chunks` (backend_cpu.rs:31-78): splits a byte buffer into up to N contiguous ranges, each boundary snapped forward to the next `\n` (or EOF) via `align_chunk_end_to_newline`.
- `scan_lines_memmem` / `scan_lines_regex` (backend_cpu.rs:111-205): the **one** per-line matching function — used both for the small-file whole-buffer scan (`first_line_number == 1`) and for every parallel chunk (`first_line_number` = that chunk's first line). The parallel path cannot diverge from serial because it's the identical predicate on a different byte range + line offset.
- `search_contents_memmem_maybe_parallel` / `_regex_maybe_parallel` (backend_cpu.rs:207-274): the dispatcher. Below 50 MiB or fewer than 2 planned chunks -> calls the whole-buffer scan directly. Otherwise -> `chunks.par_iter().map(|c| scan_lines_*(...)).collect::<Vec<Vec<CpuMatch>>>()`, then a sequential `.flatten()`.
- Threshold: `LARGE_FILE_PARALLEL_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 50 * 1024 * 1024`, chosen to exactly match `native_search.rs::LARGE_FILE_CHUNK_THRESHOLD_BYTES` (native_search.rs:28) rather than inventing a new number, so "large file" means the same thing everywhere in `tg`.
- Chunk count: one per available core (`std::thread::available_parallelism()`), same fallback policy as `native_search.rs::configured_chunk_parallelism_threads` when no override is configured. `backend_cpu.rs` has no config struct (plain method args only), so there's no override knob here.
- Multi-file directory walk in `search_with_paths` is **untouched** (still a serial `for entry in WalkDir` loop) — per "don't double-parallelize," only the per-file scan gained intra-file parallelism; a large file hit mid-walk benefits too, but the walk's own structure is unchanged.

## Correctness argument (the crux)

1. Matching was **already** strictly per-line before this change — a match never looks past a `\n`. So partitioning the file at line boundaries cannot change *which* lines match, only which thread checks them.
2. Chunk boundaries are always contiguous and newline-aligned — every byte of the file is scanned by exactly one chunk, so no line is ever duplicated or dropped at a seam. (Verified by property tests across chunk counts 2..=16, see below.)
3. `Vec<LineAlignedChunk>::par_iter().map(..)` stays an `IndexedParallelIterator` throughout (`Map<I, F>: IndexedParallelIterator` when `I: IndexedParallelIterator`, confirmed against rayon 1.12's published docs — a `Vec`'s `par_iter()` always is one). `collect()` on an indexed parallel iterator reassembles results in source order regardless of which thread finishes first, so flattening the per-chunk match vectors in chunk order reproduces the serial scan's exact match order.

## Tests

All in `rust_core/src/backend_cpu.rs`'s new `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` unless noted:

- `plan_line_aligned_chunks_{empty_content,single_requested_chunk}_returns_empty` -- degenerate-input contract.
- `plan_line_aligned_chunks_boundaries_never_split_a_line` + `..._full_coverage_across_many_chunk_counts` -- contiguity (`chunk[i].end == chunk[i+1].start`), full coverage (`chunks[0].start == 0`, `chunks.last().end == content.len()`), and newline-alignment, the second across chunk counts 2..=16 on variable-length-line content.
- `align_chunk_end_to_newline_{snaps_forward_when_mid_line,unchanged_when_already_at_boundary,runs_to_eof_when_no_more_newlines}` -- direct boundary-snapping unit tests.
- `scan_lines_memmem_chunked_matches_whole_buffer_serial_scan` / `..._invert_match_...` / `scan_lines_regex_chunked_matches_serial` -- **the crux test**: needles placed at the first line, the last line, and immediately around every internal boundary of a deterministic 5-chunk plan; asserts the chunked-and-reassembled `Vec<CpuMatch>` is `assert_eq!`-identical to a direct whole-buffer scan (memmem, regex, and inverted-match modes all covered).
- `scan_lines_memmem_no_match_chunked_matches_serial_empty_result` -- the explicit no-match edge case: a l

author: alexrao2000
body:
Implements ADR-0059 decision 1 (`docs/adr/0059-sandbox-is-a-bounded-resource-envelope.md`).

No container in the chart declared an `ephemeral-storage` request or limit. `runner.resources` set cpu and memory only, and the same block is reused for the `bundle-fetch` and `bundle-extract` init containers. Disk was therefore the one resource dimension with no ceiling: the kubelet had nothing to schedule against and could not cap or evict an overrunning pod on its own account, leaving node-level `DiskPressure` eviction (which ranks victims by raw usage across the whole node, not by fault) as the only backstop.

## Changes

- `agentSandbox.runner.resources` (shared by the runner container and the `bundle-fetch`/`bundle-extract` init containers) now declares `ephemeral-storage` alongside `cpu`/`memory`: request `512Mi`, limit `4Gi`.
- `agentSandbox.runner.liteLLM.resources` (the LiteLLM sidecar) now declares `ephemeral-storage`: request `64Mi`, limit `256Mi` — the sidecar has no bundle/writable-path volume of its own, so a small fixed ceiling covers its writable layer and logs.
- Both changes are strictly additive to the existing `requests`/`limits` maps; the template already renders `resources` via `toYaml`, so no template change was needed.
- Sizing follows the ADR's decision 6 philosophy: bound a runaway (cloning a large repo, installing a big dependency tree, generating large artifacts), not constrain that same legitimate work. Every value stays operator-overridable via the standard values mechanism (e.g. `--set agentSandbox.runner.resources.limits.ephemeral-storage=8Gi`).
- Added `charts/agentos/ci/ephemeral-storage-assertions.sh`, a render-assert proving every sandbox container (runner, both init containers, and the litellm sidecar when enabled) renders an `ephemeral-storage` request and limit, and that an operator override is honored. Wired into `.github/workflows/helm-ci.yaml` alongside the existing render-assert scripts.

## Out of scope (tracked by ADR-0059, not this issue)

Per-volume `sizeLimit` on the `bundles`/`mc-config`/`writablePaths` `emptyDir` volumes (decision 2), bundle ingestion size/ratio caps (decision 3), the tenant `ResourceQuota`/`LimitRange` (decision 4), and the sandbox `PriorityClass` (decision 5) are separate decisions under the same ADR and are not addressed here.

```
bash charts/agentos/ci/render-assertions.sh
bash charts/agentos/ci/ephemeral-storage-assertions.sh
bash charts/agentos/ci/sandbox-hardening-assertions.sh
bash charts/agentos/ci/litellm-sidecar-assertions.sh
```
All pass.

author: noyitz
body:
## Problem

When a `ResponseProcessor` plugin is in the response chain, the framework sets `NeedsResponseBuffering=true` and accumulates all SSE chunks. At EndOfStream, `json.Unmarshal` fails because the buffered body is SSE format (`event: ...\ndata: {...}\n\n`), not a JSON object. All response plugins are skipped with:

```
Failed to parse response body as JSON, skipping response plugins
error: invalid character 'e' looking for beginning of value
```

This wastes CPU on buffering and prevents response plugins from processing streaming responses.

## Fix

Add `parseSSEResponseBody` as a fallback when `json.Unmarshal` fails:

1. Scan the buffered body line by line
2. Keep only lines starting with `data:`
3. Strip the `data:` prefix and parse each as JSON
4. Skip empty lines and `[DONE]`
5. Merge `model`, `usage`, and content fields across all events into a single `map[string]any`
6. Reconstruct content in the provider's native structure (e.g., Anthropic content block array) so downstream translators can process it

The merged map becomes `reqCtx.Response.Body`, allowing response plugins to read model name, usage info, and message content from SSE streams.

Handles both Anthropic Messages format (content_block_delta, usage at top level) and OpenAI format (choices[].delta.content, usage nested in response).

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed on a live cluster:

- **Before**: `ResponseProcessor` in response chain + streaming Anthropic model → `"Failed to parse response body as JSON, skipping response plugins"` → response passes through untranslated
- **After**: Same request → `"parsed SSE response body for response plugins"` → response plugins run, content and usage correctly extracted, translation succeeds

## Related

- PRs #138 and #153 (closed in favor of PR #169's chunk processing path — but the buffered path still needs SSE parsing when `ResponseProcessor` plugins are present)

author: acksell
body:
## Motivation

We embed the SDK in a Go daemon that runs one `codex app-server` per user session. Each session needs its own environment — most importantly `CODEX_HOME` (isolated auth/state per tenant) and sometimes `CODEX_API_KEY`. Today `SpawnOptions` offers no way to set environment on the spawned process, so the only options are mutating the daemon's own environment with `os.Setenv` (races when sessions spawn concurrently) or replacing the transport wholesale.

## Change

- `SpawnOptions.Env []string` — extra `"KEY=value"` entries appended to the inherited environment; since later entries win for duplicate keys, an entry overrides an inherited variable of the same name. Nil keeps today's behavior (inherit unchanged).
- `rpc.SpawnStdio` takes the entries as a trailing variadic parameter, so existing call sites stay source-compatible.

```go
codex.New(ctx, codex.Options{
    Spawn: codex.SpawnOptions{
        CodexPath: "/usr/local/bin/codex",
        Env:       []string{"CODEX_HOME=/srv/tenants/alice/.codex"},
    },
})
```

## Design note: `[]string` vs `map[string]string`

Three reasons for the slice form:

1. **It's what makes the `rpc.SpawnStdio` change non-breaking.** A trailing variadic parameter is the only way to extend the exported signature without touching existing call sites, and a variadic must be a slice type — `env ...string` composes as `SpawnStdio(ctx, bin, args, stderr, spawn.Env...)`.
2. **It mirrors `exec.Cmd.Env` exactly** — entries pass straight through with no conversion layer, and the semantics (last duplicate wins) are the standard library's own.
3. **Deterministic order.** Ranging over a map would randomize the appended entries run-to-run — harmless to exec's duplicate handling, but noisy for logging and reproducibility.

The tradeoff is that a map is more ergonomic and catches malformed entries (missing `=`) at the type level. Happy to switch `SpawnOptions.Env` to `map[string]string` (sorted before append, converted at the `SpawnStdio` boundary) if you prefer that shape — the variadic transport signature works either way.

## Tests

`TestSpawnStdioExtraEnv` spawns `/bin/sh` through the real transport and asserts all three behaviors in one round-trip: extra entry visible, parent environment still inherited, duplicate key overridden. `TestSpawnStdioWithoutEnvInheritsParent` guards the no-env default. Both skip on Windows. `go test ./...` passes.

author: rapaicm9
body:
A developer shortcut that unlocks Pro for the caller without a purchase, for exercising gated features while the payment provider is mocked. It is the purchase flow's tail without the charge or the purchase record - nothing was bought - and announces the same EntitlementChanged; already-Pro is an idempotent no-op.

The endpoint is mapped only in Development: the host wires it behind an IsDevelopment check, so it cannot exist in production at all, which an integration test pins by asserting a 404 there against a 204 in Development. It reads the caller through Identity's IUserContext - the first consumer of that seam, and Billing never parsing another module's tokens. A near-copy of Identity's ProblemDetails mapper rides along as Billing's first endpoint needs it; a shared web-edge home waits for the third module so every copy migrates at once.

## @cat-factory/contracts@0.154.2

### Patch Changes

- 91ea6b7: observability: forward the container agent's liveness heartbeat so a quiet-but-alive run stops looking wedged.

  A long, output-less phase — a `pr-reviewer` reading hundreds of files, say — advances the harness heartbeat but not its subtask counts. That heartbeat was dropped at the transport boundary: `ContainerAgentExecutor.pollJob` forwarded phase/progress/follow-ups but never `view.heartbeatAt`, so `agent_runs.updated_at` only moved on a progress change. A live-but-quiet run was indistinguishable from a wedged one to the DB, the stale-run sweeper (keys off `updated_at`), and the UI (a client clock off `startedAt`, not a server liveness signal). This is the observable-heartbeat gap ADR 0026 P3 named (its D2.1/D3 restored progress + the watchdog heartbeat, not the observable one).

  `RunnerJobView` now carries `heartbeatAt` (Cloudflare/local cast the harness view verbatim; the runner pool maps an optional `heartbeatPath`), `pollJob` forwards it as the running `AgentJobUpdate.lastActivityAt`, and the engine folds it onto the step's new `lastActivityAt` **throttled** (`shouldPersistActivity`, a 20s window well under the 5-min sweeper lease) — so a live-but-quiet run keeps `updated_at` fresh while a wedged run's frozen heartbeat correctly lets it go stale. The field rides the step JSON, so both runtimes persist it with no migration. The SPA surfaces "active Ns ago" in `StepRunMeta` (and thus the PR-review window), distinct from the elapsed clock. No harness change (the `heartbeatAt` field already exists), so no image bump.

- 48 V driver / PSU rows

Synced to the placeholder language already in `data.json`.

## 2. `config.js` — variant overrides keyed by item name
Per-variant qty overrides are keyed by item **name**, with names `\u`-escaped. Renaming the wire items in `data.json` would have **silently orphaned those keys** and broken the M3-2 overrides. Keys updated to match.

## Conductor sizing
The 12AWG power wire and 18AWG distribution wire are power-distribution items already marked professional/private scope — the gauge in their names and source notes was an inconsistent leftover. Both are now scope placeholders.

Shielded motor cable (18AWG 4C) **keeps** its gauge deliberately: motor circuits are low-voltage motion, inside the public scope per `ELECTRICAL_SCOPE_BOUNDARY.md`, which excludes branch-circuit, contactor, and high-current power-distribution design.

## Verification
Scanned with unicode decoding — **Git Bash `grep -F` gives false negatives on these files**, which is why the `index.html` and `config.js` copies were missed on the first pass. 65 items intact, JSON valid, publish output 29 files, zero residual strings.

## Pre-existing, not addressed here
3 `config.js` override keys were already orphaned before this change and never apply: `Frame Stiffener — Long Span Reinforcement`, `GT2 Timing Belt 10mm (Reinforced)`, `V-Groove Delrin Wheels (Polycarbonate)`.

author: kyle-sexton
body:
## What

Sharpens the `orchestrate` skill's per-worker tiering (imperative 7) into an explicit **volume-based default**, and broadens "tier" from model-only to model **and** reasoning effort.

## Why

Carried from the re-anchor round-2 ledger (task #3), observed in production: an `/orchestrate` run fanned out ~100–200 agents, all on the top-tier model. PR #340 (0.9.1) fixed the root spawn-inherit bug — SPEC EVERY SPAWN + CALIBRATE now carry a per-worker tier — but the residual enhancement (making the tier *default* flip on volume) was never built. The prior text stated the direction as a gradient ("the wider the fan-out, the cheaper the default per-worker tier") without wiring the verify/judge carve-out as the standing exception, and never named reasoning effort as a tiering lever.

## Change

`plugins/session-flow/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md` — imperative 7:

- Past a wide fan-out, the cheaper tier is now the **DEFAULT the whole fleet inherits** (volume multiplies every notch of over-provisioning).
- The **standing exception** is an explicitly hard stage — verify, judge/adjudicate, judgment-heavy synthesis — which keeps the parent tier. A premium fan-out outside those stages is a per-stage decision to justify, never a default to inherit.
- **Tier is model AND effort**: match reasoning depth (effort), not just the model, to the subtask.

`context/sources.md` — three new verbatim citations grounding the change in current official docs: the per-worker `effort` frontmatter lever, the workflow fleet-model inherit mechanism, and the platform's own wide-run threshold (its `Large workflow` warning + `/config` size guideline). Per the skill's model-/tool-agnostic construction, these version-pinned specifics stay in `sources.md`, never the imperatives or export brief.

## Grounding (fresh docs, this session)

- Subagent `model` precedence + `inherit` default, `effort` field, cost-routing guidance — <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents>
- Workflow fleet-model inheritance, per-stage routing, `Large workflow` threshold + size guideline — <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows>

## Gates

- `check-skill.sh orchestrate`: PASS (7/7 trigger phrases preserved, 125/500 lines, markdownlint clean)
- `check-changelog-parity.sh --check` and `--check-bump origin/main`: PASS
- `validate-plugin-contracts.mjs`, `generate-catalog.mjs --check`, `claude plugin validate .`: PASS
- Version bumped 0.12.2 → 0.12.3 with CHANGELOG entry in the same diff.

## Related

- PR #340 — the session-flow 0.9.1 spawn-inherit fix this builds on (SPEC EVERY SPAWN + CALIBRATE carrying a per-worker tier); not closed by this PR.
- The re-anchor round-2 ledger task #3 production observation that motivated the residual enhancement.

Closes #863.

## BR-002A — Store-path archaeology & contract proof

BR-002 execution (tracing the saw_lab/rmos store-layer kwarg defect) invalidated two load-bearing assumptions in the BR-001 next-candidate packet, so the implementation handoff was **not** implementation-ready. Per the re-scope ruling, this PR **corrects the living remediation artifacts** and **issues BR-002A** — a bounded archaeology/contract-proof Dev Order with **no production mutation**. body:
## Triggering Context

**Run triggered by:** Merged connector PR — [feat(source-uptick)!: update to 1.0.0 (#73740)](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/pull/73740), picked up by the autodoc workflow from source commit `e9f60008bb4d2056b980f3bebe2c5f6af4269446` on `master`.

**Relevant context:** https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/pull/73740

**Confidence impact:** The triggering PR is a merged, clearly-scoped connector release (v2.14 → v2.15 upgrade with field removals), which gives high certainty about what changed and keeps the Triggering Context score high.

## Documentation Confidence Assessment

**Overall Confidence: 4/5**

| Dimension | Score | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| Code Comprehension | 5/5 | Manifest-only declarative source; auth, pagination, retries, and incremental cursor are all self-contained in `manifest.yaml`. |
| API Documentation Quality | 4/5 | Official Uptick support docs cover versioning, patch notes, getting started, and an Airbyte-specific guide, but do not quantify rate limits. |
| Change Scope & Risk | 4/5 | Small, targeted additions (18 lines): clarified prerequisites and added incremental-sync and rate-limit notes. |
| Existing Doc Maturity | 4/5 | Well-established ~213-line doc with good structure and a few gaps around auth and sync behavior. |
| Connector Sensitivity | 5/5 | Community connector with low usage (`ql` 100, `sl` 100). |
| Triggering Context | 4/5 | Triggered from a merged, clearly-scoped 1.0.0 release PR. |

### What I Verified vs. What I Inferred

- **Verified from code**: OAuth 2.0 password grant against `{base_url}/api/oauth2/token/` using `client_id`, `client_secret`, `username`, and `password`; incremental streams use the `updated` cursor with the `updatedsince` request parameter; the error handler retries up to 5 times using the `Retry-After` header; pagination follows `response.links.next`.
- **Verified from API docs**: The Client ID and Client Secret are generated via **Control Panel > Uptick API > Create Application**; the connector also requires an Uptick user account with permission to view the resources being synced ([Using AirByte with Uptick](https://support.uptickhq.com/en/articles/12032752-using-airbyte-with-uptick-connecting-to-the-api)); Uptick enforces rate limits / reasonable-use guidelines and exposes an `updatedsince` filter for sync ([Uptick API - Overview and patch notes](https://support.uptickhq.com/en/articles/6728314-uptick-api-overview-and-patch-notes)).
- **Inferred**: Nothing material beyond the above; specific numeric rate limits are not published by Uptick, so the docs describe the connector's `Retry-After` backoff behavior rather than a fixed quota.

### Areas of Concern

- Uptick does not publish quantitative rate limits, so the Rate limits section describes the connector's retry behavior and general guidance rather than exact thresholds.
- The connector's `metadata.yaml` `externalDocumentationUrls` points to `https://developer.uptick.com/`, which does not currently resolve. This is a metadata/connector concern, not a docs-page change, so it is left out of scope for this docs PR.

---

## What

Improves the `source-uptick` connector documentation (`docs/integrations/sources/uptick.md`) so a data engineer new to Uptick can configure the connector correctly and understand its sync behavior.

## How

- **Prerequisites (correction + addition)**: Clarified that the connector authenticates with OAuth 2.0 using the password grant, so it needs *both* an OAuth application (Client ID + Secret) *and* an Uptick user account (email + password) with permission to view the resources being synced. The previous list omitted the user account and its permission requirement. Linked directly to the Uptick "Getting started" article for generating credentials.
- **Incremental sync (addition)**: Added a short subsection explaining that incremental streams use each record's `updated` timestamp as the cursor via the Uptick API's `updatedsince` filter, and that full-refresh streams are re-read in full.
- **Rate limits (addition)**: Added a section noting Uptick's rate-limit / reasonable-use policy and that the connector honors the `Retry-After` header (up to five retries), with guidance to sync only needed streams/fields.

I did not modify `uptick-migrations.md`: it accurately and completely documents the 1.0.0 field removals, and the playbook forbids cosmetic-only migration-guide edits. The 1.0.0 changelog entry (date `2026-07-21`, PR `73740`) was validated and is correct.

## Review Guide

- `docs/integrations/sources/uptick.md` — Prerequisites (lines ~5-13), Incremental sync (lines ~153-155), Rate limits (lines ~157-159).

## User Impact

Users get accurate setup prerequisites (including the required user account and permissions) and a clearer understanding of incremental sync and rate-limit behavior. No connector runtime behavior changes.

## Phase 2 verification

The CI **Build Airbyte Docs**, **Docs / MarkDownLint**, **Docs / Vale**, and **Format Check** jobs all pass. A local `pnpm build` from `docusaurus/` could not complete because `pnpm install` failed on an unrelated `postman-code-generators` postinstall step (a Corepack/Yarn version mismatch in this environment), not because of these doc changes. The passing CI docs build confirms the change builds cleanly.

## Can this PR be safely reverted and rolled back?

- [x] YES 💚
- [ ] NO ❌

author: andi1180
body:
`platform.leads.contact_name` war seit B1-1 EIN Freitextfeld, geteilt über alle Einstiegspunkte. Für eine korrekte Anrede in künftiger Korrespondenz (u. a. Rechnungs-Wächter, Fahrplan B9) ist es durch `first_name`/`last_name` ersetzt — **an der Quelle getrennt, nicht später abgeleitet**: jede Zerlegung eines Freitextnamens ist eine Heuristik und scheitert bei Doppelnamen, Namenszusätzen und Titeln, und der Fehler landet dann in der Anrede einer echten E-Mail.

## Migration `20260724090000_split_contact_name.sql`

- Zwei Spalten + Backfill + `drop column contact_name` **in einem Schritt**. Der zweistufige Rollout entfällt begründet: der reale Bestand trägt keine echten Leads mit diesem Feld (die Testfälle sind bereits anonymisiert, und `anonymize_lead` nullt es seit B1-3). Zerlegungsregel: bis zum ERSTEN Leerzeichen → Vorname, Rest → Nachname; **ein Einzelwort wird zum NACHNAMEN** (als Vorname geführt fehlte es später in der Anrede).
- `capture_lead` und `admin_update_lead` per **DROP + CREATE** (Muster B3-1 — `create or replace` kann die Parameterliste nicht umbauen, ein blosses CREATE erzeugte eine mehrdeutige zweite Überladung). Die zwei Parameter stehen an **derselben Stelle** wie das frühere `p_contact_name`. Grants danach erneut gesetzt: `capture_lead` service_role-only, `admin_update_lead` authenticated-only.
- `guard_anonymized_lead` schützt **16 statt 15 Spalten** (beide Namensfelder EINZELN — ein Schutz nur auf den Nachnamen liesse den Vornamen frei änderbar); `platform.anonymize_lead` nullt beide.
- **`admin_list_leads`, `admin_export_leads` und `admin_get_lead` standen nicht in der Aufgabenstellung** und sind trotzdem Teil der Migration: sie lasen `ld.contact_name` und wären erst beim ERSTEN Aufruf gebrochen, nicht beim Anwenden der Migration (dieselbe plpgsql-Eigenschaft wie der B3-4-Befund).

## Zusammenführungssemantik

`first_name`/`last_name` sind **Identitätsfelder** und folgen `coalesce(Bestand, neu)` wie `company`/`phone` — **nicht** der B3-1-Segmentierungsregel. Beide werden **einzeln** zusammengeführt, mit Leerstring-Normalisierung (`nullif(btrim(…),'')`).

## Anwendung

Kontaktformular mit **zwei Pflichtfeldern** (einziger Einstiegspunkt mit dieser Anforderung — auf eine Kontaktanfrage folgt eine Antwort mit Anrede; `autocomplete` auf `given-name`/`family-name`), Registry, Erfassungsablauf, CSV-Export (**zwei Spalten statt einer** — der Grund für die Trennung gilt für die Datei genauso wie für die Anzeige), Admin-Korrekturformular (dort beide optional). Die interne Mail an energy@coolin.at führt beide in **einer** Zeile zusammen — reine Darstellung, der Bestand bleibt getrennt.

## Verifikation

- **DB-Gate 291/291** (274 bestehende + 17 neue in `lead-name-split.test.ts`). author: ahvega
body:
## Problem

`extract-text.py` could not run. `openai-whisper==20231117` is uninstallable on this project's Python 3.14 venv — its sdist `setup.py` imports `pkg_resources`, absent from the modern build env — so five of its six dependencies were missing and the script died at line 2:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotenv'
```

`py_compile` passed the whole time, which is why it went unnoticed. That gate only parses; it never resolves an import.

## The second failure, found while checking the torch pin

The pinned `torch 2.11.0+cu128` cannot run kernels on this project's GPU:

```
arch_list: ['sm_75', 'sm_80', 'sm_86', 'sm_90', 'sm_100', 'sm_120']
Quadro P5000 -> sm_61
torch.cuda.is_available() -> True     # silent: reports available, computes nothing
```

`transcribe_local.py` was never affected — CTranslate2 does its compute and torch serves only as a source of cuBLAS/cuDNN DLLs. But `extract-text.py` routed inference *through* torch, so even with its dependencies installed it would have failed on the GPU. Moving it to faster-whisper puts it on the engine that does support Pascal.

This also bounds the upgrade: the cu128 index tops out at 2.11.0+cu128 (already installed). PyPI's 2.13.0 is a different build — newer CUDA, still no sm_61, and it would swap the cuDNN majors ctranslate2 loads. **The torch pin stays.**

## Changes

**`extract-text.py`** — transcribe via faster-whisper/CTranslate2 (`int8` default per the sm_61 quirk); delete the simulated progress bars (they slept 5s after transcription and 1s after translation, reading 0% during the actual work) in favour of per-segment progress driven by the real decode generator; return non-zero on failure, where every error path previously exited 0; require `--url` instead of silently downloading a hardcoded default video; resolve the download path from yt-dlp's `requested_downloads` rather than assuming `temp/audio.wav`; chunk DeepL input under the 128 KiB request cap; drop the hardcoded free-tier endpoint so Pro keys work; drop the heading keyword list (`monetizar`, `patreon`, …) inherited from one specific test video, leaving punctuation-only detection; add `--model/--device/--compute/--language/--output/--target-lang/--no-translate`.

**`cuda_dlls.py`** (new) — extract the torch cuBLAS/cuDNN DLL lookup shared by both scripts.

**`transcribe_local.py`** — use the shared helper; normalise an empty language argument to auto-detect.

**`requirements.txt`** — pins to current: `yt-dlp` 2024.3.10 → 2026.7.4 (stale extractors break downloads first), `deepl` 1.30.0, `python-dotenv` 1.2.2, `ctranslate2` 4.8.1. Drops `openai-whisper`, plus `ffmpeg-python` and `numpy` (imported nowhere) and `tqdm` (used only by the deleted fake bars). `pip list` now matches the pins in both directions.

**Docs** — correct the claims this work falsified: `extract-text.py` was documented as "working, stable"; the README's install command failed, advertised a nonexistent transcript-reuse feature, and showed a `whisper.load_model(fp16=...)` call taking an argument that does not exist. Adds an import check to the verification gate.

## Verification

- `py_compile` on all three modules
- import resolution across `deepl,dotenv,yt_dlp,faster_whisper,ctranslate2,torch` — the gate that would have caught the original breakage
- GPU smoke test, exit 0 on the P5000, for **both** scripts (re-run after the `cuda_dlls` extraction)
- `extract-text.py`'s `load_model`/`transcribe` exercised on CUDA with no CPU fallback
- `chunk_text` boundary and no-boundary cases: limit respected, no text lost
- exit codes: `2` with no `--url`, `1` on a bad URL

**Unverified seam:** a live YouTube download of real media. Testing against a nonexistent video ID confirmed yt-dlp 2026.7.4 reaches YouTube's API and errors correctly, but no third-party content was pulled.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Switch YouTube transcription from openai-whisper/torch to faster-whisper/CTranslate2, repair CUDA/DLL handling, and bring the CLI, dependencies, and docs in line with the working GPU environment.

New Features:
- Add configurable model, device, compute type, language, output path, and target language options plus an option to skip translation in extract-text.py.
- Report live per-segment transcription progress and include the source URL in generated markdown transcripts.
- Introduce a shared cuda_dlls helper to locate and register torch-bundled CUDA/cuDNN DLLs for CTranslate2-based tools.

Bug Fixes:
- Make extract-text.py runnable again by replacing the uninstallable openai-whisper dependency and fixing its dependency imports.
- Ensure CUDA-based transcription works on the Quadro P5000 by routing all GPU compute through CTranslate2 instead of torch and preloading the correct DLLs.
- Return non-zero exit codes on download, transcription, or translation failures and require an explicit --url instead of silently using a hardcoded video.

Enhancements:
- Rewrite extract-text.py to use faster-whisper for transcription, with real-time progress, safer audio download handling, and more robust error handling.
- Improve markdown formatting and heading detection to rely on punctuation and numbering instead of hardcoded Spanish topic keywords.
- Chunk DeepL requests to respect API size limits and support both free and Pro endpoints without hardcoded URLs.
- Normalize empty language arguments in transcribe_local.py to trigger auto-detection and reuse the shared CUDA DLL loader.

Build:
- Update requirements.txt to align with the actual working environment, pinning faster-whisper, ctranslate2, yt-dlp, deepl, python-dotenv, and torch 2.11.0+cu128 from the cu128 index while dropping unused packages and openai-whisper.

Documentation:
- Update README, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md to describe the faster-whisper-based pipeline, CUDA/DLL behavior, required verification gates, CLI options, and the non-inference role of torch on this hardware.

author: conormccarter
body:
A `ContentAdmission` could be forged and could expire. `ContentAdmission::for_durable_content_write` was public and took arbitrary parts, so an embedder could mint an admission for bytes nobody wrote and the publisher would trust it. And the admission carried its own one-hour clock, so a sufficiently delayed queue could turn a prepared publication into a failure even though durable bytes do not stop being durable.

Admissions are now producer-only and clockless. The constructor is crate-private, and every admission originates from one of four events: an acknowledged LoonFS-managed content write (`prepare_stored_content`, which consumes the `StoredContent` returned by the write — `StoredContent` is now sealed against literal construction and deserialization), full durable validation (`prepare_existing_content_ref`, the one new public producer, used by `put_file_content_ref` and by tests that previously forged admissions), direct-put HEAD completion, and signed-token verification. Wire-token expiry is unchanged and checked exactly once at verification; the resulting in-process admission never expires, and the clock parameter is gone from the admission check end to end. Producers return the opaque `PreparedContent` pair; the candidate envelope that will carry it through the publisher is the next PR's work. The two expired-admission tests are deleted because the concept they pinned no longer exists; a new unit test pins that a verified token's admission outlives the token itself. No wire-visible changes.

One known edge deliberately left for the envelope PR: `StoredContent`'s fields stay public, so a caller holding a legitimate instance could still overwrite its `content_ref` before preparing it. Closing that fully means making `PreparedContent` the only currency through the seam, which is the next restructuring anyway.

author: sammy-maldonado
body:
## Linear

- Issue: [HOR-39 — US-019 Add mandatory pull request CI checks](https://linear.app/itd-sm/issue/HOR-39/us-019-add-mandatory-pull-request-ci-checks)

## Summary

Adds the first automated check in this repository: `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` run on
every Pull Request targeting `DEV`, `QA` or `main`.

HOR-38 established the promotion path and recorded an honest weakness — no CI existed, so
all five Pull Requests merged so far reported *"no checks reported"*. `docs/git-workflow.md`
§6 states the distinction this closes:

> "No checks reported" and "checks passed" are not the same statement, and recording them
> as if they were is how an unverified change reaches `main`.

This Pull Request is the first in the repository that can actually report a passing check.

## Scope

One file added: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

### Events

```yaml
pull_request:
  branches: [DEV, QA, main]
workflow_dispatch:
```

`push` is deliberately absent. The Git workflow forbids direct pushes to the permanent
branches, so every change reaches them through a Pull Request — `pull_request` alone covers
every entry point. Adding `push` would double every run for no additional coverage.

### Job

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Workflow name | `CI` |
| Job name (the check) | `Test / Build` |
| Runner | `ubuntu-latest` |
| Timeout | 15 minutes |
| Permissions | `contents: read` |

### Steps

```txt
actions/checkout@v4
pnpm/action-setup@v4
actions/setup-node@v4   node-version 24.15.0, cache: pnpm
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

### Two deliberate choices

**`pnpm/action-setup` carries no `version` input.** The action reads the pinned version from
the `packageManager` field in `package.json` (`pnpm@11.1.2`). Passing it twice creates two
places to update and a mismatch error the day they drift apart. One source of truth.

**`concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`.** A new push to the same Pull Request makes the
previous run obsolete; letting it finish burns minutes and can report a stale verdict
against the newer commit.

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

## Verification — the CI condition was reproduced locally

Running the gates on a working tree that has a `.env` proves nothing about a runner that has
none. The environment was reproduced rather than assumed: a clean clone of this branch into a
temporary directory, which by definition carries no `.env`, then install, test and build with
`DATABASE_URL` unset in the shell.

```bash
git clone --branch chore/HOR-39-github-actions-ci <repo> <tmp>
env -u DATABASE_URL pnpm install --frozen-lockfile   # postinstall: prisma generate && nuxt prepare
env -u DATABASE_URL pnpm test
env -u DATABASE_URL pnpm build
```

Result: **all three succeed with no environment variables whatsoever.**

`prisma generate` was the risk — it is a common CI failure that needs a dummy
`DATABASE_URL`. It does not here: `generate` reads `prisma/schema.prisma` and never resolves
the datasource URL. Verified, not assumed.

**Consequence: the workflow declares no `env:` block and needs no secrets, real or dummy.**

## Out of scope

- **Branch protection.** Requiring this check on `DEV`, `QA` and `main` is separate work and
  needs the real check name first — tracked in its own issue.
- **Release Please.** Independent task, deliberately not bundled.
- **`lint` and `typecheck`.** Those scripts do not exist in `package.json`. A CI step calling
  a script that does not exist fails; adding the scripts is separate work.
- **No MariaDB service.** The 26 tests are pure unit tests over server-side logic with no
  database access. A service container would add minutes and prove nothing.
- No application code, schema, dependency, or database change. HOR-37 not touched.

## Files changed

```txt
.github/workflows/ci.yml   +51   new file
```

No other file was modified. `prisma/schema.prisma`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`,
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.env*` and `data/private/` are all unchanged.

## Commands executed

```bash
git switch DEV && git pull --ff-only
git switch -c chore/HOR-39-github-actions-ci
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm build
git diff --check
git commit -m "ci: add pull request test and build workflow (HOR-39)"
```

## Tests

`pnpm test` — 2 files, **26 tests passed**, on the working tree and again in the clean clone.

## Build

`pnpm build` — `Build complete!` (10.4 MB / 2.88 MB gzip), both environments.

## Secrets

No secrets are referenced. No `.env*` file was opened. Nothing connects to a database or to
production.

## Risks

- The check is advisory until branch protection requires it. It reports, it does not yet
  block — a red run can still be merged past by hand.
- `ubuntu-latest` moves under us over time. That is the accepted trade for not pinning to an
  image that goes unsupported.

## Pending decisions

- Configuring GitHub branch protection to require `Test / Build` — needs Sammy's
  authorisation and is tracked separately.

author: val-grasley
body:
## What

Closes #814 (S0: the instantiation-laundering vein) by specifying and enforcing **W3 method-scheme fidelity** — the missing well-formedness rule of the dictionary translation — rather than the variance-aware type-pair walk the issue proposed. Two commits of substance, the second closing everything an adversarial review broke in the first.

**Spec** (`docs/spec/DICT-SEMANTICS.md` §3 W3 + §10; `docs/spec/EFFECTS-SEMANTICS.md` §6): an impl **or default** method body must inhabit the method's declared scheme at the instance head *at full generality* — the non-head quantified type and effect variables are the **caller's** (`var` re-instantiates them freshly per use), so the body may not pin them, identify them, or impose undeclared predicates on them. The variance-walk alternative is rejected *in the spec*, with the reason: flexible pinning is a **type**-soundness crash independent of effects (`mk d = 42` under `mk : a -> b` → caller at `b := String` crashes; likewise `pick : a -> b -> c -> b` returning the `c`), so no per-datatype variance machinery is needed. §6 also gains the **dual of Option A**: an effect var's argument-position occurrences must be covered by its non-argument occurrences (else the interface declaration is rejected — `T-EFFECT-ARG-UNCOVERED`), which must live at the declaration because the same-tail row-unification arm loses the atom.

**Typechecker** (post-unify survivor inspection = the `checkAnnotTooGeneral` C3 discipline; union-find monotonicity makes it observationally the skolem check):

- **type axis** (`T-IMPL-TOO-SPECIFIC`): scheme vars survive as distinct unbound TVars, disjoint from impl-head vars;
- **constraint axis**: obligations on scheme vars must be entailed by declared method-level constraints under `requires`-closure (`ifaceSelfAndSupers` — deliberately not `expandSupersPairs`, whose WS-1b gate is dict-slot policy and would miss `Monoid ⊨ Semigroup`), read from **both** obligation channels — method occurrences *and* constrained-helper call obligations;
- **effect axis** (`T-EFFECT-LAUNDER`): method effect vars gain no atom beyond declared per-occurrence coverage (IO-expanded) — catches off-arrow-spine pours the #803 walk can't see; quiet when #803's pre-unify walk already flagged the body;
- **generic default path** (`checkDefaultMethodRigidity`): the same rule where cross-module impls actually get checked (`fillImplDefaults` is same-module only) — all signature vars are survivors including interface typarams, whose obligations are entailed by the interface itself + requires-closure;
- **phantom-obligation fix at the source**: a lambda/pattern-bound local shadowing a method name resolves to a monomorphic scheme and no longer records a method obligation (`isMonoLocalScheme` guards at `inferMethodAt` + `inferVarPlain`) — previously the prelude `filter p t = …` default under a user interface with a method named `p` recorded a phantom `P elem` obligation.

**Deliberate carve-out (#817):** a method effect var unifying with an *instance-head row parameter* is admitted — Async v1's shipped `Mappable`/`Thenable` impls cannot be written otherwise (the sound result row `e ⊔ e'` is inexpressible with `f` fixed to `Async e`). ## What

Lets `snap_to_network` and `build_feed` route along a caller-chosen OSM network via a pyrosm Overpass-style tag filter, instead of only the fixed `network_type` — the resolved custom-filter follow-up:

- `snap_to_network(waypoints, pbf, custom_filter={"railway": ["tram"]})` restricts the routing network to exactly the matching ways (tram rails, heavy rail, or any tag selection); `filter_type` defaults to `"keep"`. `build_feed` forwards the same through a new `snap_custom_filter=` argument.
- Implementation note baked into the code and docstrings: a bare pyrosm `custom_filter` *unions* with the `network_type` base rather than restricting, so the restriction uses `network_type="all"` with a keep-filter (verified empirically — a cycleway filter yields a cycleway-only graph). When `custom_filter` is `None`, the plain `network_type` path is unchanged.

## Verification

Three new deterministic tests against the pinned Helsinki extract prove the mechanism: a road-type filter still routes the road-connected waypoints (LineString), a cycleway-only filter correctly leaves those road points unconnected (`no network path`), and a `railway=tram` filter reports an empty network — because this cropped sample contains no active `railway=tram`, only abandoned/platform/razed rail, so the tram-routing path is asserted through its empty-network error rather than a positive route (documented). A `build_feed(snap_custom_filter=...)` scenario builds a valid feed. Full suite: 139 passed, 1 skipped locally; docs build warning-free; black + flake8 clean. The OS/Python matrix runs in CI.

The editor's `/api/shapes/snap` and CLI passthrough of the filter is left for after this ships in a core release (the editor depends on a released core).

and `firmware/README.md:99` all still expect those paths, and a fresh clone had
no way to populate them: `git clone --recursive` and `git submodule update --init`

author: bbockelm
body:
Writing a batch was one request/ack round-trip **per ad** (`Tx.NewClassAd` in a loop), so a large batch became a multi-second flush purely from wire latency even when the DB applied each ad in microseconds — a 1000-ad batch is 1000 serial round-trips (the collector saw a 1032-ad flush take 2.5s while the DB reported single-digit-ms maxima).

## `opNewAdBatch`

Applies many ads to a transaction in a **single round-trip**, under **one transaction-lock acquisition** on the server. The reply lists the ads the server rejected (unparseable) **by index**, so a caller logs those and treats the rest as applied — mirroring `opNewAd`'s existing skip-the-bad-ad behavior so one bad ad never loses the batch. That per-chunk reply is effectively a **windowed ack**: it acknowledges the whole chunk and reports individual failures selectively.

## Two client entry points

- **`NewClassAdBatch`** — one chunk, one round-trip.
- **`NewClassAdBatchPipelined(items, chunkSize)`** — splits into `chunkSize`-ad chunks and sends **every chunk frame back-to-back without waiting for any ack**, then collects them. So chunks flow independently of the acks and the whole batch costs **~one round-trip** (not one per ad, nor one serialized round-trip per chunk), while each message stays small and the server does `~len/chunkSize` goroutine-dispatches/lock-acquisitions for the batch, not one per ad. A dropped connection or a reaped transaction (`no such transaction`) comes back as an error so the caller aborts and replays.

## Semantics preserved

Nothing durably commits until the final `opCommit` (which still does the conflict check). Per-ad skip-the-bad-ad and abort-and-replay both survive — the reject list just arrives per-window instead of per-ad.

## Tests

Mixed valid/rejected, empty, a 500-ad single batch, and a pipelined 400-ad/32-chunk batch that reports a bad ad at its **global** index. Green under `-race`; full `dbrpc` suite green.

The collector will call `NewClassAdBatchPipelined` with a modest chunk size (~32–64) in a follow-up, once this is tagged.

body:
## Summary

- adds `send_http_request_from_id`, `create_repeater_tab_from_id`, `send_to_intruder_from_id`, and `send_to_organizer_from_id`
- resolves project-scoped Proxy, Site Map, or Organizer references instead of asking the model to reconstruct raw HTTP
- applies bounded immutable patches for method, path, headers, typed parameters, and text/base64 bodies
- adds exact-request/diff approval for routing actions, including **Allow Once**, explicit global **Always Allow**, and **Deny**
- returns structured execution status, bounded response previews, and explicit `not_started` / `completed` / `uncertain` states

## Safety and behavior

- validates the current Burp project before source access and fails closed for stale or changed opaque Site Map IDs
- applies source-specific project-data approval before resolving a request
- keeps the original `HttpService`; a patch cannot silently redirect the destination host, port, or TLS mode
- caps source/result requests at 2 MiB, body replacements at 1 MiB, response previews at 64 KiB, and header/parameter mutations at 64 each
- rejects CR/LF header injection, invalid tokens, duplicate set-header/set-parameter keys, oversized fields, and ambiguous body/parameter combinations
- defaults replay to the source HTTP version, no redirects, and a 30-second response timeout (100 ms–120 s accepted)
- never retries an action whose Burp API delivery may be ambiguous; `executionState=uncertain` tells clients to reconcile manually
- preserves an unmodified Organizer response where Montoya supports it and never attaches a stale response after patching
- records completed replay responses in Site Map on a best-effort basis without changing an already-completed result
- emits redacted audit lines without request bodies or header values

Selecting **Always Allow** intentionally disables all later request-routing prompts and updates the MCP checkbox immediately. Re-enabling `Require approval for request routing actions` restores prompts. Cancellation before or during an approval cannot later persist an allow decision.

## Performance

- uses filtered Montoya lookup overloads for Proxy HTTP, Proxy WebSocket, and Organizer IDs instead of requesting full returned snapshots
- applies unified-search metadata filters before body sizing, notes, Site Map fingerprints, and serialization
- compiles method/status/MIME filters into sets once per query
- computes request size from `bodyOffset + body.length`, lazily renders exact request text only for interactive approval, and batches parameter mutations
- normalizes raw HTTP preludes in one pass and reuses HTTP/2 header maps and parsed auto-approval targets
- a Java 21 allocation probe reduced HTTP normalization allocation by 33.5% for a 1 MiB-body input and 52.5% for a 256 KiB prelude while preserving output

## Compatibility

Existing tools and valid calls retain their output and behavior. Nullable names on the legacy Repeater/Intruder tools are now genuinely optional and dispatch to Montoya's no-name overload when omitted. Community exposes 33 tools after this PR; Professional exposes 37.

## Validation

- [x] embedded-proxy end-to-end tests cover action schema/result relay
- [x] official initialize, ping, tools/list, DNS-rebinding, and concurrent-POST conformance scenarios pass with no failures or warnings

- [x] Burp Professional v2026.6 native runtime: all four actions completed from one Site Map stable ID, Repeater/Intruder/Organizer routing succeeded, Organizer preserved its response, and replay returned the exact patched POST body/header response
- [x] extracted stdio proxy negotiated `2025-11-25`, listed all 37 Professional tools, and completed a stable-ID Repeater action
- [x] replayed response was searchable in Site Map and the Organizer side effect was searchable with `hasResponse=true`

body:
## Problema
En el ejemplo reportado: capa 1 \$2.356/m2 + capa 2 \$11.655/m2 = \$14.011/m2 esperado, pero "Costo pintura" mostraba \$17.949/m2 — un 28% más caro de lo que corresponde, cobrado de más al cliente.

## Causa
`desgloseItem()` en `src/cotizador-data.js` usaba el costo de **compra** de pintura (envases completos, redondeado hacia arriba con sobrante) como el costo/m2 del item — en vez del costo **teórico** de pintura realmente consumida, que es lo que la propia etiqueta "Costo pintura ... mils promedio por rango" dice que debería mostrar, y lo que coincide con la suma de los valores \$/m2 de cada capa ya visibles en la misma tabla.

El sobrante de un envase (ej: 2,5 L o 5,0 L que quedan) se va a inventario para usarse en otro trabajo — no es un costo real de este item específico, así que no correspondía cargárselo al cliente.

## Fix
`costoM2` (y por lo tanto `Precio/m2` y `Total item`) ahora usa el costo teórico de pintura (litros realmente consumidos, mils promedio) — coincide con la suma de las capas mostradas en la tabla.

La sección "Compra de pintura (envases completos)" se mantiene sin cambios, como referencia operativa de cuánto comprar realmente esta vez — ya no afecta el precio cobrado.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` pasa sin errores
- [x] Verificado con los valores exactos del reporte: ahora "Costo pintura" da \$14.011/m2 (= \$2.356 + \$11.655, la suma de las capas), en vez de \$17.949/m2

author: jdx
body:
## Problem

The [release-plz workflow](https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/actions/runs/29794049055/job/88521647762) fails at `npm version 4.2.1 --no-git-tag-version` with `npm error Version not changed` (exit 1).

The chain of events in `scripts/release-plz.sh`:

1. `package.json` (4.2.1) matches the latest release (v4.2.1) → takes the "Nothing to release" branch, then checks for unreleased changes.
2. There are 6 commits since v4.2.1, but they're all `chore(deps)` Renovate commits.
3. `git cliff --bumped-version` returns **v4.2.1** (`WARN > There is nothing to bump`) because those commits don't trigger a semver bump.
4. The existing changelog guard doesn't catch this — `git cliff --bump --unreleased` still emits a non-empty block that isn't *exactly* `<!-- generated by git-cliff -->`.
5. The script proceeds to `npm version 4.2.1` (same version) → npm errors out.

## Fix

Bail out early when the git-cliff bumped version equals the latest tag / current package version, so the job succeeds with nothing to do instead of attempting a no-op version bump.

author: sunib
body:
Adds markdown linting to the repo, writes down the conventions it enforces, and gates it on a
short list of files rather than the whole tree.

## What runs

`task lint-docs` is now three checks, and `task lint` includes it:

| Task | Tool | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `lint-doc-links` | `hack/doccheck` | every reference resolves, including doc paths cited in Go comments |
| `lint-markdown` | markdownlint-cli2 | structure: fences, headings, lists, blank lines |
| `lint-prose` | Vale + a repo-local `HouseStyle` | em dashes, American spelling, product name, words to cut |

Both new tools are installed in the **`ci`** stage of the devcontainer, so CI and local runs are the
same check. Node moved from `dev` to `ci` with them, since markdownlint-cli2 is an npm package.

## Why the gate is narrow

Structure and prose gate only the files [`.docs-lint-scope`](.docs-lint-scope) lists, today
`README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/configuration.md`. Measured with the committed
config, 102 of 174 files fail markdownlint and 148 of 174 fail Vale, almost all of the latter on em
dashes. Fixing the tree would be one enormous commit colliding with everything in flight, so the
list starts at three files and grows as documents are cleaned. Those three are brought into
compliance here; `task lint-markdown DOCS_SCOPE=all` shows the rest of the backlog.

The scope is a committed list, not a git diff. The diff version needs a merge base, CI checks out
shallow, and an unreachable base made the file list *empty*, which is a green gate that checks
nothing. `hack/docs-files.sh` is the single place that resolves it and fails if the list is missing,
empty, or names an untracked path.

Reference checking is not staged this way: `lint-doc-links` still covers every tracked file.

## Also here

- **The e2e Gitea image now comes from Docker Hub.** `docker.gitea.com` became unreachable from CI
  and the devcontainer, and the pod stuck in `ImagePullBackOff` killed every leg in `BeforeSuite`.
  Same image, digest verified. Docker Hub anonymous rate limits are the trade; a pull-through cache
  is the follow-up.
- **This unblocks `main`.** #263 merged a `docs/INDEX.md` row linking to `style-guide.md` and
  `design/docs-linting.md`, which only exist here, so `doccheck` fails on `main` today and takes the
  Release workflow down with it.
- [`docs/style-guide.md`](docs/style-guide.md) records the conventions, and
  [`docs/design/docs-linting.md`](docs/design/docs-linting.md) carries the measurements behind every
  configuration choice. `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` describe the new gate.

author: gozala
body:
Bounds node size at **every** level of the tree, turning the leaf-size distribution from an uncontrolled tail (a 7.4 MB outlier leaf, a single unbounded index root) into a tight band around a ~64 KB target, while keeping every decision a pure function of the sorted key set so replicas stay convergent and edits stay local.

Stacked on #396. Ships byte-pacing on by default (`max_segment = 64K`, ceiling `3×`, hybrid anchors).

## The rules

Each is a pure function of the sorted key sequence — no decision reads where a previous boundary landed, so there is no dolt-style cascade and independent replicas build byte-identical trees.

- **Veto** — a seam whose distinguishing prefix exceeds `max_separator` is rejected at every level. Index bytes stay bounded at the moment of the cut, replacing the old demotion of long keys to rank 0.
- **Weight coin** — leaf cut probability is `entry_weight / max_segment`, pacing nodes by bytes rather than key count. `entry_weight` counts the serialized payload, so the target meters real encoded bytes.
- **Bank** — weight walked past on vetoed seams is charged to the next accepted seam, resetting at every accepted seam. Near-duplicate clusters split at their short-separator glue seams; measured from the key sequence, not from cut positions, so an edit changes at most one decision.
- **Frame ceiling** — a run between coin cuts over `ceiling × target` is force-split, clipping the coin's natural exponential tail.
- **Index-level pacing** — the same coin + ceiling apply to index nodes (weighted by separator + child-hash + overhead), so no node at any level grows unbounded. This is what lets the tree grow a second and third index level instead of one ever-growing root.
- **Edit-stable anchors** — forced cuts are placed by a left-anchored greedy sweep at the most stable semantic break (shortest-separator, hash-tail tiebreak). Windows that close before an edit keep byte-identical boundaries, so a reshape re-hashes only the nodes it actually changed — the property that keeps sync footprint proportional to real change.

## Space and shape — Stack Exchange history, 8192 commits, ~64 KB target

Real edit history (`retro-full.csv`, 117 236 facts / 50 553 transactions via `scripts/se-transform.py`), one commit per source edit.

| leaf distribution | demotion baseline | this PR (3× default) | this PR (2×) |
|---|---|---|---|
| largest leaf | **7.44 MB** | 226 KB | 189 KB |
| mean | skewed | 65 KB (1.02×) | 50 KB |
| p90 | — | 140 KB | 104 KB |
| p99 | — | 189 KB | 128 KB |
| bytes in 100K+ leaves | ~90% | 45% | 25% |
| index levels | 1 (unbounded root) | **3** | 3 |

The 7.4 MB→226 KB collapse is the headline: demotion built unbounded leaves from runs of near-duplicate keys, and the index never split. Byte-pacing plus the ceiling bound leaves near the target, and index-level pacing grows real index levels so per-commit work stops scaling with tree size. The distribution now tracks the exponential renewal shape (fraction over 2× target = 13.9% vs theoretical e⁻² = 13.5%); the residual max is that tail, not a mechanism gap. Tonk (no near-duplicate clusters) is byte-identical to the weight coin alone, confirming the extra rules are inert where they should be.

## Block reads/writes — the architecture-level metrics

Reads set query latency (each miss is a round trip on a partial replica); writes set disk amplification **and sync footprint** (each written block is one a peer must fetch). Both are deterministic per input, so they compare cleanly regardless of machine.

**Store writes per replay (SE, 8192 commits, mem backend)** — byte-identical re-stores are pure waste (encode+hash a block the store already holds):

| | 3× bisection | 3× this PR | 2× bisection | 2× this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| byte-identical re-stores | 296 | **237** (−20%) | 556 | **457** (−18%) |
| index nodes | 3 | 3 | 12 | **4** |
| index buffer flushes (novelty_ops) | 443 | 443 | 808 | **443** |

Edit-stable placement is what drops the re-store count: with stable boundaries the index-piece pass-through (untouched pieces stay persistent links, no re-encode/re-hash/store) actually fires. At 2× it also collapses index-node churn (12→4) and index buffering (808→443) — fewer boundaries move per edit, so fewer blocks change hash per commit. A separate baseline fix (bead dialog-db-59) stopped the enqueue cascade from lifting-and-re-storing untouched children, removing a class that was ~24–26% of sealed bytes.

**Query reads stay flat with history depth (SE `se.post/title` scan):** 2 → 4 block reads across depths 8 … 8192 while results grow 4 → 1362 (90×). Cardinality-one supersession keeps queried state size-independent of history; the read path never walks the history region.

**App workload reads (tonk bug tracker, real concept queries):** open issues 9–12, closed 6–8, assigned 3–4 block reads (run-to-run variation from random entity minting shifting boundaries). At parity with `main` (9–18 / 6–12 / 4–5 in #396) — full version control plus byte-pacing adds no read amplification to app joins.

## Commit throughput and the 3×-vs-2× default

SE 8192 replay total (mem, indicative wall clock): index pacing + the memo + the enqueue fix took the no-ceiling replay from 31.9 s to ~11 s; 3× runs ~15 s, 2× ~20 s. Main at this workload was ~35 s while minting no version control at all.

**3× is the default.** Edit-stable placement made 2× *viable* (its per-edit re-split cost is no longer pathological, and its re-store churn dropped), but 2× still force-splits far more frames, so it costs ~30% more commit wall clock for a tighter distribution. 2× is a documented option where node-size variance matters more than commit CPU; on a read/scan-dominated workload its tighter distribution could tip the balance, worth re-measuring before switching. Both are per-tree manifest fields, so the choice travels with the data and different trees can carry different values while each stays internally convergent.

## Correctness

All rules pinned by convergence tests (byte-identical trees across insertion orders and incremental-vs-rebuild oracles), edit-locality tests (an edit re-decides only the enclosing window), and the `max_segment = 0` identity guard (the pre-pacing tree is reproduced byte-for-byte). Shape-sensitive fixtures were made default-agnostic (they pin their own manifest) so retuning defaults later won't churn them. Full native suite: 2060 tests, green.

body:
## Summary
`ComfyUIWrapperService` (609 lines, 9 public methods, **0 tests**) sits underneath every ComfyUI feature — captioning, inpainting, upscale, outpaint. It constructed `new HttpClient` internally from a bare `string baseUrl`, opened raw WebSockets, and inlined the workflow-payload construction that encodes **undocumented, reverse-engineered contracts** with the `comfyui_queue_manager` and `ShowText|pysssss` plugins — shapes that would break silently the day those plugins change.

## Change (issue items 1–3; item 4 deferred as documented follow-up)
1. **`BuildPromptPayload` extracted as a pure function** — a line-for-line move of the inline builder (property names, insertion order, nesting, plugin-contract literals, `client_id` placement all identical — review verified zero drift). The undocumented plugin envelope is now pinned by a char-for-char `ToJsonString()` assertion: the current bytes ARE the spec, and any drift now fails a test instead of silently breaking four features.
2. **HttpClient/HttpMessageHandler ctor seam** — the legacy `string baseUrl` ctor delegates (call sites untouched; same BaseAddress + 10-min timeout) and ownership is explicit via `disposeHttpClient`: the service disposes only clients it created; injected clients survive (test-pinned). HTTP paths are now drivable by the repo's established `FakeHttpHandler` pattern.
3. **Pure WS/history parsing** — `ParseProgressMessage` maps the progress protocol 1:1 (review walked every branch: execution_error/executing/progress/status/unknown, identical ignore/complete/error rules and throw wording); `ParseHistoryOutputs` + text/image output extraction likewise pure and tested.

Item 4 (`IWebSocketFactory` + injected `ILogger`) deferred — documented in the report, nothing half-landed.

## Tests
38 new tests (service previously had 0): exact-envelope bytes, node-patching semantics, missing-node warning path, every WS message branch, history/result parsing, HttpClient disposal ownership. Full unit suite: **2998/2998**.
Task-reviewed (spec + quality, Opus): approved — all three drift risks (payload, WS parsing, HTTP ownership) verified clean branch-by-branch against the deleted code; the no-`[Obsolete]` judgment adjudicated correct (the legacy ctor is a live delegating overload, not a superseded duplicate).

## ⚠️ Before merge
