author: dhh1128
body:
## Summary

signify-ts has the CESR primitive classes (`Matter`, `Counter`, `Indexer`) and can
**emit** framed streams (`eventing.messagize`), but there is no parser that
**consumes** a stream — no equivalent of keripy's `keri.core.parsing.Parser`. This
PR adds one: `src/keri/core/parsing.ts`, a deterministic v1 CESR stream walker.

## What it does

- Frames a byte stream into messages + typed attachment groups, by the
  **version-string size** and the **attachment counters** — never by sniffing a
  leading `{`, so it works uniformly for JSON and (with an injected decoder) binary
  CBOR/MGPK bodies.
- **Delegates all sizing** to the existing `Counter` / `Matter` / `Indexer` classes
  (their `{ qb64 }` constructor + `.code`/`.count`/`.qb64`); it adds no code tables.
- Carries **byte-span provenance** (`{ start, end }`) on every node, so callers can
  map any decoded node back to the exact source bytes.
- Is **resilient**: on a code it cannot frame it stops and reports a typed error,
  returning everything parsed so far (`{ messages, errors, consumed }`) — a single
  bad byte never discards the prefix that did parse. `-V`/`-0V` material-quadlet
  wrappers are treated as resilience boundaries (their self-declared size lets the
  walk resume past undecodable inner content).
- **Pluggable body decoders**: JSON is built in; CBOR/MGPK etc. are decoded only
  when a decoder for that serialization is injected via `ParseOptions`. An undecoded
  body is still framed (`sad: null`).

Public API: `parse(bytes, opts?)`, `parseVersion(bytes, at)`, and the typed output
contract (`ParseResult`, `CesrMessage`, `AttachmentGroup`, `Primitive`,
`ParseError`, …). Wired into the barrel via one line in `src/exports.ts`.

## No new dependencies

**This PR adds zero dependencies — runtime or dev.** `package.json` and the lockfile
are untouched. `parsing.ts` imports only `./counter.ts`, `./indexer.ts`,
`./matter.ts` (modules signify-ts already ships) plus JS builtins (`TextDecoder`,
`JSON`). It reuses the primitive classes rather than adding anything.

## Excludable for consumers who don't want it

The module is **side-effect-free**: it does no work at import time (the shared
`TextDecoder` is created lazily on first use, not at module load). So a consumer
using **named imports** (`import { Matter } from 'signify-ts'`) with any
tree-shaking bundler drops `parsing.js` entirely when the parser is unused. If it
*is* included, the footprint is small — pure JS, no transitive deps.

Two caveats / optional follow-ups (maintainers' call — deliberately **not** in this PR):
- The barrel's `export default exp` (namespace) in `src/index.ts` defeats
  tree-shaking for anyone using the **default** import; named imports are unaffected.
- Adding `"sideEffects": false` to `package.json` and/or a subpath export
  (`signify-ts/parsing`) would make exclusion first-class, but those are repo-wide
  packaging decisions to validate separately.

## Testing

`test/core/parsing.test.ts` — 30 tests, inline keripy-derived vectors (matching the
existing house convention), covering: version parsing; `-A/-B/-C/-D/-E/-F/-G/-H/-I`
groups; `-V`/`-0V` nested decomposition and resilience boundaries; the Matter vs
Indexer primitive-class discriminator; and every error path (no-version-string,
malformed-body, unparseable-counter, unframable-group).

Gates: `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm run pretty:check`, and
`npx vitest run test/core/parsing.test.ts` all pass. (The 4 unrelated failures in
`test/app/*` require a running KERIA agent and are pre-existing on `main`.)

## Scope

**CESR v1 only.** signify-ts's counter/version-string machinery is v1 today (no v2
count-code table, no genus/version model beyond the opaque `--AAA` counter,
`Serials` is JSON-only, `deversify`/`VEREX` are locked to the 17-char v1 version
string), and this parser matches that. The v2 additions (v2 count codes,
genus/version, a v2 version-string parser) are a separate follow-up so this PR stays
a self-contained, reviewable unit.

author: zachtheyek
body:
Closes #151

Implements all six follow-ups deferred out of the #120 code review.

## Robustness

**(1) All 6 observation files validated up front in `_process_cadence`** (`preprocessing.py`). Previously only the primary ON file's rank and time-bin count were checked. Triage found the issue's cited failure mode had drifted: `_sliding_normality_k2` now derives its sample count from the rows it receives, so a short non-primary ON file no longer raises an `IndexError` — it silently degrades the k2 statistic, and the hard failure moved downstream to `_extract_stamps_worker`, where a short row count in ANY of the 6 files (ON *or* OFF — broader than the issue stated) raises a broadcast `ValueError` against the fixed `(n_stamps, 6, time_bins, stored_width)` memmap slot, swallowed as a whole-cadence skip mid-extraction. The new up-front loop checks rank-3 and `n_time >= time_bins` for every file, and skips the cadence with a warning naming the offending file(s) before any ED work or `.tmp.npy` creation. Comments/tests reflect the drifted reality.

The cadence is deliberately dropped whole rather than salvaging 5 observations: the `(n, 6, time_bins, width)` stamp tensor and the `num_observations=6` contract downstream (encoder reshape, RF features, ABACAD viz) have no representation for a 5-observation cadence — documented in the code comment.

**(2) Sequential per-cadence load on the streaming path** (`preprocessing.py`, `main.py`). `load_inference_data` grows `parallel: bool = True`; `_infer_cadence` passes `parallel=False`. The streaming path loads exactly one already-downsampled cadence `.npy` whose per-cadence work is a cheap vectorized log-norm, so forking a fresh `n_processes` chunk pool mid-loop — while the prefetch thread drives the persistent energy-detection pool — double-subscribed the CPU (~2x `n_processes` workers) for no gain. Docs (`PREPROCESSING.md`, `INFERENCE_PIPELINE.md`) updated to match.

## Code quality

**(3) Suggestion-block collision** (`cli.py`). `_build_suggestion_block` keyed proposals by `err.field`, so the two `inference.stamp_width` errors (equality with `width_bin`, divisibility by `downsample_factor`) silently overwrote each other's fix. Proposals are now keyed on `(field, fix_kind)` — one flag line per violation, honest even when a flag repeats with different candidate values.

**(4) Config-level coupling assertion** (`config.py`). `Config.__init__` now raises if `inference.stamp_width != data.width_bin`, surfacing a divergent source-level default edit at config-init time instead of deep inside `load_inference_data`. CLI overrides remain validated in `collect_validation_errors`.

## Test coverage

**(5) Latent padding-row truncation** (`tests/unit/test_inference.py`). A stubbed encoder/RF `InferencePipeline` (via `__new__`) pins `inference.py`'s `latents = latents[: n_samples * self.num_observations]`: the RF sees exactly `n_samples * num_observations` rows, `n_processed` reports the real snippet count, and row signatures prove the survivors are the real snippets in snippet-major order.

**(6) Multi-replica sharding geometry** (`tests/unit/test_inference.py`). `prepare_distributed_inf_dataset` is now exercised with `num_replicas` in (1, 2), covering `global_batch = per_replica x num_replicas > per_replica` — the production case the tail-drop fix targets. Docstring notes that true cross-replica distribution still needs the gpu-marked smoke.

Also shipped: tests for (1)–(4) (short/wrong-rank files at ON position 2 and OFF positions, no-`.tmp.npy` assertion, no-pool/no-SHM assertion for `parallel=False` with output pinned to the same log-norm oracle as the parallel-path tests, both stamp-width fixes surviving in the suggestion block, config guard raise), plus the `_StubPreprocessor` in `test_main.py` now asserts the streaming loop passes `parallel=False`.

## Verification

- `tests/unit/test_config.py` + `tests/unit/test_cli_validation.py`: 113 passed
- `tests/unit/test_inference.py`: 14 passed
- `tests/unit/test_preprocessing.py` + `tests/unit/test_main.py`: 126 passed

All run locally in the TF venv with `-m "not gpu and not cluster"`; full suite deferred to CI. `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean via pre-commit on all changed files. No `cli.py` flag/help changes, so no README CLI Reference regeneration needed.

## Maintainer decisions applied

- **Whole-cadence skip for a short file** (per the issue's "or" branch and the triage gameplan): did NOT implement "clamp/skip only the short file" — a 5-obs cadence has no downstream representation. Veto would mean redesigning the stamp-tensor contract.
- **Rank problems raise `ValueError` (logged skip via `process_pending_cadence`), short-time-bin problems warn + return `None`** — preserving the two pre-existing failure styles rather than unifying them.
- **Config guard placed at the end of `Config.__init__`** (the singleton isn't a dataclass, so no literal `__post_init__` exists). It catches divergent source-level defaults only; post-init CLI mutation stays covered by `collect_validation_errors`.
- **Duplicate `--stamp-width` lines in the suggestion block are allowed** (the gameplan's "honest" option) instead of post-filtering to a single all-constraints-satisfying proposal.
- Renamed the test helper `_rewrite_primary_rank` -> `_rewrite_rank` in `test_preprocessing.py` since it is now also used on a non-primary file.

author: euglopi
body:
**Net:** Legislator profiles have a "Legislative Service" section — which chambers a member was elected to, in which years, and their current term — that has been **hidden** because our database held none of that. This PR scrapes it from the official bios into a new table, exposes it on the API, and turns the section on for both the web and mobile profile screens. Closes #486.

## Two-level acceptance criteria

- [x] **Parser reads each member's bio → ordered election lines + current-chamber term.** — Net: pulls the "elected in X, re-elected Y…" facts straight from the government source, both chambers' formats.
- [x] **Stored as ordered rows so multi-chamber members are represented, term counted alone.** — Net: a senator who served in the House first shows both tenures; the term counts only the current chamber.
- [x] **API detail endpoint returns the full ordered history (not just `current_service`).** — Net: the app can read the whole timeline, not only today's seat.
- [x] **Frontend renders the multi-chamber model and stops fabricating history; section turns on (mobile + web).** — Net: the section appears, truthfully, on both layouts.
- [x] **Verified against a known multi-chamber member.** — Net: proven on Sen. Steve Green (House 2012→Senate 2022, Term 1st), the exact case it exists for.

## What changed
- **Parser** `alethical/pipeline/legislator_service.py`. Senate = dedicated "Legislative Service:" table (chamber-qualified "Elected:" rows + re-elections + one "Term:"); House = embedded in "Biographical Information:" (initial year only + authoritative "Term:", implicitly House). Lines with no "to the {chamber}" qualifier default to the member's current chamber. Fixtures are **verbatim real-source HTML** (guards the #328 fake-fixture failure mode).
- **Storage:** new `legislator_election_history` table (one row per chamber tenure, `period_sequence` ordered, `reelection_years` JSONB, `term_number` on the current-chamber row only). Chosen over `legislator_service_period` because its NOT-NULL session/chamber/district FKs can't represent prior-chamber tenures we never ingested. Migration `0005` is **create-table only**, verified upgrade→downgrade→upgrade on Postgres.
- **API:** additive `service_history` include on `GET /legislators/{id}` (schema + serializer + `selectinload`).
- **Frontend:** `mapLegislator` maps the real history into the design's `{label, elected}[]` + `term` model and **stops fabricating** the "2025–present" entry; both redesign screens render the card only when real data is present. Stale "not built — no data" comment on the web screen updated.
- **Backfill script:** dry-run by default; `--name-like`/`--limit` scope a live check; per-member commit isolates failures.

## Verification
- Backend suite green vs. real Postgres (75/75 on parser + API-contract; the one repo-wide failure is `test_rag_pipeline` hitting the live OpenAI embeddings API — a pre-existing network gate, unrelated). `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean.
- Frontend `tsc --noEmit` + `prettier --check .` clean. **Live QA** against a locally-seeded DB: web (desktop) rendered a multi-chamber member; mobile rendered a single-chamber member — both exactly matching the design copy, no console errors.
- **Full prod dry-run parsed all 200 current members** — 224 rows, 24 multi-chamber, **0 no-data / 0 fetch errors**. Green + Anderson match the issue's confirmed data exactly.

## ⚠️ Propose-first: do not merge until the prod rollout is approved
`.github/workflows/migrate.yml` auto-runs `alembic upgrade head` **against production** on any push to `main` touching `alembic/**` or `models.py` — so **merging this PR applies migration 0005 to prod**, and the task gates migrations as propose-first. The rollout after merge is:
1. Merge → migrate.yml creates the table in prod (additive; `git revert` + downgrade reverse it).
2. Scoped live check: `python -m alethical.pipeline.legislator_service --name-like Green --write` then `--name-like Anderson --write`, read back, confirm the timelines.
3. Full run: `python -m alethical.pipeline.legislator_service --write` (~200 members, free public bios, additive/idempotent).

Stale-reference check: web screen's "Legislative Service not built" comment updated in this PR; no other artifacts describe the old no-data state.

body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

**What changed:**

Add a typed `summary.table` service to Hollywood scripts, with explicit text and code cell constructors and escaped GitHub rendering.

**Why:**

Actions need readable step summaries without shell heredocs, raw HTML, or ambiguous string formatting. The typed cell boundary makes unsafe or malformed summary values unrepresentable through the public API.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Keep reviewed diffs small. If this adds more than 500 lines outside generated files or lockfiles, split it.

**Lines added, excluding generated files and lockfiles:** 287

## Test Plan

- [x] CLA/Vouch check passes, or this PR only updates `VOUCHED.td`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm test`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `npm run package`

Targeted verification: `npm test -- --run src/github.test.ts src/script-runtime.test.ts src/script.test.ts` (22 passed).

## Generated Output

Hollywood now generates a local `check-runtime` action and calls it from the existing trusted `Actionlint` job after building local actions:

```yaml
- name: Check Hollywood runtime
  uses: ./.github/actions/check-runtime
```

`npm run check` confirmed that the generated workflow, `action.yml`, and TypeScript entrypoint match their typed source. `dist/` was also regenerated.

## Repro / Showcase

```typescript
await summary.table("Integration test", [
  { label: "Environment", value: summaryCode("preview") },
  { label: "Result", value: summaryText("PASS") },
]);
```

The GitHub step summary renders a two-column table. Titles, labels, and values are HTML-escaped, and callers cannot pass raw HTML, Markdown, or bare string cells.

Hollywood dogfoods this path through its generated `check-runtime` action. A local execution produced:

```text
::group::node --version
v24.18.0
  ok       15ms  node --version
::endgroup::
```

and wrote the typed `Hollywood runtime` summary table with `Node` and `Result` rows. See the successful [CI / Actionlint dogfood job](https://github.com/dedalus-labs/hollywood/actions/runs/29868386087/job/88762183794).

## Release Impact

- [x] Runtime/library behavior changed
- [ ] CLI behavior changed
- [x] Generated YAML changed
- [x] Package contents changed
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] N/A

## Compatibility

Additive API; Node.js and package-manager requirements are unchanged. Local `runAction` calls receive a no-op summary service by default. A script that explicitly requests a GitHub summary fails clearly when the GitHub summary surface is unavailable.

## Reviewers

- Domain: @windsornguyen
- Readability: @windsornguyen

## Notes for Reviewers

The public API deliberately exposes only `summaryText` and `summaryCode`. Rendering is owned by the runtime adapter, and the GitHub adapter escapes every user-controlled field before emitting HTML. The dogfood action runs only in the existing same-repository trusted CI job, so external forks do not gain an executable PR path.

## Changelog

**[2026-07-21]**

Feedback received:

- (none yet)

Changes made:

- Added a generated runtime action that dogfoods typed exec and summaries in CI
- Added typed script summaries and GitHub table rendering
- Added escaping and unavailable-summary contract tests
- Documented the summary API with generic examples

body:
## Summary

Makes the DuckDuckGo search path resilient without paying for an indexing provider. The `html.duckduckgo.com/html/` endpoint rate-limits aggressively and blocks headless UAs, so `web_search`/`web_summarize` silently returned empty bodies the parser couldn't handle. (From the `codingagent-41ab7d7b` review.)

## Changes
- **Rotating User-Agent pool** (`_USER_AGENTS` + `_pick_user_agent`); `_USER_AGENT` kept as a back-compat alias.
- **`_ddg_search()`** tries (1) `html.duckduckgo.com/html/` → (2) `lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/` → (3) Playwright-rendered `duckduckgo.com`, returning the first non-empty result set — the browser only spins up on the hard cases, so the common path stays fast. Wired into both `web_search` and `web_summarize`, replacing the single-endpoint hard failure.
- **`_parse_ddg_lite_results()`** for the lite endpoint layout; **`_ddg_render_results()`** Playwright fallback (no-op when Playwright absent).
- **`_extract_content()`** prefers `trafilatura` (better boilerplate/ad stripping) with the existing BeautifulSoup heuristic as graceful fallback (`_NATIVE_AVAILABLE` pattern).
- **New `web` optional extra** in `pyproject.toml` (playwright + trafilatura); import sites stay lazy/guarded so the base install degrades to plain HTTP + BS4. README documents it.

## Tests
23 pre-existing + 12 new (`test_web_search_fallback_unit.py`) — **35 passed**.

Part of the same review that produced #610/#611/#612.

author: matt-ffffff
body:
## Summary

- The staging Function host indexed **zero** functions after a successful deploy, so every `/api/*` route returned 404 (health smoke test failed).
- Root cause: the Functions deploy package only shipped the **root** hoisted `node_modules`, but npm leaves some `@bccweb/api` **production** deps un-hoisted under `apps/api/node_modules` (`puppeteer-core`, `@puppeteer/browsers`). Flex zip-deploys `node_modules` as-is (`remoteBuild=false`), so the entry-point import chain (`index.ts` → `briefPdf.ts` → `pdf.ts` → `import puppeteer from "puppeteer-core"`) hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. With `FUNCTIONS_NODE_BLOCK_ON_ENTRY_POINT_ERROR=true`, a failed entry point blocks **all** function registration.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/deploy-app.yml`: after copying the root `node_modules`, overlay `apps/api/node_modules` into the deploy tree so the nested prod deps ship too.

## Verification

- Confirmed empirically: `puppeteer-core@25.3.0` is nested under `apps/api/node_modules` (NOT root); `@sparticuz/chromium` is hoisted to root.
- Reproduced the deploy assembly locally: root-only `node_modules` lacks `puppeteer-core`; after the overlay, `puppeteer-core` + `@puppeteer/browsers` are present and Node resolves `puppeteer-core` from the `pdf.js` path.
- Live diagnosis: `az functionapp function list` returned `[]`; App Insights showed `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'puppeteer-core' imported from .../dist/src/lib/pdf.js`; SWA `/api/*` forwarded to the backend with the Function's telemetry identity (routing was NOT the problem).
- The real end-to-end gate is the staging redeploy smoke test (`/api/health`, `/api/seasons`) which runs on merge to `main`.

body:
## Summary

The Slack bot currently forwards only message text. This PR makes images attached to Slack messages reach the agent as prompt attachments, using the session-attachments pipeline introduced in #1019 — the bot becomes a second producer alongside the web composer. No control-plane or sandbox-runtime changes.

**Flow**: Slack file (`url_private`, bot-token download) → multipart POST to the existing `/sessions/:id/attachments` store → `{attachmentId, name}` references on the prompt.

## What's covered

- **DMs** — including image-only messages: Slack delivers file uploads as the `file_share` subtype, possibly with no text, so DM dispatchability now accepts them and an image-only message gets a synthesized prompt body.
- **App mentions** — `app_mention` events don't carry the message's `files` array, so files are recovered with a single-message `conversations.history`/`replies` lookup (`latest` + `inclusive=true` + `limit=1`; setting `oldest=ts` too would create a zero-width window Slack returns empty).
- **Thread follow-ups** — images on replies are attached to the existing session's next prompt.
- **Clarification flow** — file metadata rides the pending request, so images survive the "which repo?" round-trip.

## Limits and failure behavior

Upstream's existing caps are enforced bot-side before upload (6 images per message, 10 MB per image, png/jpeg/webp/gif). Oversized files, failed downloads, and rejected uploads never block the message — they're logged and counted, and the bot posts a threaded warning telling the user how many images were dropped, pointing at the most common cause (missing `files:read` scope).

## Setup

Requires the `files:read` bot scope (added to GETTING_STARTED, app reinstall needed).

## Testing

- Unit tests for the new attachments module (download/upload/caps/drop accounting), `getMessageFiles` (both lookup shapes, error arm), `file_share` DM dispatch, and launcher reference passing.
- Four existing event tests were scoped to distinguish thread-history fetches (`limit=200`) from the new single-message file lookup (`limit=1`).
- End-to-end verification on a private deployment is in progress: DM with image, mention with image, thread reply with image, image-only DM, and the dropped-image warning path.

author: raifdmueller
body:
## Problem

Die `/go/{token}`-Seite, auf die die QR-Codes im eBook zeigen, sprang per JavaScript sofort zu YouTube:

```js
if(url)window.location.replace(url);
```

Daraus folgten zwei Probleme:

1. **QR-Scans wurden nicht gezählt.** Die Seite enthielt kein GoatCounter-Snippet, und der Besucher war weg, bevor überhaupt etwas hätte laden können. In der Statistik tauchten die Scans nicht auf.
2. **Das Video lief außerhalb des eigenen Kontexts** — direkt auf YouTube, ohne den zugehörigen Konzepttext.

## Lösung

`/go/{token}` führt jetzt auf `/concept/{id}`. Diese Seite existiert bereits, bettet das Video über `youtubeEmbed()` ein, zeigt den Konzepttext und trägt das GoatCounter-Snippet. Beide Probleme sind damit ohne neuen Seitentyp gelöst.

Zusätzlich: **statischer `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` statt JavaScript.** Die Weiterleitung funktioniert damit auch ohne JS, was vorher nicht der Fall war.

## Tests

`generateGoRedirect()` war bisher nicht getestet. Drei Tests ergänzt:

- leitet auf die Konzeptseite, nicht zu YouTube
- funktioniert ohne JavaScript (Meta-Refresh vorhanden)
- bietet bei blockiertem Refresh einen sichtbaren Link

Vorher 76 Tests, jetzt 79, alle grün.

## Zu prüfen

Ob GoatCounter QR-Traffic von organischem Traffic unterscheiden soll. Aktuell landen beide als normaler Aufruf von `/concept/{id}` in der Statistik. Falls die Unterscheidung gewünscht ist, wäre ein Query-Parameter (z. B. `?via=qr`) der nächste Schritt — bewusst nicht Teil dieses PRs.

author: git-on-my-level
body: ## Summary Fixes a critical data race on `RewindDatabase.currentUserId` (SCA-8). `currentUserId` was declared `nonisolated(unsafe) static var String?`. It was written from the `RewindDatabase` actor (`retargetEffectiveOwner`/`configure`) and read from `nonisolated static func markCleanShutdown()` — called synchronously from `OmiApp` during termination on the main thread — and from `AgentVMService` inside a `MainActor.run { … }` on a different executor. `String?` is a non-atomic, reference-counted type, so a concurrent write + read is a genuine data race that can crash via use-after-free on the string's heap storage (not a benign Bool flag). ## Change - Replace the stored `nonisolated(unsafe) static var currentUserId: String?` with a private `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` plus a computed `static var currentUserId` whose `get`/`set` funnel through the lock. - `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` is `Sendable` and its critical section is synchronous (no actor hop, no suspension), so reads/writes from any executor (the `RewindDatabase` actor, `MainActor`, and the `nonisolated` shutdown path) are atomic. - The call-site API is unchanged, so no production callers (`RewindDatabase.swift`, `RewindStorage.swift`, `AgentVMService.swift`, `OmiApp.swift`) or any tests need edits. - This matches the existing in-repo pattern (`RewindVideoDirectoryMutation`, `QueryTracer`) which already use `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` for cross-executor mutable state. ## Test New `RewindDatabaseCurrentUserIdConcurrencyTests`: - `testCurrentUserIdRoundTripsThroughLock` — get/set round-trip including `nil`. - `testConcurrentReadWriteIsRaceFree` — 8 writers (distinct IDs) × 4 readers, 5k iterations each, in a task group; asserts every read returns a coherent written value (one of the writer IDs or `nil`), never a torn/garbage pointer. Under the prior `nonisolated(unsafe)` storage this would surface as a torn value or a use-after-free trap; with the lock it completes cleanly. ## Verification - `xcrun swift build -c debug --package-path Desktop` — **Build complete**. - `xcrun swift test --package-path Desktop --filter RewindDatabaseCurrentUserIdConcurrencyTests` — 2 passed. - `xcrun swift test --package-path Desktop --filter RewindDatabaseLifecycleTests` — 4 passed (exercises `configure` + `currentUserId` set/read). - `xcrun swift test --package-path Desktop --filter RewindRetentionCleanupTests` — 1 passed (exercises `RewindStorage.initialize()` read path). - `xcrun swift test --package-path Desktop --filter ActionItemsFTSRepairTests` — 2 passed (exercises `ActionItemStorage` read path). - `swift-format-wrapper.sh lint` on both changed files — clean. Refs SCA-8. ## Product invariants affected - INV-AUTH-1 — the `currentUserId` lock-gating strengthens the effective-owner boundary (race-free per-owner `RewindDatabase` retargeting/configure described in INV-AUTH-1); no change to session invalidation, 401 handling, or owner-transition policy. Failure-Class: none

Replace verbose command echoing with compact grouped command reports, elapsed times, status labels, streamed child output, and an automatic GitHub step-summary table.

```text
artifact sync artifact://cache/.../dev/linux-arm64-aaaa...aaaa/ artifact://releases/.../runs/build-123/ --exclude images/source.img.zst --region ... +2 args

## What

Introduces authentication end to end — email + password with JWT (access + refresh),
verified on both HTTP requests and the WebSocket handshake — turning the anonymous
shared canvas into named users behind a sign-in gate.

Approach and phases are documented in client/docs/AUTH_PLAN.md.

## Changes (by phase)

Server
- users — in-memory user store, passwords hashed with bcrypt.
- auth — HS256 JWT (access 15 min + refresh 7 days); secret from JWT_SECRET (dev fallback).
- P1 — signup / login / refresh mutations + me query. Failures reported generically.
- P2 — HTTP middleware injects the user id into context; requireUser guard.
- P3 — WS InitFunc verifies the connectionParams token and rejects unauthenticated sockets.

Client (P4)
- AuthProvider (login/signup/logout + session restore from the refresh token).
- Token-aware Apollo links: Bearer header on HTTP, authToken in WS connectionParams.
- /login and /signup screens + a RequireAuth gate; access token in memory, refresh in localStorage.
- Cursor display name defaults to the signed-in account.

## Testing
- Server: go build / vet / test green; WS auth has a unit test + real-socket integration test.
- Client: tsc clean, 116/116 unit tests, production build clean.
- Manual (Playwright): guest→/login; signup→board; name from account; reload restores session; no console errors.

author: jdelic
body:
The ip-address: lines in the generated nsd.conf were hardcoded to the wildcard 0.0.0.0@53/::@53, with no way to bind to a specific address instead. That's a problem under network.mode = "host" deployments where another service already owns a more specific address (e.g. a link-local cluster-internal resolver) on port 53, since the wildcard bind can conflict with it.

Add NSD_LISTEN_ADDRESSES (comma-separated ip[@port] entries, default 0.0.0.0@53,::@53 to preserve current behavior), generating one ip-address: line per entry the same way NSD_SECONDARIES already does for notify/provide-xfr.

author: ho1yshif
body:
## Problem

`POST /api/analyze` intermittently returns **502 Bad gateway** (the UI shows a **"Try again"** button; clicking it usually works). That "try again works" is the tell: it's not a real error but a brief, self-healing upstream gap.

`gitnexus-server` is a single-instance private service with a persistent disk, so it **cannot do zero-downtime deploys**. Every restart/redeploy leaves a few-second window where the old instance is gone and the new one hasn't bound its port / propagated its internal DNS name. A proxied `/api/*` call landing in that window fails to connect, and `proxyToUpstream` returned 502 on the first error with **no retry** — exposing the transient gap to the user. (Confirmed via live logs: both `socket hang up` and `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` errors fired inside deploy windows; steady-state proxied `/api/heartbeat` returns 200.)

This is a connect failure, not a slow-request timeout — that path already returns 504.

## Fix

Make `proxyToUpstream` (`docker-server.mjs`) retry **connection-establishment failures** a few times with short backoff, *before* any response byte reaches the browser. Steady-state behavior is unchanged; only the restart gap is absorbed.

Correctness guarantees:

- **Only retries before the response has started** (`!res.headersSent`). Once the body is partially written it can't be replayed — keep today's behavior (destroy the socket).
- **Only retries connect-level codes** (`ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `ETIMEDOUT`). The upstream received nothing, so a re-attempt **cannot double-execute a job**. The idle-timeout path (504) is untouched.
- **Replays only small, known-length bodies**: `Content-Length` ≤ 256 KB is buffered up front (the tiny `POST /api/analyze` JSON always qualifies); GET/HEAD are trivially replayable. Larger/unknown-length bodies (the multipart `POST /api/analyze/upload` route) **stream once with no retry**, exactly as today — never buffer an upload.
- **Bounded**: 3 attempts, ~250ms→500ms backoff (< ~1s total). A genuinely-down upstream still fails fast with 502.

## Config

Two knobs, documented in `.env.example`:

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `GITNEXUS_PROXY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` | `3` | Retry budget; set `1` to disable |
| `GITNEXUS_PROXY_RETRY_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `262144` | Max body size buffered to make a request retryable |

## Tests

Adds 4 integration tests to `docker-server.test.mjs`:
1. Connection-refused POST → retries → succeeds once the upstream binds (asserts the upstream ran the job **exactly once** and the buffered body replayed intact).
2. Upstream stays down → returns 502 after the retry budget.
3. Upstream sends headers then drops mid-body → **no replay** (no duplicate job).
4. Body over the cap → streamed, not buffered, not retried.

Full suite: **28/28 passing**; prettier + eslint clean.

## Scope

`docker-server.mjs` (the web proxy) + its test + `.env.example` only. No change to `render.yaml` topology or the server's job/SSE model — single-instance-with-disk is correct for the server; the fix belongs in the proxy.

author: onnokh
body:
Two fixes for the Sleevy MCP integration, both in `apps/api`.

## 1. OAuth refresh tokens (`offline_access`)

The `sleevy_mcp` connection kept expiring with *"No refresh token is stored"*. Root cause: the `@better-auth/oauth-provider` was configured with `scopes: [...V1_SCOPES]`, which **replaces** the plugin's default scope list (it's an authoritative allowlist, not a merge) and silently dropped the standard `offline_access` scope.

The token endpoint only issues a refresh token when `offline_access` is among the granted scopes, so DCR/MCP clients got an access token but **no refresh token** — connections expired after the access-token TTL with nothing to refresh against. (Linear/Notion kept `offline_access` in their allowlists, which is why only Sleevy was affected.)

**Fix:** keep `V1_SCOPES` as the domain-scope source of truth, and union in a separate `OAUTH_PROTOCOL_SCOPES` (`offline_access`) at the provider boundary. The provider now advertises it in `scopes_supported` and issues refresh tokens.

> ⚠️ After deploy, existing connections need a **one-time reauth** to obtain a refresh token — this can't be applied retroactively.

## 2. Spec-compliant MCP Server Card (SEP-2127)

The server card was served at a non-standard path (`/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`) with a non-standard body (a bespoke `authentication` field, missing all four required fields).

**Fix:** serve it at the ratified `/.well-known/mcp-server-card` path with the SEP-2127 shape (`$schema`, `name`, `version`, `description`, `remotes[]`), keeping the old path as a legacy alias. OAuth is intentionally *not* described in the card — clients discover it via `oauth-protected-resource`. `supportedProtocolVersions` is sourced from the MCP SDK so it stays truthful across upgrades. Adds the required CORS + caching headers.

## Testing

- `bun test test/server/http-app.test.ts test/runtime/mcp-app.test.ts test/runtime/better-auth-schema.test.ts` — 25 pass
- `tsc --noEmit` clean

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

integrations.sh only probes the **apex** `sleevy.app`, while these well-known routes are served on `api.sleevy.app`. Making its checklist go green would require also serving the card from the web app's apex — deferred pending a decision.

author: dcccrypto
body:
Closes #373.

## The bug

The v17 pre-submit re-verification wrapped its **entire** block — the still-undercollateralized margin recheck, the maintenance-margin re-parse, and the oracle-drift guard — in `try { … } catch { /* proceed cautiously */ }` with an empty catch. Any throw fell straight through to the send with **no checks applied**.

The v12.x path directly below is unwrapped and already fails closed. v17 is the live mainnet layout, so the asymmetry ran the wrong way.

The "proceed cautiously — the on-chain program will reject" justification covers the closed/topped-up case. It does **not** cover the drift guard, which the code itself documents as having no on-chain counterpart:

> The on-chain Liquidate instruction carries no price bound, so keeper-side drift detection is the only available mitigation.

So on a throw, a liquidation could be submitted at unbounded drift with no backstop anywhere — keeper-side skipped, on-chain nonexistent. Triggers aren't attacker-controlled (malformed wrapper bytes in `parseWrapperConfigV17`, a cluster-time RPC error, the M-6 owner-check failure in `fetchSlabWithRetry`) but they're reachable.

## The fix

Narrow the `try` to the fetch/parse of re-verification data and `return null` on failure. The drift and margin checks now run **outside** it, so their failure aborts the submit. Matches the H-8 pattern already applied to the inner `reMmBps` parse.

**Trade-off, stated plainly:** during RPC instability the keeper now *skips* these liquidations instead of submitting them blind. That's the intended posture and the one v12.x already had — the next scan cycle retries. It trades some liquidation coverage under RPC flakiness for never submitting an unverified liquidation.

## Verification

The issue asked for a test where `parseWrapperConfigV17` throws and `keeperSend` is never called. Added that, plus the slab-re-fetch throw, plus two contrast tests proving the checks still *run* on the healthy path (otherwise "fail closed" could be implemented as "always return null" and the first two would still pass).

I verified these against the **original code**, not a hand-rolled mutation — my first mutation attempt produced a broken hybrid that passed and would have let a useless test through:

```
ORIGINAL fail-open liquidation.ts + new tests  → 2 failed   ✅ they catch the bug
fixed liquidation.ts + new tests               → 4 passed
```

## Second finding: the existing drift test was vacuous

While building the contrast case I found the pre-existing test — `aborts v17 liquidation when fresh wrapper price drifts beyond the configured limit` — **passes with the drift guard entirely commented out.**

Its wrapper config had `oracleTargetPublishTime: 0n`, so `resolveV17WrapperPrice` treated the EWMA as stale and returned `0n`. The test aborted on the `freshPrice === 0n` guard and never reached the drift check.

So the mitigation this whole issue exists to protect had **no working test coverage**. Fixed by giving it a fresh publish time; the 100% drift (1.0 → 2.0 against a 150bps limit) is now what actually aborts. Mutation-verified: disabling the guard fails it.

## Checks

- Full keeper suite: **979 passed, 0 failures**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean

Touches liquidation safety logic on the live mainnet path — **wants a security review before merge**, not just a functional one.

body:
## Three bugs fixed

### 1. Worker search and sort not working
`workerKeys.list` only included `status` in the query key — `search`, `sortBy`, and `sortOrder` were missing. When the user typed in the search box or changed sort controls, React Query returned the stale cached result because the query key hadn't changed. The API call was never re-executed with the new filter values.

**Fix**: Changed `workerKeys.list` to accept an options object with all four filter params so the cache key changes when any filter changes.

### 2. Work items TreeView ignores sortBy/sortOrder
The `TreeView` component received `sortBy` and `sortOrder` as props (lines 252-253) but never passed them to `useListWorkItems` (line 258). The tree always returned items in default order. The `KanbanBoard` component was already correct — it passed sort params through. `TreeView` was the outlier.

**Fix**: Pass `sortBy` and `sortOrder` to the API call in `TreeView`.

### 3. Batch delete swallows errors
Both `useBatchDeleteWorkers` and `useBatchDeleteWorkItems` used `Promise.allSettled`. When any individual delete call failed (RLS, permissions, network), the promise resolved successfully and the `onSuccess` callback fired, making the UI claim items were deleted when they were not.

**Fix**: Changed to `Promise.all` so a single failure rejects the entire batch and the mutation's `onError` handler fires.

author: kossoy
body:
Refs #1019

Greptile Summary

This PR adds bounded recovery escalation for repeated outcome failures. The main changes are: - Caps automatic recovery after a configurable number of unchanged failures. - Files and deduplicates a repair issue for the capped failure. - Sends a futile-recovery notification after issue creation. - Allows repair issues through the red-outcome ready hold. - Disables generic gate-streak escalation when automatic recovery owns the flow.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The repair classification and issue publication paths need fixes before merging. An arbitrary issue-body substring can bypass the red-outcome hold. Command health details can expose secret formats that the redactor does not recognize. The core recovery cap, deduplication, and notification state flow is otherwise coherent. internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go; internal/supervisor/outcome_repair.go

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Reproduced verification that a body marker bypasses the red hold by running a focused Go test through the real orchestrator startNewWorkers flow with failing outcome health, capped recovery, and a red-outcome supervisor hold, showing the marker-bearing issue starting a worker while the unmarked control was held. - Confirmed that an ordinary maestro-ready issue labeled only by its body marker was classified as repair work solely because its body quoted the marker prefix. - Validated the dispatch path could leak secrets by running the real dispatchFutileOutcomeRecovery path with a capped healthcheck\_command and a synthetic bearerless JWT, where the fake GitHub client received exactly one issue creation request containing the unredacted JWT. - Observed that the reproduction printed FIXTURE\_PRESENT\_IN\_PUBLISHED\_BODY=true and produced the exact generated issue payload. - End-to-end supervisor and orchestrator tests ran to completion with no race issues reported, after which the pre-change baseline showed compilation failure due to the missing feature API/state. author: monlamltd-collab
body:
## Root cause

`bagshaws` had **no recogniser** and depended entirely on the AI extractor.

- Last good AI pass (**11 Jul 2026**) recovered **22 of 23** lots and dropped the SOLD-PRIOR one.
- Every pass since produced a single junk row (`lot 275`, `url = https://www.bagshawsauctions.co.uk/` — the catalogue root).
- With nothing re-confirming them, the 22 real lots aged past the **7-day freshness window** in `get_active_lots` → the house went dark (82 rows stored, ~0 live).

Two secondary defects rode along: every lot was stamped `auction_date = 2099-12-31` (inherited from the house's only `auction_calendar` row, an `always_on` placeholder), and the SOLD-PRIOR lot was invisible entirely.

The catalogue itself is trivially scrapeable: a **hand-maintained static HTML page** (table layout, no CMS, no JS, no anti-bot, HTTP 200 from a plain fetch). Its lot cards link out to the Sequence/Connells group's shared national sale on `barnardmarcusauctions.co.uk/auctions/{DD-month-YYYY}/{id}/` — which is exactly what the pre-existing `RECALL_SENTINELS.bagshaws` already matched.

## The fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/pipeline/firecrawl-extract.js` | `recogniseBagshawsLotsFromMarkdown()` — deterministic parse, keyed by the Sequence lot id (the sentinel's capture group, so the Crawlee recovery/corroboration path can match it) |
| `lib/scraper/house-recognisers.js` | registered `staticCatalogue: true, maxPages: 1` with the existing sentinel → plain HTTP → turndown → recogniser. **No browser, no AI.** |
| `lib/houses.js` | `rewriteUrl()` pins *any* `bagshawsauctions.co.uk` URL to the root, so a stale calendar row or a healed `Auction-Results.html` (which lists **past** sales) can never become the scrape target |
| `tests/test-bagshaws-recogniser.js` | new hermetic test, wired into `npm test` |
| `docs/houses/bagshaws.md` + README/CLAUDE.md | per-house dossier + doc-drift updates |

Three contracts the parse enforces:

1. **Anti-leak.** A `**Sold Prior**` lot emits `lot_status='sold'` and never persists as available. (Lot 274, cross-confirmed `sold` on its Barnard Marcus lot page.)
2. **Real auction date.** Parsed from the lot-URL date slug (`28-july-2026` → `2026-07-28`) and stamped per lot. `lot._auctionDate` outranks the calendar in `persist-lots.js`, so this replaces the `2099-12-31` placeholder — which is what makes the house *expire* correctly after the hammer instead of showing ended lots forever. A **past** slug is reported verbatim (no roll-forward — the Maggs 2026-05-12 trap), so `get_active_lots` simply drops those lots.
3. **Broken anchor recovery.** One lot's text link is `href="link"` — a hand-editing typo on the live page. Its thumbnail link is intact and the image basename **is** the lot number (`257.jpg` → Lot 257), so URL + photo come from there rather than dropping the lot. Verified: the recovered id `707825` really is *66 Wythburn Road, Chesterfield*.

## Live parity (verified against the live site 2026-07-21, not a fixture)

```
rewriteUrl → https://www.bagshawsauctions.co.uk/
sentinel ids: 23 | recognised: 23
survived normaliseScrapedLot: 23 / 23
status: { available: 22, sold: 1 }
future-dated: 23 | past/missing: 0
with price: 22 | with image: 23 | with url: 23
distinct images: 23 | distinct urls: 23 | distinct addrs: 23
leak check → only non-available lot: 274 sold  (274, Uttoxeter New Road, DERBY, DE22 3LL)
```

- **23 / 23 = 100% recall**, measured *after* `normaliseScrapedLot` (not regex hits).
- **Ended leak: none.** The single sold lot is the only non-available one, and it is the only lot without a guide price — no price bled from a neighbour.
- **Real data, not placeholders.** Addresses carry UK postcodes; the 22 guides are real (`£35,000`–`£700,000`); all 23 photos are distinct per-lot JPEGs on the house's own server (spot-checked `274.jpg` → HTTP 200, 10,254 bytes; `261.jpg` → 200, 9,418 bytes) — no hero bleed, and the page logo / award / Sequence footer images never bind to a lot.
- All 23 lots dated `2026-07-28` (a future sale), matching the page banner *"Our Next Major Auction will be Held on Tuesday 28th July"* and the lot pages' own *"Auction: 28th July 2026"*.

## DB / calendar changes still needed

**None required to ship.** Two optional hygiene items:

1. **Junk rows expire on their own.** Three pre-existing rows will stop being re-seen and age out of the 7-day window: `url='https://www.bagshawsauctions.co.uk/'` (lot 275 dup, the AI's last output), `url='https://www.bagshawsauctions.co.uk/link'` (lot 257 under the broken href), and `url='/'` (lot 1, "32-34 The Cornmarket", last seen 2026-06-03). Delete them only if the clutter matters — no code depends on it.
2. **Calendar row.** `auction_calendar` for `bagshaws` is a single `2099-12-31 always_on` placeholder pointing at `https://bagshawsauctions.co.uk`. Harmless now that the recogniser stamps the real date; the honest fix is a dated row per sale.

## Test evidence

- `node tests/test-bagshaws-recogniser.js` → **26 passed, 0 failed**. Covers: keyed by lot id; sold-prior never available; no price bleed onto the sold lot; broken-anchor URL + photo recovery via the thumbnail; auction date from the URL slug; a **past** slug kept past (no roll-forward); multi-line address joins with no double commas; distinct photos / no hero bleed; logo & spacer never bind to a lot; survival through `normaliseScrapedLot`; empty/null/lot-less input → empty map.
- `npm test` → **exit 0** (full suite, including `test-sentinel-coverage.js`).

## Not in scope

`foxandsons` and `williamhbrownnorwich` run the *same* hand-built Sequence template and contribute adjacent lot ranges to the same national sale (138–159 and 234–252 vs Bagshaws' 253–275). `foxandsons` is currently healthy on the AI path; `williamhbrownnorwich` is stale (last seen 2026-07-11) and is a strong candidate for the same recogniser — but as a separate, separately-verified change.

author: artokun
body:
**main's CI has been red since #262** on `interrupt kills the in-flight child tree` — *Test timed out in 5000ms*.

It isn't a flaky test. It's a real race the test caught, with a user-visible symptom: **press Stop right after Send and the turn never ends.**

## Three defects, each of which alone loses the interrupt

**1. `interrupt()` dropped the request during the spawn window**

```js
const child = this.child;
if (!child) return;        // ← returns BEFORE setting the flag
this.interrupted = true;
```

`this.child` is only assigned *after* `spawn()` returns, so a Stop landing in that window set nothing and killed nothing. The flag is now raised **first and unconditionally** — it's the durable signal; the kill is best-effort.

**2. The per-turn reset ran at turn START**

`run()` awaits `prepare()` and the channel before reaching `runTurn`, so a Stop arriving during that setup was cleared moments later by `this.interrupted = false`. It's now cleared when a turn **settles** (after being consumed to pick the result), so it survives startup and the next turn still begins clean.

**3. The catch-up kill fired before anything was listening**

Acting on a pending interrupt at child-assignment time killed the child **before** the `exit`/`error` listeners were attached — the death was delivered to nobody and the turn never settled. The kill now runs immediately *after* those listeners are wired.

(3) is the one that kept the new regression test hanging even after (1) and (2) were fixed. Killing something before you can observe it dying is its own bug, and it would bite in production too — not just against a synchronous test fake.

## Regression test

Interrupts **without** waiting for the spawn, so it deterministically lands in the startup window:

- fails against the previous code (hangs to the 5s timeout)
- passes now, verified **green 5 runs in a row**

## Verification

`tsc` clean; **142 files / 1636 tests green**.

Found while getting CI green for #265 (LTX Director skill) — that PR is docs-only and was failing on this pre-existing breakage, not on its own content.

author: ggekos
body:
Trims the residual per-request object reads from the cost epic (#108). From `main`.

## Changes

**1. Memoize the produce compacted-policy check.** `produce` read the topic config (`describe_config` → conditional GET of `topic-metadata/<name>.json`) on **every batch**, only to decide the coalesce route (is `cleanup.policy` compact?). Now `topic_is_compacted` memoizes it per topic (TTL = `HIGH_WATERMARK_HINT_TTL`). The policy changes only on a rare `AlterConfigs`, so a steady-state produce reads it from memory; a change is still observed within the window. Leaves the shared `topic_meta` fresh-read invariant untouched (a dedicated memo, not a cache on `topic_metadata`).

**2. Skip the LATEST tail-timestamp `records/` LIST on pure-segment topics.** `list_offsets` LATEST fell back to a `records/` LIST for the tail timestamp when the footer index had none. A pure-segment coalesced topic has no legacy `records/` objects, so that LIST scans an empty prefix and returns nothing — skip it (gated on the now-cheap `has_legacy_records` memo, #110) and report no timestamp, **equivalent** to the empty listing but without the tier-1 LIST on the continuous consumer-lag path. Hybrid / non-coalesced topics still list for the legacy tail mtime.

## Deliberately excluded: the seq-floor GET

The ticket also proposed caching the per-flush `read_seq_floor` GET. **Not done** — the seq floor is the monotonic lower bound that prevents segment-sequence-name **reuse after retention** (#77); a stale (lower) cached floor could derive a freed-and-reused name → corruption. It stays a fresh read. Its cost is ~1 tier-2 GET/flush — negligible next to that risk.

## Tests

- `topic_is_compacted_is_memoized` — 20 repeated checks issue **zero** object-store requests after the first.
- `latest_list_offsets_on_pure_segment_issues_no_records_list` — 20 repeated LATEST polls issue **zero** `records/` LISTs.
- **187/187** storage tests pass (existing LATEST/Timestamp regression tests cover the changed branch); `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` + `fmt --check` clean.

Part of #108. Closes #113.

backend and one MongoDB, so this single responsive Next.js console administers the whole
platform. Rebuilt in place — same stack (Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, Mongoose,
shared JWT), matching VokiToki's design tokens — re-architected into clean, reusable,
permission-gated, fully audited components, with several new capability areas.

**Foundation**
- Resynced Mongoose models with the Go source-of-truth; added `AuditLog`, `Announcement`,
  `AdminSetting`, `BotChat` models.
- `lib/permissions.ts` — two-tier role → permission matrix (single source of truth).
- `lib/withAdmin.ts` — one wrapper for every admin route: auth + permission + rate-limit +
  audit + error handling.

- **Dashboard** — KPI overview + 7-day activity charts.
- **Analytics** *(new)* — growth, DAU/MAU, message volume, media breakdown, top users.
- **Users** — search/filter/sort; ban, timeout, deactivate, promote, hard-delete

- **Chats & Groups** *(new)* — detail drawer, member removal, conversation deletion.

  An existing `admin` with no explicit tier is treated as Super Admin (backward compatible).

author: drdonik
body:
## Problem

Als Homescreen-PWA auf dem iPhone fragte die App bei **jedem** Start nach der Standort-Berechtigung. Ursache ist eine iOS-Einschränkung: Homescreen-Web-Apps laufen in einem isolierten WebKit-Kontext und speichern die Geolocation-Berechtigung **nicht** dauerhaft – es gibt keine Web-API oder iOS-Einstellung, um sie permanent zu erteilen. Ausgelöst wurde der Dialog konkret durch den `getCurrentPosition()`-Aufruf bei jedem Start.

## Lösung

Der Live-Standort wird im Alltag gar nicht gebraucht (fester Pendel-Ort). Die Standort-Zeile im Header wird deshalb selbst zum **antippbaren Umschalter** – ohne zusätzliches UI-Element:

- **Zu Hause** (Standard): feste Basler Koordinaten, **nie ein Standort-Dialog**, sofort Wetterdaten.
- **Auf Reisen**: ortet **live** beim Umschalten (hier ist der iOS-Dialog gewollt), cacht das Ergebnis und ortet beim blossen Öffnen/Zurückkehren **nicht** neu.

Der gewählte Modus wird in `localStorage` gespeichert und bleibt über App-Neustarts erhalten.

### Prompt-Bilanz
- **Zu Hause:** null Dialoge, egal wie oft die App geöffnet wird.
- **Auf Reisen:** ein Dialog nur beim bewussten Umschalten.

## Änderungen (`index.html`)

- `getPosition()`/`FALLBACK` ersetzt durch `HOME` (feste Koordinaten), `getTravelPos()` (Live-Ortung) und `resolvePosition(forceLocate)` (Modus-Logik mit Cache).
- Neuer Modus-Zustand `locMode` (persistiert) und `toggleLocMode()`.
- `#loc`-Zeile rendert den Modus als antippbaren Button (dezente gepunktete Unterstreichung); Klick-Handler einmalig gebunden.
- `loadData(forceLocate)` reicht den Ortungs-Wunsch durch.

author: claire-mn
body:
## Summary

Pins the external hook in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to the commit SHA its tag currently resolves to, with the tag kept as a `# frozen:` comment (same convention as `pre-commit autoupdate --freeze`). Behavior is unchanged.

- pre-commit-hooks: `v3.1.0` → `ebc15addedad713c86ef18ae9632c88e187dd0af`

## Why

A tag is a mutable pointer — if a hook's upstream repo is ever compromised (stolen maintainer credentials, hijacked token), the attacker can retarget an existing tag to malicious code and every consumer pinned to that tag picks it up on the next run, with no diff on our side. This happened to `tj-actions/changed-files` in March 2025: 350+ tags were retargeted to a secret-dumping commit, hitting ~23k repos ([writeup](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/)). A commit SHA can't be retargeted, so pinning to it closes that vector. Same practice as OpenSSF Scorecard's [Pinned-Dependencies check](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies) and GitHub's own guidance for Actions — applies equally here since `rev:` is fetched the same way.

Checked GitHub's security-advisories API and the GitHub Advisory Database for pre-commit-hooks first — no known CVEs or compromises, so this is proactive rather than a response to an incident.

## Verification

- `pre-commit validate-config .pre-commit-config.yaml` passes
- YAML still parses cleanly
- Diff touches only the one `rev:` line

Companion to teamsnap/claude-plugins#298, part of a fan-out pinning pre-commit hook revs across TeamSnap repos.

body:
## Incident
Production's Neon database was missing `manual_macro_entries` and `daily_targets` entirely — `/log-meal` and `/daily` have been erroring in production (`relation "daily_targets" does not exist`) since the Log Meal slice shipped, because this repo never had a path that applies migrations to production. `npm run migrate` only ever targeted `.env.local` (the dev branch, used by local dev and Preview deployments); `migrate:ci` only migrates the disposable per-run branch CI creates for integration tests. A migration file landing on `main` was never the same thing as it reaching production.

## Hotfix (already applied, verified)
- Took a Neon branch snapshot of production as a rollback point before touching anything.
- Confirmed via the `pgmigrations` ledger + table list that production was in the clean "2-pending" state (no drift) before applying anything.
- Applied the two pending migrations directly to production: `1784567579158_create-manual-macro-entries-and-daily-targets`, `1784588946036_add-updated-at-to-manual-macro-entries`.
- Verified: ledger shows both applied; production logs show `/log-meal`, `/daily`, `/weekly`, `/settings/targets`, `/status` all loading clean (info-level only) post-migration, with zero new errors since.

## This PR — closing the gap
- New `migrate-production` CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): runs `npm run migrate:prod` against a `PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` repo secret on every push to `main`, gated on the `test` job passing first.
- Deliberately its own CI job, not a Vercel build step — the Vercel build fires on every Preview deployment too, which would attempt prod migrations on every PR. A dedicated `migrate-production` concurrency group serializes it across close-together merges.
- New `migrate:prod` script in `package.json` (same underlying `node-pg-migrate up`, targeting the prod secret instead of `.env.local`).
- `docs/definition-of-ready-and-done.md`: added "migrations reach production" as a baseline Definition of Done item, so a future slice can't merge a migration and consider it done without confirming this job went green. (Note: the canonical vault node for this standard needs the same edit — that's a PM-side step, not performed here, per the source-in-vault/snapshot-in-repo convention.)
- `README.md`: documents the new `migrate:prod` path and why it exists.

## Setup required before this job can run for real
`PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` does not exist as a repo secret yet — I did not set it myself (same reasoning as not touching the sensitive `DATABASE_URL` value directly): run `gh secret set PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL --repo albimartai/jerkai` and paste the production connection string when prompted.

## Test plan
- [x] Lint, typecheck, unit, component all green locally
- [x] YAML syntax validated
- [x] Hotfix verified live against production (see above)
- [x] `PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` secret needs to be set before merging, or the new job will fail on the next push to main
- [x] CI green on this PR

body: The system interface's Playwright e2e suite runs as part of the default `uv run pytest`, but when the frontend isn't built it would hang for ~20 minutes instead of skipping: each test loads the "Frontend not built" placeholder and then burns its timeout waiting for selectors that can never appear, and because the project sets `timeout_func_only=true` a stuck browser launch or server fixture is entirely unbounded. Separately, ten e2e tests had been silently skipped since the single-dockview simplification, so real UI regressions went uncaught. This adds a build-conditional module skip that fails fast (~0.06s) with a clear "frontend not built" message when `static/index.html` is missing, caps every e2e test's setup and body with `func_only=False` timeouts so no path can hang unbounded, and rewrites the ten stale dockview tests against the current DOM so they run and pass again. CI still builds the frontend first, so it continues to run the full e2e suite.

author: scollis
body:
## Summary

Adds **temporal interpolation of radar volumes by advection** — reconstruct a volume at a time *between* two observed volumes by estimating a dense, height-resolved motion field with optical flow and advecting the bracketing volumes to the target time before blending.

This complements the existing `grid_displacement_pc` (a single rigid displacement by phase correlation): a spatially varying field handles storms in which convective cells and stratiform regions move differently — the regime where a single vector fails.

The interpolation runs on the radar's **native (azimuth, range, elevation) gate geometry**, so the output is an ordinary `Radar`, not a grid.

## What's added

- `pyart/retrieve/advect_interpolate.py`
  - `grid_optical_flow(grid1, grid2, field, ...)` — per-level TV-L1 optical flow returning the **physical** grid1→grid2 echo displacement in metres (velocity is `displacement / dt`, no sign flip). scikit-image is guarded as an optional dependency via `MissingOptionalDependency`.
  - `advection_interpolate(radar1, radar2, alpha=/target_time=, ...)` — per-gate advection + time blend on `radar1`'s native geometry, returning a `Radar`.
- `pyart/testing/sample_objects.py`
  - `make_advecting_scene_radar` / `make_advection_interpolation_triplet` — an analytic reflectivity scene translating at a **known** velocity, providing exact ground truth for interpolation tests (styled to match the existing `make_*` builders).
- `tests/retrieve/test_advect_interpolate.py` — motion recovery, reconstruction quality, morph-beats-average, and α-endpoint recovery (guards the warp-sign convention). Skipped cleanly when scikit-image is absent.
- Exports wired into `pyart/retrieve/__init__.py`.

## Validation (synthetic scene, known rigid translation u=−12, v=+8 m/s)

Verified against the installed Py-ART:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| motion direction | Δ 0.19° |
| motion speed | 99% of true |
| t2 reconstruction | RMSE 0.031 dBZ, CC 1.000 |
| no-motion linear average | RMSE 1.73 dBZ |
| α=0 → t1 / α=1 → t3 | RMSE 0.012 / 0.020 |

## Notes

- The advection advantage over a plain time average is largest at long range, where gates are large and echo moves several gate-widths between volumes.
- Purely kinematic morphing cannot represent storm growth/decay, so residual error concentrates at cell edges.
- Depends only on `pyart.map.grid_from_radars`, `pyart.exceptions`, and `pyart.core`.

Prepared with Claude.

Co-authored-by: Scott Collis <scollis.acrf@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: bcandido
body:
## What changed and why

This addresses **item 4** of the PR #236 review (append-only re-scheduling) and, on top of that fix, adds a **scheduled workouts table** to the Routines page with filters, configurable pagination, and auto-refresh.

Garmin does not dedup schedules server-side: each `POST /workout-service/schedule/{id}` appends a new calendar entry. As a result, re-scheduling a routine stacked duplicate entries. We now track the `workoutScheduleId` Garmin returns and unschedule the prior entries before booking new dates, making (re)scheduling idempotent. With that tracking stored in a new `routine_schedules` table, the `/routines` page now lists scheduled entries (date + routine), with start-date and name filters, an adjustable page size, and per-row removal.

## Technical details

### Files changed
- `src/hevy2garmin/garmin.py` — `schedule_workout` now returns the `workoutScheduleId` (defensive: `None` if the body has no parseable id); new `unschedule_workout` helper (`DELETE /workout-service/schedule/{id}`).
- `src/hevy2garmin/db_interface.py` / `db_sqlite.py` / `db_postgres.py` — new `routine_schedules` table (one row per calendar entry) and methods: `add_routine_schedule`, `get_routine_schedule_ids`, `get_routine_scheduled_dates`, `clear_routine_schedules`, `delete_routine_schedule`, `get_upcoming_routine_schedules`, `count_upcoming_routine_schedules` (the last two support an optional title filter and share a FROM/JOIN/WHERE builder); `delete_synced_routine` also clears the routine's schedule rows.
- `src/hevy2garmin/sync.py` — `_reschedule_routine` helper (unschedule prior ids → clear → book new dates → record the returned ids; `unschedule_prior` flag), used by `schedule_routine` and the `sync_routines` restore path; `unschedule_routine_entry` (removes one entry and stops tracking it); `_is_not_found` helper to distinguish a 404.
- `src/hevy2garmin/server.py` — `routines_page` loads the schedules from the DB outside the Hevy fetch try/except; `_schedules_context(page, start_date, title, page_size)` helper; routes `GET /api/routines/schedules` (with `page`/`start`/`q`/`size`) and `POST /api/routines/{id}/schedule/{schedule_id}/unschedule`; `HX-Trigger: refreshSchedules` header on the schedule/sync endpoints.
- `src/hevy2garmin/templates/routine_schedules.html` — new HTMX partial (table + pagination + page-size selector + Remove button + empty state) that refreshes itself on the `refreshSchedules` event; included by `routines.html`, which hosts the filter form.
- `tests/test_routine.py` / `tests/test_db.py` — coverage for the new behavior (backend + UI).

### UI features
- **Scheduled workouts table**: date + routine name.
- **Filters**: start date (default: today) and routine-name search (case-insensitive substring, debounced). The form lives outside the swapped table, so typing keeps focus.
- **Page size**: a "Per page" selector below the table with 10 / 25 / 100 (default 10), validated against the allowed set.
- **Auto-refresh**: creating a new schedule (or running a sync) reloads the table via an HTMX event, no full page reload.
- **Remove**: each row unschedules the entry on Garmin and stops tracking it locally.
- Start date, name, and page size are preserved across pagination, removal, and refresh.

### Review fixes
A code review flagged four points, all addressed:
1. **Orphaned entry on transient failure** — `unschedule_routine_entry` only drops the tracking row on success or a **404** (already gone on Garmin). On a transient error (429/500/network) it re-raises so the route shows an error toast and the entry stays tracked for retry, instead of becoming an orphaned, unremovable calendar entry.
2. **Recurring dates lost on re-sync** — a content-change re-sync now re-books **every** date the routine had tracked (not just the earliest), preventing silent loss of recurring sessions.
3. **Redundant unschedule calls** — in the restore path the old workout was just deleted (its calendar entries already cascaded away), so `_reschedule_routine(unschedule_prior=False)` skips the per-id `unschedule_workout` calls (1s rate-limit each, all 404s).
4. **Duplicated SQL** — `get_upcoming_routine_schedules` and `count_upcoming_routine_schedules` share an `_upcoming_from_where(...)` builder per backend instead of repeating the FROM/JOIN/WHERE.

### Approach and trade-offs
I chose a normalized `routine_schedules` table (keyed by `hevy_routine_id + schedule_id`) over a JSON list in a single column, because a routine can accumulate many entries (recurring goes up to 52) and mutating a serialized list in one cell is awkward to maintain. Unscheduling during a reschedule is best-effort (an entry already gone on Garmin just 404s and is ignored); the manual removal path distinguishes a 404 from transient errors. The UI table reads local DB state only, so it renders even when the Hevy fetch fails; "today" is computed on the server and injected into the DB methods, keeping them pure/testable (ISO dates compare correctly as text). The name filter is a case-insensitive substring, without escaping wildcards (the user's own data). Page size is validated against `(10, 25, 100)` and falls back to 10 if invalid.

### How to test
```bash
# SQLite (default)
PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/test_routine.py tests/test_db.py -q
PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/ -q
# Postgres (CI parity — the DB layer changed)
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://test:test@localhost:5432/hevy2garmin_test PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/ -q
```
Manual: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m hevy2garmin.cli serve --port 8123`, open `http://localhost:8123/routines`, schedule a routine twice for the same date and confirm only one Garmin calendar entry exists; check the "Scheduled workouts" table, filter by name (the table updates without losing focus) and by start date, change the page size (10/25/100), paginate, and use the Remove button.

Reviewer note: the assumed key in the schedule POST response is `workoutScheduleId`. If it differs, parsing falls back to `None` (degrades to "not tracked", without breaking scheduling).

### Breaking changes
No contract breakage. There is an **additive, backward-compatible schema change**: a new `routine_schedules` table created via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on both backends (SQLite and Postgres). No existing column was altered or removed.

### Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] No sensitive data in logs or responses
- [x] Migrations are backward-compatible (new table, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`)
- [ ] Feature flag (not applicable)

author: edpft
body:
Closes the gap left by #7: Dependabot covers cargo and github-actions, but does
not understand `flake.lock`, so nix inputs on a flake-based repo drift until
someone runs `nix flake update` by hand.

`nix-flake-update.yml` runs it on the caller's schedule and opens a pull
request, so the update goes through CI and review like any other change.
Re-running force-pushes the branch, which updates the existing pull request
rather than opening a second one.

## Why not `DeterminateSystems/update-flake-lock`?

It is the only maintained action for this — there is no nix-community
equivalent — but as of v3 it no longer installs nix itself, so it amounts to
`nix flake update` plus PR creation. Doing that directly costs about fifteen
lines, adds no vendor to the supply chain, and keeps this repo on the
`nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action` the other nix workflows already use.

## Caveat worth knowing before enabling it

Pull requests opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not raise workflow
events, so the update will arrive with **no CI run against it**. Pass a
personal access token as the `token` secret if you want it checked before
merging. This is documented in the README, and is the same limitation the
Determinate Systems action carries.

`actionlint` passes on all nine workflows.

author: cradcliff187
body:
## What this adds

Chris's ask: *"If we're gonna change the status of an estimate, why would it not inform the user of anything connected to it and give them the opportunity to allow for the other items to move along?"*

Rule 27's carry-forward is automatic but **silent** — and it has two blind spots this PR closes with UI, not with new write paths:

### 1. Status-change dialog now shows connected records

`EstimateStatusSelector`'s approve/un-approve confirmation gains a "what's attached" section: accepted quotes (count + $), other attached quotes, expense allocations (count + $), dispatch assignment links, generated contracts, and AIA SOV presence.

- **Un-approve**: shows this estimate's own attachments — they stay attached, but cost tracking stops reading them once it's no longer the baseline.
- **Approve**: shows attachments on the estimate(s) about to be *un*-approved. Status changes never re-point FKs (only `create_estimate_version` does), so those records will NOT follow — the dialog says so and points at New Version as the carrying path.
- Advisory only: fetch failure never blocks the status change; zero connections renders nothing extra.

Real-data example: un-approving `225-005-EST-01` now surfaces **9 accepted quotes · $378,180** and **161 expense allocations** before the user confirms.

### 2. Save pre-flight: dropped lines with attachments get an explicit review

`EstimateForm.handleSave` now checks, **before any write**, for lines this save would leave behind that still have quotes / allocations / dispatch links:

- **Edit-in-place**: removed rows about to be DELETEd (quote FKs would go NULL via cascade — the previously-silent path at the old `toDelete` comment).
- **New-version save**: source-estimate (and currently-approved-estimate) lines not claimed via `sourceLineItemId` — the exact orphan class from Gotcha #65 ($121K found in the June audit).

The dialog lists each line with its attachments and offers per-line **Restore & review** (line returns to the form; the RPC's `source_line_item_id` re-point then carries everything automatically — restore deliberately cancels the save so the PM sees the totals change before committing) or **Save without them** (explicit, informed). Lines on a non-source estimate render informational-only, since the RPC's ownership guard would skip re-pointing them; the hint says to switch "Copy from".

Clean 1:1 versioning (every line carried) hits zero new friction — no dialog, no extra queries beyond the pre-flight reads.

## Implementation notes

- New shared read-side helper [src/utils/estimateConnections.ts](../blob/feat/estimate-connected-records-awareness/src/utils/estimateConnections.ts) powers both surfaces; everything is read-only.
- Dialog follows the promise-based `useConfirmDialog` pattern (Gotcha #73, z-[75]); single scroll zone per Gotcha #40; split correlations use `expense_splits.split_amount`, whole-expense ones `expenses.amount`.
- No DB/RPC changes. No new write paths.

## Verification

- `npm run pre-deploy` ✅, `npm run type-check` ✅, `npm run build` (incl. PWA) ✅
- ESLint: zero new findings (the 4 errors in touched files pre-exist on main — verified via stash-lint)
- All five PostgREST embed shapes validated against the live API (200s), including the nested `quotes→payees` embed
- **Not click-verified**: the local preview session was signed out and estimate surfaces need an admin login. Suggested manual pass on SYS-TEST: (a) open an approved estimate with accepted quotes → status pill → change status → confirm the attached-records box renders; (b) New Version → delete a quoted line → Save → confirm the review dialog appears and Restore returns the line.

## Summary

Reworks the auto plan-generator engine so the fastest plan for an on-track student (no reprovações) **is the curriculum grade itself**, keeps the project sequence (Gerência de Projetos → Projetos I → Projetos II) consecutive and in order, and treats Saturday offerings as neutral for conflict detection. Fixes a bug where the project chain could be dropped entirely.

## Related issue

<!-- none -->

## Type of change

- [x] ✨ `feat` — new feature
- [x] 🐛 `fix` — bug fix

## What changed

- **`lib/schedule-conflict.ts`** — `SATURDAY_DAY` + `stripNeutralDays()`; the generator strips Saturday cells before conflict tests so a Saturday offering never blocks a course. Timetable UI unchanged.
- **`lib/plan-generator/generate.ts`** — grade-anchored packer: each course targets `max(startN, course.phase)` and only slides later when a prerequisite, conflict, credit cap, or turno filter forces it (never earlier). Consecutive-in-order placement for the project sequence group. Fixes the group being abandoned when a member's external prerequisite (`Introdução a Projetos`) wasn't placed yet.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch is off `main`
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [ ] `pnpm run lint` — n/a (repo's legacy `next lint` needs a flat ESLint config; relied on `tsc --noEmit`, clean)
- [x] `pnpm run build` passes (`next build` exit 0)
- [x] Tested locally (see below)
- [x] Docs updated (`sprints/01-auto-plan-generator/review.md`)

## How I tested

Ran the engine against the **real Sistemas de Informação (238_20111)** and **Ciências da Computação (208)** curricula pulled from prod, plus synthetic harnesses:

- On-track SI student → all 46 mandatory courses on their nominal phase, 9 phases = `totalPhases` (the grade).
- Project chain: Gerência → sem 7, Projetos I → sem 8, Projetos II → sem 9 (consecutive, in order); holds off-track too.
- Off-track (failed phase-1 course) re-plans the failure to sem 2, graduates in 8; 0 unplaceable.
- Turno filter: morning-only vs night-only pick disjoint sections; unmatched → `no-section-in-turno`.
- Saturday-only same-time courses co-exist in one semester; weekday same-time courses split across semesters.

## Notes for reviewers

- The project sequence is matched by **course name** (`SEQUENCE_GROUP_MATCHERS`), so it's degree-specific: present in SI, absent in CS208 (TCC I/II). Other degrees fall back to their natural prereq chain. Worth generalizing later.
- Full acceptance-criteria walkthrough in `sprints/01-auto-plan-generator/review.md`.

author: metascroy
body:
Reverts pytorch/executorch#21041

This change breaks executorch/backends/arm/test:addmm
test_addmm_u55_INT[basic] on Corstone-300: the model output is all zeros
instead of the reference [[2,4],[6,8]].

Root cause: running FuseDuplicateUsersPass after InsertRescalePass. In the
[basic] case x1 and x3 are value-identical, so FuseEqualPlaceholdersPass
merges them into a single placeholder that feeds both the matmul operand
and the bias/add path. After rescale insertion, that shared producer has
multiple tosa.RESCALE users, and fusing them corrupts the quantized addmm
data flow, zeroing the output. Bisected to the late FuseDuplicateUsersPass
insertion specifically (reordering EnsureUniqueOutputNodesPass is not the
cause).

author: yazzbert
body:
W1 chunk 5 of the Better Auth implementation ([handoff](https://github.com/yazzbert/FiBuKI-selfhost/blob/main/handoffs/2026-07-21-w1-better-auth-impl.md)), per the approved decision (docs/decisions.md 2026-07-21): **unauthenticated `app/api/*` requests answer `401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}` instead of 500**, and the two routes that echoed internal error text into the body no longer do. Flips all 6 api-smoke xfail marks.

## What changed

- **[`lib/auth/get-server-user.ts`](lib/auth/get-server-user.ts)** — `getServerUserIdWithFallback` now throws a typed `UnauthorizedError` (message unchanged, so the existing `/Unauthorized/` smoke pins hold). New `unauthorizedResponse(error)` returns the single 401 shape for that error and `null` for anything else — never any internal text.
- **43 consumer routes** — every `catch` wrapping the auth call now opens with the two-line guard:
  ```ts
  const unauthorized = unauthorizedResponse(error);
  if (unauthorized) return unauthorized;
  ```
  Applied by a brace-matching codemod (guard inserted only into the catch of the `try` that actually contains the `getServerUserIdWithFallback` call — inner catches untouched), then the whole diff reviewed by hand. `chat/route.ts` had the call **outside** any try (the throw escaped to a Next default 500 — and chat is a route the selfhost UI calls); it got a minimal dedicated try/catch.
- **Two deliberate exceptions:**
  - `auth/device/approve` already answers its own 401 via an inner try/catch — left as is.
  - `finapi/callback` is a **browser** redirect target (finAPI web form): an `UnauthorizedError` there redirects to `/login` — the route's own previously-dead intent — rather than answering JSON to a human.
- **`functions/src/api-smoke/auth-routes.test.ts`** — the 6 `⚠ …answers 401…` marks flipped to plain tests; header updated. No assertion weakened; the passing "JSON error, no crash" pins are unchanged.

The now-truly-dead `if (!userId) return 401` branches inside the routes are untouched — removing them is per-route cleanup, not part of this contract change.

## Verification

The api-smoke suite requires root `node_modules`, which the audit box intentionally doesn't have — **the "App API routes (auth smoke)" CI job is the gate for this PR.** The changed-file typecheck rides the normal Next build job.

Touches the Firebase build (approved): behavior change is strictly unauthenticated-request response shape.
