## Problem

With the per-type "Fill" style enabled, a detection that has a polygon gets both its polygon *and* its bounding rectangle filled, shading the whole box area.

## Fix

When a detection has polygon geometry, the fill setting now applies solely to the polygon; the bounding rectangle stays unfilled. Detections with only a rectangle keep the existing fill behavior. The rectangle layer already computed a per-detection `hasPoly` flag, which the fill style function now respects.

author: nithiink
body:
Fixes the auto-fixable findings from the 2026-07-21 daily security review. Refs #52.

## Fixes (mapped to findings)

### M1 — `backend/claude_runner.py` (`SDKClaudeRunner._map_decision`, ExitPlanMode branch)
The branch approved the plan whenever the answer contained an intent word (`auto`/`manual`/`proceed`/`approve`), **even after `decide_permission` had already resolved it to `deny`**. So a decline such as `"do not proceed"` (which contains `"proceed"`) was inverted into `PermissionResultAllow()`, defeating the module's documented fail-closed contract.
**Fix:** short-circuit on an explicit `deny` before the intent-substring test.

### M2 — `backend/tmux_runner.py` (`_classify_plan_choice`)
The `manual`/`auto` intent substrings (`"manual"`, `"approve edit"`, `"each edit"`, `"review edit"`, `"auto"`) were tested **before** the decline branch, and that decline branch only caught negations at the *start* of the phrase. `"do not approve edits"` matched `"approve edit"` → `manual`, and a phrase like `"please don't switch to auto"` matched `"auto"` → escalated to auto-approve-everything mode.
**Fix:** evaluate an explicit decline (`decide_permission(c) == "deny"`) first.

### L1 — `frontend/next.config.mjs`
Added a `headers()` block applying `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` to all routes — clickjacking protection + defense-in-depth for the command-proxying UI (which binds `0.0.0.0` in network mode).

## Verification
`decide_permission` was checked in isolation to confirm the fixes preserve the happy paths:
- Declines that contain intent words → `deny` (now correctly short-circuited): `"do not proceed"`, `"don't approve"`, `"do not approve edits"`, `"please don't switch to auto"`.
- Genuine approvals → still approved: `"proceed"`, `"manually approve edits"`, `"auto"` (→ `None`, handled by the existing intent path), `"yes"`, `"approve"`.

No existing test references `_map_decision`, `_classify_plan_choice`, or `SAFE_TOOLS`, so behavior of the covered paths is unchanged. (The full pytest suite couldn't run in the review sandbox — `claude_agent_sdk` isn't installed there — so please let CI exercise it.)

## Left for manual attention (not in this PR)
- **M3 — `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` auto-approved as `safe`** (`backend/permissions.py:12-17`): a real prompt-injection exfiltration/SSRF path (unprompted `WebFetch` can carry local data to an arbitrary host), but removing it from `SAFE_TOOLS` is a deliberate product/UX tradeoff, so it's left for a maintainer decision.
- **Broad default Origin regex / no Host-header validation** — tracked in the still-open #49.
- **`NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` in `dev:network`** — previously reported (#23/#36); loopback-capped.

author: wibias
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `schtasks /create` requires an elevated (admin) token. The update worker inherits the non-elevated proxy's privileges, so a service-managed install updated from the GUI or a normal terminal fails with access denied (`Zugriff verweigert`). The old code threw an error or only warned, leaving the proxy stopped after a successful update.

## Fix

Both the GUI path (`src/update/job.ts`) and the CLI path (`src/update/index.ts`) now detect the service reinstall failure and fall back to spawning the proxy directly (detached, with `--port` pinned to the pre-update port). The update never leaves the user without a running proxy.

The stale service manager can be refreshed later with an admin `ocx service install`.

## Changes

- `src/update/job.ts`: GUI restart path tracks `serviceOk` instead of throwing on non-zero exit; falls through to `spawnDetachedStart` on failure with an informative log message.
- `src/update/index.ts`: CLI restart path spawns the proxy directly (detached) when `svc.status !== 0` instead of only printing a warning.
- `tests/update-job.test.ts`: New test asserting that a service reinstall failure (`runService` returns `{ status: 1 }`) triggers the `spawnStart` fallback with the correct port.

author: ksuetani
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-98622

## What Is Being Fixed

Inside a Publication, clicking Delete on a page and then quickly triggering Delete again (double-click, or reopening the delete modal while the first fetch is still in flight) produces two concurrent delete requests. Both attempt to insert CTEntry rows against the unique index `(ctCollectionId, modelClassNameId, modelClassPK)`, which under MySQL 8 InnoDB REPEATABLE READ collide on next-key locks and surface as a `SQLTransactionRollbackException` stack trace to the user.

## How It Is Being Fixed

A JavaScript guard blocks the second attempt of the same delete when the session is inside a Publication. `LayoutActionsDisplayContext`, `LayoutsAdminManagementToolbarDisplayContext`, and `LayoutsTreeDisplayContext` now expose `CTCollectionThreadLocal.getCTCollectionId()` as `ctCollectionId` on the delete dropdown item's data (or the tree config), so `openDeleteLayoutModal.js` and `PagesTree.js` can decide whether to guard without scraping the DOM.

Each of the two client modules maintains a module-scope `Set` of in-flight delete URLs, added on Confirm-click and cleared when the delete promise settles. A second attempt on the same URL surfaces a danger toast — "This page is currently being deleted in the selected publication." — and the modal does not reopen. Different pages remain independently deletable, and deletes outside a Publication behave unchanged (no guard applies).

## PR Check

body:
## Finding M1 (Bruker→NIfTI/BIDS mapping audit)

`Header` never called `set_qform`/`set_sform`, so nibabel's from-affine defaults
applied: `sform_code=2` (ALIGNED) and `qform_code=0` (qform unused). For
scanner-native data the correct code is `1` (NIFTI_XFORM_SCANNER_ANAT), and both
forms should carry the transform (matching dcm2niix). Modern tools read the sform
first so orientation is preserved in practice, but tools that only honor the
qform got an unoriented image, and code 2 mislabels provenance.

## Fix

`_set_sform_qform` tags both forms with the image affine and code 1. Verified to
survive a save round-trip (`qform_code=sform_code=1`, both affines equal input).

## Tests

Added to `tests/09_nifti_header_test.py`: round-trip a saved image and assert both
codes are 1 and both forms equal the input affine.

author: joglekara
body:
## Summary

Adds a collision operator for `vlasov1d` whose equilibrium is a **super-Gaussian** $f_0 \propto \exp(-\beta|v-\bar v|^m)$ instead of a Maxwellian:

```yaml
terms:
  fokker_planck:
    is_on: True
    type: super_gaussian
    m: 3.0
    self_consistent_beta: {enabled: True, max_steps: 3}   # recommended for long runs
```

This is the 1D-1V counterpart of maintaining a Langdon/DLM inverse-bremsstrahlung-heated distribution: the standard LB/Dougherty operators actively maxwellianize a super-Gaussian background, which is unwanted in Landau-damping / LPI studies with DLM distributions. This operator *maintains* a prescribed order `m` (it does not generate `m` dynamically — no heating/e-e competition as in the VFP-1D IB operator; a prescribed `m(x,t)` from Matte's fit is a possible follow-up).

## Design

- **Exact-potential drift**: `C_edge = D·Δφ/dv` with `φ = β|v-v̄|^m`, rather than the midpoint derivative. Chang-Cooper's fixed point satisfies `f_{i+1}/f_i = exp(-C·dv/D)`, so this makes the *sampled* super-Gaussian the exact discrete equilibrium. (The midpoint form is exact only at m=2 and causes secular temperature drift otherwise.)
- **Energy-conserving β closure**: `β = n/(m·⟨|v-v̄|^m⟩)` — the generalization of the LB/Dougherty `β = 1/(2T)`, which it equals at m=2 — refined by a Newton solve of the δ-weighted **discrete energy-flux condition** `Σₑ vₑ(w·f̃(w) + Δf) = 0`. A sampled super-Gaussian is an exact root of this condition, so the discrete equilibrium is exactly stationary (no secular drift, verified < 1e-8 over 100 collision times). The Newton reuses the existing `self_consistent_beta` config knobs.
- `m=2` reduces to `chang_cooper_dougherty` step for step (tested).
- `find_self_consistent_beta` is generalized to super-Gaussian targets (`m` parameter, default 2.0 preserves existing behavior bitwise).

## Conservation properties

- **Density**: exact (zero-flux BC).
- **Energy**: exact at equilibrium (with `self_consistent_beta` enabled); off-equilibrium transients carry a one-time O(ν·dt) offset from operator splitting (β frozen from fⁿ during the implicit step) — first-order convergence in dt verified in tests; negligible at production ν·dt.
- **Momentum**: exact for f symmetric about v̄; skewed transients exchange momentum at O(skewness) (the m=2 `C ∝ v-v̄` cancellation doesn't generalize). Documented in the config reference.

## Testing

- 8 new tests in `tests/test_vlasov1d/test_super_gaussian_fp.py`: SG fixed point (m=3, 4), no secular drift at equilibrium, Maxwellian→SG relaxation with O(dt) energy-error convergence, Dougherty control (maxwellianizes the same IC), shifted-SG momentum conservation, m=2 ≡ Dougherty, self-consistent-β unit test.
- Existing suites pass: vlasov1d FP relaxation/conservation/momentum + config validation (24), vfp1d FP model tests (10).
- End-to-end smoke via `ergoExo` on the FP-conservation config with `type: super_gaussian`: kurtosis 3.00 → 2.44 toward the m=3 target 2.418, density conserved to 1e-14.

Note: `test_config_regression.py` has 3 pre-existing failures on `main` (stale baselines from the `vmin` feature), unrelated to this PR and being fixed separately.

author: thierrycantin-demers
body:
The store `Collector` recorded `param.val()` and never applied the param mapper's `on_save` (`transform_for_save` had no callers). The load side validates the persisted shape and applies `on_load`, so any shape-mapped param (a `Col`-layout `Linear` weight) failed to reload from a saved record: first save works, every later load errors with a shape mismatch.

Fix: collect through `transform_for_save()`. Adds a round-trip regression test with a transpose-mapped param.

Note: applying a record onto an already-initialized shape-mapped param would still mismatch (`lazy_shape()` returns the live form there); loading onto a fresh lazy module, the common path, is what this fixes.

author: sedaoran
body: The server sends a lecture unit's release date as an ISO string. The server-side date conversion only transformed the top-level releaseDate for text/online units; for attachment/video units it converted only the nested attachment date, so the unit's own releaseDate reached the edit form as a raw ISO string and the date picker displayed an unformatted timestamp. Convert the unit's own releaseDate for every unit type in both convertLectureUnitResponseDatesFromServer and convertLectureUnitDateFromServer. Closes #13259 ### Summary When editing a File/Video lecture unit that has a release date, the release-date field showed a raw ISO timestamp (e.g. `2026-07-15T13:39:00+02:00`) instead of a formatted date, and the form misbehaved until the date was re-entered manually. The unit's own `releaseDate` was never converted from the server representation for attachment/video units, so the raw string reached the date picker. This PR converts the unit's own `releaseDate` for **every** unit type, fixing both the display and the form behavior. ### Checklist #### General - [x] This is a small issue that I tested locally and was confirmed by another developer on a test server. - [x] Language: I followed the [guidelines for inclusive, diversity-sensitive, and appreciative language](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/language). - [x] I chose a title conforming to the [naming conventions for pull requests](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/development-process#pr-naming-conventions). #### Client - [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a very good performance, prevented too many (unnecessary) REST calls and made sure the UI is responsive, even with large data (e.g. using paging). - [x] I **strictly** followed the principle of **data economy** for all client-server REST calls. - [x] I **strictly** followed the [client coding guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/client-development). - [x] I added multiple integration tests (Vitest) related to the features (with a high test coverage), while following the [test guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/client-tests). - [x] I documented the TypeScript code using JSDoc style. ### Motivation and Context When editing a File/Video lecture unit that has a release date, the release-date field displayed a raw ISO timestamp instead of the formatted date used everywhere else, and the form did not behave normally until the date was manually re-selected. The server sends a lecture unit's release date as an ISO string. The server-side date conversion (`convertLectureUnitResponseDatesFromServer` / `convertLectureUnitDateFromServer` in `lecture-unit.service.ts`) only transformed the top-level `releaseDate` for text/online units. For attachment/video units it converted only the nested attachment date, so the unit's own `releaseDate` reached the edit form (`edit-attachment-video-unit.component.ts`, `formProperties.releaseDate = unit.releaseDate`) as a raw ISO string, which the date picker then rendered unformatted. Closes #13259 ### Description Convert the unit's own `releaseDate` unconditionally (via `convertDateFromServer`) for every unit type in both `convertLectureUnitResponseDatesFromServer` and `convertLectureUnitDateFromServer`. The type-specific conversions of the nested attachment/exercise dates are unchanged. This guarantees the raw ISO string from the server is never passed to the date picker, regardless of unit type. Added Vitest regression tests covering the attachment/video unit release-date conversion on both the response and array paths. ### Steps for Testing Prerequisites: - 1 Instructor or Editor - 1 Course with 1 Lecture 1. Log in to Artemis as an Instructor/Editor. 2. Navigate to the Lecture and open the **Lecture Units** section. 3. Create a **File/Video** unit: set a name, attach a PDF, and set a **release date**. Save. 4. Click **Edit** on the created unit. 5. Verify the release-date field shows the date in the normal formatted representation (not a raw ISO timestamp like `2026-07-15T13:39:00+02:00`). 6. Verify the form can be saved without having to re-enter the release date. ### Testserver States You can manage test servers using [Helios](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/). Check environment statuses in the [environment list](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/repo/69562331/environment/list). To deploy to a test server, go to the [CI/CD](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/repo/69562331/ci-cd) page, find your PR or branch, and trigger the deployment. ### Review Progress #### Code Review - [ ] Code Review 1 - [ ] Code Review 2 #### Manual Tests - [ ] Test 1 - [ ] Test 2 ### Test Coverage #### Client | Class/File | Line Coverage | Lines | Expects | Ratio | |------------|-------------:|------:|--------:|------:| | lecture-unit.service.ts | 97.40% | 176 | 32 | 18.2 | _Last updated: 2026-07-30 19:10:13 UTC_ ### Screenshots _UI change: before fix : after fix : ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed lecture unit release dates not being consistently converted for display. * Ensured attachment video and other lecture unit dates work correctly with date pickers. * Added coverage for date conversion in both individual and array responses.

body:
Backlog fix wave part4-2: four singleton fix-needed community PRs, each salvaged, repaired per the adversarial-review findings, and rebased onto current master. Original authors credited via Co-authored-by on each commit. Nothing is closed here — references only.

## Takeover of #1417 — fix(lint): only unwrap whole-page code fences
Detection used `/m` regexes (a fence anywhere) while the fixer used string-anchored regexes, so a note that merely *contains* a ` ```markdown ` block lost only its closing fence and was re-corrupted every autopilot lint cycle. Detection and fix now share a single `analyzeMarkdownWrap` check. The PR's unrelated `plugin.json` + perplexity-research commits were dropped (off-mission, reference a private external system).

## Takeover of #1341 — fix(extract): don't split timeline bullets on bare hyphens
The bullet separator regex split on any `[—–-]` with optional whitespace, so hyphenated slugs (`acme-consulting-group`) were split mid-word into bogus source/summary pairs. The plain hyphen now requires surrounding whitespace; em/en dashes keep their old optional-space behavior. Unlike the original PR's replacement, spaced-plain-hyphen, unspaced-em-dash, long, and parenthesized sources all keep extracting — no data regression for existing brains.

## Takeover of #1294 — fix: Windows compat (CRLF frontmatter, posix relTarget, read-only apply-migrations, gbrainDir contract)
All four verified bugs land: CRLF-tolerant frontmatter parsing (shared `extractFrontmatterBlock` helper replaces three hand-rolled copies), `posix.join` for portable skillpack `relTarget` keys, `apply-migrations --list/--dry-run` skip the schema-drift preflight DB connect, and preferences' `gbrainDir()` now delegates to `configDir()` so GBRAIN_HOME means the same thing everywhere. New on top of the PR: a one-time legacy-path adoption moves `preferences.json` + `migrations/completed.jsonl` from the old `$GBRAIN_HOME/...` location so the contract unification can't orphan an existing migration ledger.

## Takeover of #1430 — fix(sync): suppress last_sync_at when git pull failed
Part A of the PR (no-op heartbeat) already shipped in v0.42.52.0 and is dropped. Part B lands rebased onto the refactored sync.ts: when the upstream pull is attempted and fails, `last_commit` still advances for converged local imports but `last_sync_at` is not stamped — on the anchor writes, the full-reimport path, and the v0.42.52.0 `up_to_date` heartbeat (which otherwise still lied about freshness after a failed pull). author: rpdavid78
body:
## Summary

- add an independent-reset TRL FixBN mode while preserving `rolling` for historical reproduction
- propagate and record the mode in the canonical CIFAR-100 runner, CIFAR-100-C evaluator, and TRL ablation/diagnostic consumers
- add a paired seed-0 rolling-vs-reset audit with draw-order, beta-grid-order, and full sweep-to-final controls
- document the protocol, limitations, artifact hashes, and escalation decision

## Root cause

The historical TRL FixBN path recalibrated BatchNorm without resetting running statistics between posterior samples. This made the predictor weakly dependent on sample and beta-sweep order. The corrected mode resets each sampled network and uses cumulative averaging (`momentum=None`) over the 25 calibration batches.

## Seed-0 audit outcome

Both modes selected `beta=4`. In the complete sweep-to-final pipeline, reset minus rolling was:

- accuracy: -0.000500 (threshold 0.002)
- NLL: +0.000827 (threshold 0.010)
- ECE: +0.002321 (threshold 0.005)
- Brier: -0.000024 (threshold 0.005)
- entropy AUROC: +0.002487 (threshold 0.010)

Independent reset was exactly invariant to reversed posterior-draw and beta-grid order. No predeclared trigger fired, so the reported five-seed TRL row does not require rerunning seeds 0-4.

## Validation

Run in the paper environment on `remote-llama` (PyTorch 2.5.1+cu121, RTX 6000 Ada):

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 31 tests passed
- `python tests/test_release_layout.py` — 31 required files verified
- `git diff --check` — clean

The definitive run artifact and the post-run decision hardening are separately hashed and explained in `docs/trl_fixbn_protocol.md`; the hardening changes validation/decision metadata only, not sampling or metric generation.

author: scoop
body:
## TL;DR — herdr 0.7.5 breaks Shepherd; this protects operators from it

herdr 0.7.5 (socket protocol 17) reshaped `agent start` so that Shepherd's spawn command — an `env …` shim (always), wrapped in `bwrap … -- env … claude …` when a bwrap sandbox backend is present — **can no longer be launched**. Verified against a live 0.7.5 server (`/proc` inspection): herdr runs `claude env NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=… claude …`, i.e. the shim tokens become positional args to claude and the compile-cache/TMPDIR pinning is lost. **This is every spawn, on the CLI path 0.7.5 actually uses — not just the socket, not just sandboxed spawns.** Shepherd cannot launch a single agent on 0.7.5.

So this PR does **not** add 0.7.5 support (that needs a new spawn mechanism — see **#1889**). It pins support to **herdr ≤ 0.7.4** and makes an accidental upgrade fail *loudly and safely* instead of cryptically:

- **Detect** the installed herdr version (`src/herdr-capabilities.ts`), refreshed after a `herdr update` and by the diagnostics probe.
- **Warn loudly at startup, keep running** — `preflight` emits a prominent banner on ≥ 0.7.5 (so an operator already on it sees why, and non-spawn surfaces still respond).
- **Fail spawns clearly** — the driver's `start()` throws `HerdrSpawnUnsupportedError` on ≥ 0.7.5 (CLI + socket) instead of spawning a broken agent.
- **Block the in-app herdr updater** — `check()` flags `latestUnsupported`, `apply()` refuses, and `HerdrUpdateModal` shows a warning + hides the run button, so nobody upgrades *into* 0.7.5 from within Shepherd.
- **Diagnostics** reports an installed ≥ 0.7.5 as an error (`diagnostics_hint_herdr_unsupported`).
- **Docs** (README + getting-started) advise pinning to 0.7.4.

## Why this shape

Earlier I explored full 0.7.4/0.7.5 dual-support, but live verification showed the 0.7.5 `agent start --kind` model can't express Shepherd's sandboxed/env-wrapped spawn, so 0.7.5 is unusable regardless. Shipping a "dual-support" that can't spawn would be misleading; the honest move is to guard against it and advise pinning, then build real 0.7.5 support (with a compatible spawn path) as one coherent change in **#1889**.

## Live verification (isolated, non-destructive)

Ran an isolated 0.7.5 server on its own socket (never touched the operator's live 0.7.4). Confirmed:
- `agent start --kind claude -- <wrapped>` runs `claude <wrapped>` → env shim becomes garbage args, pinning lost (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`).
- Strict agent names: v075 rejects `TASK-01` / names with spaces (`invalid_agent_name`).
- Targeting: `terminal_id` rejected (`agent_not_found`); only `pane_id`/name accepted.
- A freshly-created tab's pane can be briefly `agent_pane_busy`.

All four are captured in #1889 as requirements for the future spawn path.

## Verification of this PR

`tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint`, full root `bun test` (7,557 pass / 0 fail), `cd ui && bun run check` + `check:i18n` (locales in parity), the `HerdrUpdateModal` browser test (incl. a new blocked-state case), and the `fallow audit` pre-push gate — all green. New tests cover the version ceiling, the spawn guard (refuses ≥0.7.5, spawns nothing), the update-block, and the diagnostics `unsupported` state.

Follow-up (real 0.7.5 support): **#1889**.

`[no-feature-entry]` — protective guard/warning, not a discoverable feature.

author: mauricioperera
body:
Implements the follow-up announced in the README's rag-local section: MicroExpert's own recall can now query [rag-local](https://github.com/MauricioPerera/rag-local) natively instead of RepoMemory — no host-side glue needed.

## Config (opt-in, default untouched)

```json
{
  "retrieval": {
    "provider": "rag-local",
    "ragLocal": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8937",
      "collection": "kb",
      "k": 5,
      "threshold": 0.35,
      "expandLinks": true,
      "hops": 2,
      "timeoutMs": 10000
    }
  }
}
```

## Design decisions

- **Only context recall is pluggable** — sessions, mining, profiles and memory packs stay on RepoMemory.
- `recall()` is now `async`; call sites updated with `await` only (2 existing test files touched: sync→async form, zero assertions changed).
- **Never crashes the user request**: rag-local unreachable/timeout → `console.warn` + empty context.
- `relevanceThreshold` (RepoMemory's unnormalized scale) deliberately does NOT apply to rag-local — its cosine `threshold` travels in the query body instead. Mixing scales would be wrong.
- Markdown links in retrieved facts are rendered to plain text before injection (small models must not see link syntax).

## Verification

- Suite **326/326** (319 existing + 7 new hermetic tests, mocked `fetch`, asserts on the exact URL/body sent).
- **Real E2E**: seeded a rag-local collection with a fact that exists nowhere else; `micro-expert serve` + 1B answered it correctly ("The Zephyr build pipeline runs on delta-9."). Killed rag-local mid-session: warn logged, request degraded gracefully.
- Measured context for why this matters: with this retrieval stack the 1B went 5-6/10 → 10/10 (lookup) and 64% → 91% (synthesis) — see [evaluaciones-modelos-locales](https://github.com/MauricioPerera/evaluaciones-modelos-locales).

author: bagsdz
body:
## Production outage fix

After #14 deployed, every DB-backed endpoint returned **500** (health endpoint stayed 200, masking it). Cause: the new engine config passed

```python
connect_args={"connect_timeout": 5, "options": "-c statement_timeout=8000"}
```

The `options` startup parameter works on a **direct** Neon endpoint but the **Neon pooler (PgBouncer) rejects unknown startup parameters**, failing every connection.

**Fix:** drop the `options` arg; keep `connect_timeout` (libpq param, safe on both direct and pooler). Runaway queries are bounded by the serverless function timeout anyway.

Merge + redeploy restores service on either endpoint (direct or `-pooler`).

- Desktop (lg+): activating swaps into a split layout, iframe left ~2/3 / detail content right ~1/3, deep-linkable via `?preview=1`, Esc + a close control return to normal. Below lg it's a plain external link — no split on phones.

Converted that row to a Tailwind v4 container query (`@container` + `@xl`) so it reflows by available width instead of viewport width.

## Deviations from issue #12's plan

This route is force-dynamic (`getSessionUser()` reads `cookies()`), so the router call is a real navigation there — it round-tripped to the server and raced/reverted the `?preview=1` param under repeated testing. `history.replaceState` is the documented shallow-routing escape hatch (Next patches it to keep `usePathname`/`useSearchParams` in sync everywhere, no refetch) and matches the issue's "no refetch" requirement more literally than the router would have.
- Everything else (opt-in flag, action-row placement, component split between trigger/layout, iframe attributes, load-timeout fallback, reduced-motion guard) matches the issue's plan as written.

author: akashsinghal
body:
## Summary

Makes stale cached-bearer challenge recovery a built-in part of the authentication flow.

- Runs normal 401 challenge handling first.
- If normal handling dead-ends and the rejected request carried an SDK-cached bearer token, replays a safe GET/HEAD once without authorization.
- Feeds a recovered 401 back through the existing realm validation, credential lookup, token exchange, caching, and retry path.

## Motivation

Some registries return an unusable challenge when an expired anonymous token is presented. In the observed `nvcr.io` case, the stale-token 401 points to `authn.nvidia.com`, which cannot mint an anonymous token, while a credential-free request returns the usable `nvcr.io/proxy_auth` challenge. A client that only follows the realm from the stale-token 401 can never recover; a one-shot credential-free probe surfaces the usable challenge.

Normal challenge handling remains authoritative. A conformant challenge, or a trusted foreign realm that accepts configured Basic credentials, completes without a cold probe.

## Behavior and safety

- Eligible only when attempt one actually attached an SDK-cached bearer token.
- Recovery runs only after standard resolution fails; conformant registries add no request.
- Limited to replayable GET/HEAD requests and exactly one cold probe.
- Bounded, cancellation-aware buffering releases a live no-challenge 401 before a same-host probe.
- Explicit or default caller authorization bypasses SDK recovery for the selected redirect client.
- Credential failures and non-401 token-endpoint failures remain terminal.
- A malformed `WWW-Authenticate` challenge is itself unusable, and parsing it no longer throws: an eligible stale-token GET/HEAD disposes the 401 and still cold-probes, while a recovery-ineligible caller gets the original 401 returned unchanged (not a surfaced parse error).
- Recovered tokens never refresh empty or opaque cache keys, and the just-received response is disposed if a post-send cache write (e.g. a custom `ICache`) throws.

## Testing

- `dotnet test tests/OrasProject.Oras.Tests/OrasProject.Oras.Tests.csproj --no-restore`
- 614 tests passed.

Привет! Собрал всё, что нужно для новой темы проекта — **анонимная юридическая защита женщин от бытового насилия**.

## 🛠️ Сначала — почему был «error»

В `src/app/page.tsx` строка `subtitle` была оборвана и «съела» поле `cta`:
```
subtitle: "…по законам Республики Казахстан: "Задать вопрос",

Из-за незакрытой кавычки **проект не собирался вообще** — это и была ошибка. Исправлено.

## ✍️ Что поменялось

- **Тексты (твои формулировки):** бейдж «🛡️ Цифровая защита и юридическая поддержка», подзаголовок, 4 карточки-примера и раздел «О проекте».
- **Казахская версия** полностью переведена на новую тему (раньше оставалась про «первую работу»).
- **Метаданные сайта** (вкладка браузера, превью ссылки) — под новую тему.
- **База знаний** (`src/knowledge-base.json`) заменена на статьи о бытовом насилии: закон «О профилактике бытового насилия», **защитное предписание**, Кодекс «О браке (супружестве) и семье», **кризисные центры**. Есть и русские, и казахские ключевые слова, поэтому карточки находят нужный закон на обоих языках.
- **AI-консультант** (`src/app/api/ask/route.ts`) переписан на надёжную схему **«поиск по закону → ответ»**:
  - отвечает **строго по найденным законам** (не выдумывает);
  - **безопасность прежде всего** — первый шаг всегда «звони 102 / 112»;
  - **работает даже без ключа Claude** (раньше без ключа сайт отдавал ошибку). Если добавить `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` в Vercel — Claude формулирует ответ красивее, строго по тем же статьям.

## ✅ Проверено локально

`npm run build` проходит. Все 4 карточки находят нужный закон (RU и KZ), свободный текст «муж угрожает…» → раздел про насилие.

## ⚠️ Важно проверить перед финалом (юридическая точность)

Я **намеренно не выдумывал точные номера статей** — в базе указаны названия законов и ссылка на adilet.zan.kz. Перед защитой стоит:
1. Вписать точные **номера статей** и прямые ссылки на документы с [adilet.zan.kz](https://adilet.zan.kz).
2. Добавить актуальный **номер национальной линии/кризисного центра** (сейчас опора на 102 и 112 — они всегда верны).

После мёржа Vercel сам пересоберёт сайт по той же ссылке.

## Summary

Single rescue branch for the HanaPath exam-programme megabatch. It carries the incorporated work from #329 (Hangul provenance/taint), #330 (sentence-eligibility schema/audit), #331 (Words C1 lesson scaffold), the retired-fleet archival, the **root-cause fix for the failing Android build**, **CI hardening**, and now **Workstream 0 exam-integrity Boxes 0D + 0E** (owner-requested before ship).

Still a draft. See *Residual work* for what remains.

## 1. Root cause fixed — Android "Learning-data audits" failure

**Box 0E — labels, disclosure, backup validation.** Every result screen shows `HanaPath result` / `Practice result` / `Legacy result · provenance incomplete` with a details card (blueprint/engine/bank versions, seed, status, retention linkage). author: webtecnica
body:
Closes #68920

## Problem
Desktop/TUI sessions leak active-session leases. When user does /new, the old session is detached with a 20s orphan-reap delay, but the lease stays active during that window. Multiple rapid /new commands exhaust max_concurrent_sessions.

## Fix
Release the lease immediately on session detach, before the orphan-reap timer starts. _release_active_session_slot is idempotent.

author: krisztiankoos
body:
## Summary

`./start-kimi.sh` (bare, no `--epic`, no prompt) died with `error: Prompt cannot be empty` — the launcher always built `kimi -p "${_forward[*]}" -m k2.7-coding --output-format stream-json`, i.e. an **empty headless prompt** with a **model alias that doesn't exist** in `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` (rejected by both kimi 0.27.0 and 0.28.1: `config.invalid: Model "k2.7-coding" is not configured`).

Fixes:

- **Launch-mode split**: bare launch (no PROMPT, no `--epic`) execs the interactive TUI with no `-p` at all. Headless one-shot (`-p`) only when a prompt exists (explicit PROMPT or epic cold-start); `--output-format stream-json` only when stdout is piped (fleet capture) — a TTY gets plain text.
- **Model aliases**: `k3` / `k2.7` / `k2.7-highspeed` (plus `k2.7-coding` and full `kimi-code/*` ids) map to configured aliases (`kimi-code/k3`, `kimi-code/kimi-for-coding`, `kimi-code/kimi-for-coding-highspeed`). Without `--model`, no `-m` is passed (config.toml `default_model` decides). Unknown models exit 1 before launch.
- **`--help-launcher` read the wrong file**: relative `$0` after `cd "$PROJECT_DIR"` (worktree redirect) resolved to the main checkout, printing code as help. Now reads the script's absolute path captured before any `cd`.
- Header documents the two launch modes; examples corrected.

## Verified live (real CLI, not just stubs)

- Bare launch → `kimi` exec'd with **zero args** (interactive TUI; no empty prompt).
- `--model k2.7 "Reply with exactly: ok"` → resolved to `kimi-code/kimi-for-coding`, headless completed (`{"role":"assistant","content":"ok"}`).
- `--help-launcher` prints only the comment header.

## Tests

`tests/test_start_kimi_launcher.py`: 3 existing cases updated to the new contract, 3 new (bare-launch-is-interactive, parametrized alias mapping ×6, unknown-model-rejected). **11/11 pass**; pre-commit ruff + pytest green.

author: fire
body:
## Summary
FDB's own docs are explicit: **"The default installation runs only one FoundationDB server process per machine (which will use only one CPU core)... Most users will want to maximize performance by running one FoundationDB server process per core"** (via `[fdbserver.<ID>]` sections in `/etc/foundationdb/foundationdb.conf`).

Every FDB-backed job in this CI, including the `ycsb` job that originally measured **workloada collapsing from 3139 to 975 ops/s under write load**, has always installed FDB via the plain `.deb` package, left at this single-process/single-core default. This PR adds `[fdbserver.<ID>]` sections (one per available core via `nproc`) to the `ycsb` job specifically, isolated from any sharding work in #5, to get a clean baseline reading.

## Result: ruled out, not confirmed

Verified the fix actually took effect — `fdbcli status` shows `FoundationDB processes - 4` after the restart (up from 1):

| | READ ops/s | UPDATE ops/s | Combined |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (single fdbserver process, original baseline) | 490.8 | 483.6 | 974.4 |
| After (4 fdbserver processes, this PR) | 428.7 | 436.1 | 864.8 |

**No improvement — if anything, slightly worse, within likely CI noise.** This rules out the single-core-FDB-test-cluster theory as the explanation for the original workloada collapse. Combined with #5's `linear-scaling` benchmark also staying flat under the same multi-process FDB config (1349→1295→1255→1216→1317 ops/s across num_shards=1,2,4,8,16, no trend), **all three bottleneck hypotheses raised this session — namespace-level FDB serialization, `mvstore` process capacity, and FDB test-cluster process count — have now been ruled out by actual measurement, not just left untested.**

## What this means for next steps
The one investigation thread from this session that could actually show *where* time goes in a commit — the `diag/commit-phase-timing` instrumentation (phase 1 existence checks, idempotency/LWV block, PLCC check, final FDB commit, changelog readback) — was started but never completed; the session moved on to the sharding architecture discussion before that run's results came back. Given three plausible architectural explanations are now ruled out, that diagnostic is the clearly indicated next step rather than another architectural guess.

## Test plan
- [x] Confirmed via `fdbcli status`: 4 FDB processes active (up from 1) after the config change
- [x] `ycsb (workloada, 0)` job passes; numbers compared against the pre-existing baseline above

## What changed

`tx stage`, `tx stage status`, `tx stage discard`, and `tx stage commit` crashed with an unhandled `System.ArgumentException` ("The value cannot be an empty string. (Parameter 'path')") when run with no active session and no `--model`. `ActiveModelResolver.ResolveReference` returns an empty `ModelReference` in that case, and `StagingStore.CanonicalSource` calls `Path.GetFullPath` on it.

`StageHandler.Status`, `Discard`, and `CommitAsync` now guard against an empty source reference and return the documented `TOMIX_NO_MODEL` diagnostic (exit 2) with a hint to connect or pass `--model` — the same shape the vertipaq and deploy handlers use. `stage discard --all` deliberately skips the guard: `DiscardAll` never touches the reference, so clearing the whole session still works without a model.

The guard lives in the handler (not the CLI layer) so it protects all three subcommands and any future callers in one place.

## Tests

Two new handler tests in `StageHandlerTests`:
- an empty reference fails with `TOMIX_NO_MODEL` / exit 2 across Status, Discard, and CommitAsync (previously threw)
- `Discard --all` still succeeds without a model

Full suite passes. Smoke-tested with a fresh `TOMIX_CONFIG_DIR`: `tx stage` and `tx stage discard --yes` now print the friendly error with exit 2 instead of a stack trace.

author: time-attack
body:
Takeover of #2545 (credit: @peterostrander2) — not closing it, just referencing.

## Problem
`gbrain sources harden` installs the durability post-commit hook, then `commitScaffolding` commits the scaffolding and immediately pushes. The freshly installed hook fires on that commit and background-pushes (`git pull --rebase` on rejection → `index.lock`), racing the foreground push.

#2545 correctly identified the race but fixed it with `git commit --no-verify`, which only bypasses pre-commit/commit-msg hooks — post-commit hooks still run under `--no-verify` (empirically verified in a scratch repo).

## Fix
- `commitScaffolding` now commits with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, which actually disables all hooks for that one invocation (including a pre-existing custom `core.hooksPath`).
- Corrected the hook template's misleading `# Bypass: git commit --no-verify` comment to document the working bypass.

## Test
`test/brain-repo-durability.serial.test.ts`: new test asserts the scaffolding commit never triggers the hook (the hook's `brain_push` always writes `$GBRAIN_HOME/brain-push.log`; the test asserts it never appears) and that the hook no longer documents the broken bypass. Fails on master (log appears — the hook really fires), passes with the fix.

Gate: `bun run typecheck` exit 0; `bun test test/brain-repo-durability.serial.test.ts` 20 pass / 0 fail. (`test/brain-durability-hook.serial.test.ts` has one unreachable-origin timeout that also fails on unmodified master in this environment — pre-existing.)

author: yebai
body:
Opened for discussion.

See https://github.com/TuringLang/Turing.jl/pull/2853#issuecomment-5358450673 for a subtle correctness issue with #2848. 

Reimplements `SMC` and `PG`/`CSMC` directly on Libtask + DynamicPPL and drops the AdvancedPS
dependency. A rewrite based on #2848 (thanks @charlesknipp; commits co-authored).

Each `observe` is one filtering step: under `ParticleMCMCContext`, every likelihood term
becomes a `Libtask.produce`, so a particle is a suspended model execution we advance, weight,
and resample. The conditional-SMC reference is reproduced by *replaying* a per-particle
`TracedRNG` (no stored trajectory); a fork is reseeded to branch off. Particle state lives in
the task's taped globals (no `task_local_storage`), and `@addlogprob!` reweights via the
likelihood accumulator.

Posteriors, log-evidence, and exact reference reproduction match the old implementation;
`gibbs.jl`, Aqua, and log-density-metadata tests pass; performance is on par.

Fix https://github.com/TuringLang/Turing.jl/issues/2781

body:
## What

Wires the OpenAI Codex CLI in as an optional **second-model reviewer**, in both layers (root dogfoods it; generated repos opt in via the new `use_codex_review` copier answer, **default off** per the no-SaaS-by-default hard rule). Local and advisory only: nothing runs in CI, no PR check depends on Codex, and `verify`/`ci` never invoke it.

- `task challenge` (→ `challenge:codex`) — adversarial review via `codex exec review`: challenges architecture/approach; hunts authz bypasses, data-loss paths, unsafe rollback, races, hidden coupling, operational failure modes, needless complexity. Supports `-- --base <ref> | --uncommitted | --commit <sha>` plus free-text focus.
- `task review` (→ `review:codex`) — verification-checkpoint review (implementation, consistency, tests) before `task ci`.
- `task codex:gate:enable|disable|status` — toggles the Claude Code codex plugin's automatic stop-gate (Stop hook: Codex reviews each editing turn, `ALLOW:`/`BLOCK:`). The script drives the plugin's own companion runtime with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` pinned to its real data dir, so it flips the **same per-workspace flag** as `/codex:setup --enable-review-gate` (verified live: enable → state file `stopReviewGate: true` → disable).
- `.codex/config.toml` — project-level Codex config (review-grade `model_reasoning_effort = "high"`, model unpinned); loads for trusted checkouts.
- AGENTS.md — findings-are-hypotheses adjudication protocol (verify → classify → fix only confirmed → regression-test → explain rejections → adjudication table) with a **3-iteration loop cap** per challenge/review loop; intended flow `check → verify → challenge → review → ci → PR`.
- `docs/guides/codex-review.md` — install/auth, plugin setup, gate mechanics (incl. fail-open when Codex is absent and per-worktree state), troubleshooting.
- `scripts/test-codex-review.sh` (`task test:codex-review`, wired into `verify`/`ci`) — offline stubbed-codex regression tests for target selection.

## ⚠️ Security-relevant settings change (called out per repo policy)

`.claude/settings.json` now declares the `openai-codex` marketplace (`openai/codex-plugin-cc`) and enables `codex@openai-codex`, so **Claude Code auto-offers/installs this third-party plugin for anyone who trusts this folder**. The template ships the same block only when `use_codex_review=true` (the template settings file became `.jinja`; it was already an allowed parity divergence and root-vs-template reconciliation stays manual).

## Dogfood: the adversarial review reviewed itself

`task challenge -- focus on the new codex wiring` ran against this change before commit. Adjudication:

| Finding | Classification | Evidence | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| [P2] Base fallback strips `origin/` from `origin/HEAD`, producing a possibly nonexistent local ref; `rev-list ... \|\| echo 0` then silently reports "Nothing to review" | **Confirmed** | Reproduced in a fixture repo (default branch `develop`, no local main/master): review was silently skipped | Fixed (keep remote-qualified ref + verify it exists, fail loudly otherwise); regression covered by `scripts/test-codex-review.sh` |

One CLI quirk was also found and fixed during smoke testing: `codex exec review` treats custom instructions as their own review mode (mutually exclusive with `--base`/`--uncommitted`/`--commit`), so the script writes the resolved scope into the instructions.

## Verification

- `task verify` — green (lint, guards, dogfood parity, new unit test, full 7-profile render matrix incl. `full` with `use_codex_review=true` and default-off assertions everywhere else)
- `task security` — green (Semgrep CE, gitleaks, audit)
- `PR_TITLE=... task guard:release-title` — releasing title confirmed (`template/` changed)
- Live smoke: real `codex exec review` adversarial run + gate enable/disable round-trip against the actual plugin state file

author: mehdibha
body:
## What

On the home page's **Composition** section, the text-field build-up had two clickable rail stops — "Input" and "TextField". This merges them into a single **"TextField"** stop, with the bare-input beat folded in as an intermediate step.

## Why

"Input" and "TextField" aren't two separate patterns to a reader — the bare input is just the seed the field grows from. Collapsing them to one stop makes the rail read as one coherent field being composed, rather than implying `Input` is a peer destination alongside `TextField`, `InputGroup`, `SearchField`, etc.

## How

The bare-`<Input />` step (`firstStep`) is demoted from a headline (clickable) to a `mid` beat and retitled "TextField". Everything downstream — pagination, step dots, the walk-between-mids logic, active-step highlighting — already keys off the `mid` flag, so no other code changes were needed.

The build-up under the single "TextField" stop is now three mid beats arriving at the full field:

1. `<Input />` — bare (opening frame)
2. wrapped in `<TextField>`
3. `+ <Label>`
4. → **TextField** headline — full field with `<Label>`, `<Input>`, `<Description>`

The opening bare-input beat dwells 2000ms (vs the 1400ms mids after it) since it's the first frame on page load.

## Notes for reviewer

- The rail now opens on "TextField" instead of "Input"; the initial preview frame is still the bare input.
- `pnpm check` and `pnpm typecheck` pass (no new warnings/errors).

body:
## Summary

- Adds `match` as a first-class expression, carried through every compiler stage (AST → TIR → MIR → Opt → Scheduler → Codegen) as a genuine N-way construct rather than desugared to nested `if`/`else`.
- v1 pattern scope: int/char/bool literals, `Enum::Variant`, `_` wildcard — with full exhaustiveness checking (no `_` needed for an enum match once every variant is covered).
- Codegen picks between a WASM `br_table` (dense case values) and a right-nested `if`/`else` chain (sparse), decided once during Opt construction (`Builder::should_use_br_table`) rather than left to the scheduler, so the choice can't desync from the `break`/`continue` depth bookkeeping built alongside it.
- Along the way, found and fixed a pre-existing, match-unrelated bug: `break`/`continue` bypassed a loop's own "commit loop-carried locals" tail code, silently losing a mutation made immediately before an early exit.

Full pipeline walkthrough, design rationale, and both bug writeups (the wrapper-chain depth off-by-one and the loop-param commit bug) are in [`devlog/2026-07-21-match-expression-and-br-table.md`](devlog/2026-07-21-match-expression-and-br-table.md).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p wx-compiler` — 668 passing (AST/TIR/MIR/Opt/scheduler tests per stage, plus wasmtime execution tests for int match, enum dispatch, and match-inside-loop break/continue for both the sparse and dense `br_table` paths)

author: srid
body:
**A bare padi launch no longer silently inherits production's state-root.** Binding now requires `KOLU_PADI_STATE_DIR` or `--state-root` — the same fail-fast shape server already uses for `KOLU_STATE_DIR`. Production nix wrappers still supply `~/.local/state/padi`; `pnpm dev` and tests keep private dirs.

Closes #1334. Implements SI2 from the [state-isolation plan](https://kolu.dev/atlas/state-isolation.html) (PR #1930 thread: delete the default, no `KOLU_ROLE`).

### Why

A daemon's identity is the digest of its state-root. `resolvePadiStateRoot()` used to fall back to `~/.local/state/padi` — production's chair — so a forgotten env could adopt or disrupt the live instance. The accident is now **unspellable**: no path, no bind.

### Shape

| Piece | What |
| --- | --- |
| Bind resolve | unset + no override → one-line crash naming `KOLU_PADI_STATE_DIR` |
| Wrappers | kolu + padi export `KOLU_PADI_STATE_DIR=…:-$HOME/.local/state/padi` (remote-shipped padi included) |
| Discovery / TUIs | still name the production formula for “none found” errors — not a bind path |
| Boot order | resolve identity **before** opening the daemon log file under that root |

> No role env, markers, or kaval changes. Wire-verb residual stays in #1912.

### Design philosophy

- **Fail-fast** — no silent default, no badge/knob override path.
- **Not electricity** — path policy stays in padi’s soul; surface-daemon still takes resolved gate/socket.
- **Reuse** — mirrors existing `KOLU_STATE_DIR` refuse pattern in `state.ts`.

### Try it locally

```sh
nix run github:juspay/kolu/fix/1334-padi-state-root-no-default
```

Las marcas del desplegable empezaban **cada una en una sangría distinta**, así que la lista se leía como texto centrado en vez de como una tabla.

body:
## Summary

You reported that dragging a task to a different column on the Task Board sometimes doesn't update its status, and separately hit a red "The board changed elsewhere before your drag finished" toast on a board with 23 tasks all in one column. Both trace back to the same file: `frontend/src/components/tasks/KanbanBoard.tsx`'s `handleDragEnd`.

**Fix 1 — trust the actual drop target.** `handleDragEnd` was determining the destination column by re-deriving it from local `columns` state (`findColumn(active.id)`), assuming that state had already absorbed the live drag-over move. If the last drag-over update and the drop landed in the same render tick, that assumption could be wrong, and the dragged task would get saved with its *original* status instead of the column it was actually dropped into — the status change would silently no-op. The fix always trusts dnd-kit's own `over` result from the drop event itself as the destination, which is authoritative for that exact drop regardless of whether local state has caught up.

**Fix 2 — stop resending the whole board on every drag.** Every drag (even one that only moves a single card) was resending status/position for *all* tasks across *all* columns, each carrying its last-known `version` for the optimistic-concurrency check. That meant a single stale version on any one of the ~20 untouched tasks elsewhere on the board could reject the entire batch with a 409 and reload the board — exactly the toast in your screenshot. The reorder payload is now scoped to only the column(s) that actually changed: source + destination for a cross-column move, or just the one column for a same-column reorder.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc -b && vite build` passes clean
- [x] Verified against a throwaway mock backend (23 seeded tasks matching your screenshot's shape) — confirmed the reorder payload correctly reflects the drop destination and no longer includes untouched columns' tasks
- [ ] Brent: please re-test dragging a card between columns on a real board and confirm status updates and no more spurious "board changed elsewhere" reloads

No migration needed — frontend-only change.

author: nrjdalal
body:
## What

Two related video-player improvements.

### Resume playback
Reopening a video continues ~5s before where you left off. A shared `useResumePosition` hook saves the position per file (keyed `infoHash:fileIndex`, not the stream URL whose port changes each launch) every 5s and on close, into the server-side prefs blob so it survives desktop restarts, and clears it once the file is watched to within 15s of the end (a finished video restarts). Works in both the native mpv player (desktop) and the browser libmedia player.

### Steadier controls
- **Play/pause** "worked only after a click or two": `togglePlay` decided from a ref refreshed a render late while the real state arrived from async player events, so a quick second click undid the first. It now decides from the freshest state (syncs the ref, flips optimistically) in both players.
- **Scrubber** thumb fought playback updates while dragging. A shared `useScrubbing` hook freezes the position during a drag and resets on every drag-end path (pointer up / cancel / lost-capture) so it can never get stuck.
- libmedia player commands (`resume`/`pause`/`seek`/`selectSubtitle`) are now `.catch`-guarded (mpv already was).

## Files
- new: `lib/use-resume-position.ts`, `lib/use-scrubbing.ts`
- `lib/prefs-store.ts`, `components/torrents/{mpv-player,libmedia-player,file-tree}.tsx`
- docs: `README.md`, `.agents/skills/design/SKILL.md`

## Review
Reviewed across three axes (Standards / Spec / Correctness) plus a verification pass. Standards clean; both specs faithful with no scope creep; four correctness findings (scrubber stuck on pointer-cancel, libmedia unhandled rejections, finished-video resurrect, cross-file ref reset) were fixed and re-verified. `check-types`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and the production `next build` all pass (pre-commit hooks green).

Known minor edges left as-is: a video opened in the brief window before prefs rehydrate on launch won't resume; an optimistic play/pause won't self-correct if the underlying player command fails (rare, local IPC). Desktop resume was confirmed working by hand; the control fixes are verified by review and reasoning (the mpv player can't be scripted in a browser).

body:
## Summary

Closes #7082. Same pattern as #7465/#7466/#7481/#7491/#7506/#7527/#7538/#7551/#7559: the issue's original surface (`sn-69-taomarketcap-subnet-api`) still verifies exactly as documented — live-verified 2026-07-21 (~21:45 UTC): HTTP 200 `application/json`, no auth, real SN69 snapshot body (also pinned by the already-merged verify test `tests/sn69-call-subnet-surface-verify.test.mjs` from #7332, which still passes against this diff) — and the issue's own "Additional surface(s) found during review (now in scope)" section itemizes the remaining registry gap. This PR registers all of it.

## What this adds (36 new surfaces)

Fetched the subnet's own OpenAPI schema (`https://api.heraldmedia.ai/openapi.json` — live-verified 2026-07-21 ~21:33 UTC: 200, exactly the **36 paths** the issue counted) and diffed against the registry: **0 of the 36 paths were covered** — the file's 5 existing surfaces are the website, the source repo, two raw-GitHub data artifacts, and the third-party TaoMarketCap snapshot; none touch the first-party API domain. 36 paths − 0 already covered = **36 missing**, one surface per path, matching the issue's itemized list exactly.

Six paths (`/admin/briefs`, `/admin/reporters`, `/contact`, `/disputes`, `/funding`, `/reveals`) carry both a GET and a POST operation on the same URL; this repo's one-surface-per-URL rule (`validate:surface`'s duplicate-URL check, #5737) keys surfaces by URL, so each such path is one surface with the POST counterpart and its token gate documented in that surface's `notes` — every operation in the issue's list is represented.

**12 public, fixed or optional-query-only, no-auth (`probe.enabled:true`)** — live-verified 2026-07-21 (~21:33 UTC), each with an unparameterized request: `/health` 200, `/briefs` 200, `/api/v2/validator/briefs` 200 (signed payload), `/registry/outlets.json` 200 (the API-served live version, distinct from the already-registered static `outlets.seed.json` on raw GitHub), `/api/v3/validator/registry` 200, `/reporting/export` 200, `/disputes` 200, `/funding` 200, `/public/articles` 200, `/public/stats` 200, `/public/leaderboard` 200 — and `/ready` **503** with a well-formed JSON readiness body (a real endpoint currently reporting not-ready — registered anyway per the issue's own Targon-precedent instruction; the probe reflects real status). Note on `/funding`: the issue grouped it with the auth-gated set ("same `/admin`-adjacent auth posture, not spot-verified individually"), but the schema declares no header params on the GET and it live-verifies **200 no-auth** — registered per observed reality, per the issue's own "every claim has to trace back to a request you actually made."

**4 public, required-query-param (`probe.enabled:false`)**: `/public/subnet/status`, `/public/epochs`, `/public/validators`, `/public/commitments`. Live-verified 2026-07-21 (~21:33 UTC), both directions on all four: unparameterized → HTTP 422 listing the exact required `network`/`netuid` fields (live validation, not an auth error); with `network=finney&netuid=69` → HTTP 200 real JSON (e.g. `/public/subnet/status` returns the live finalized-block/neuron snapshot). Callable today via `call_subnet_surface`'s own `query` argument.

**1 public SSE stream (`kind:"sse"`, `probe.enabled:false`)**: `/public/events`. The issue listed it with the query-param JSON group, but live verification (2026-07-21 ~21:35 UTC, `network=finney&netuid=69`) shows HTTP 200 with `content-type: text/event-stream` — a long-lived Server-Sent Events stream of `finalized_block`/indexer events, not a one-shot JSON body; unparameterized → 422 listing the required fields. Registered `kind:"sse"` accordingly (matching the registry's existing SSE-surface convention).

**1 public path-param (`probe.enabled:false`, literal `{brief_id}` template percent-encoded in the `url` since raw braces fail the `url` `format:"uri"` schema check)**: `/public/briefs/{brief_id}/economics`. Live-verified 2026-07-21 (~21:34 UTC) with a placeholder id: without query params → 422 listing the required `network`/`netuid` fields (the placeholder path segment itself is accepted); with `network=finney&netuid=69` → 404 `{"detail":"no confirmed economics for brief"}` — a clean domain not-found, not an auth gate.

**7 auth-gated GET (`auth_required:true`, `auth:{scheme:"custom",location:"header",...}`, `probe.enabled:false`)** — every one individually live-verified 2026-07-21 (~21:33 UTC): HTTP 401 `{"detail":"unauthorized"}` unauthenticated: `/admin/briefs`, `/admin/reporters`, `/admin/registry/draft` (x-admin-token), `/validator/results` (x-results-token), `/reveals` (x-reveals-token), `/users/coverage`, `/contact` (x-service-token). Three of these (`/validator/results`, `/reveals`, `/users/coverage`) were listed as no-auth in the issue's review section, but they 401 live — the schema declares their token headers `required:false`, yet the app enforces them; registered per observed reality with the evidence in each surface's notes.

**11 auth-gated write-only POST (`auth_required:true`, `probe.enabled:false`)** — the issue's remaining itemized operations, each on its own unique URL: `/admin/briefs/{brief_id}/close`, `/admin/briefs/{brief_id}/fund`, `/admin/registry/editions`, `/admin/registry/outlets`, `/admin/registry/outlets/{outlet_id}/status`, `/admin/registry/discard` (x-admin-token); `/results`, `/api/v3/validator/snapshots`, `/api/v3/validator/weight-receipts` (x-results-token); `/users/upsert`, `/contact/{contact_id}/status` (x-service-token). Registered per the issue's own instruction for the auth-gated set ("register with `auth_required:true`, `probe.enabled:false`"). Not spot-verified individually — the issue's own section says the write endpoints were "not spot-verified individually," and an unauthenticated state-changing POST against a production validator-facing system isn't a safe verification to run — but each token gate is live-verified enforced (401) on a sibling GET carrying the same header (x-admin-token → `GET /admin/briefs`; x-results-token → `GET /validator/results`; x-service-token → `GET /contact`), and the registration follows the same merged precedent as #7540 (SN59)'s POST-operation surfaces.

## Schema/tooling notes (same as the lineage)

- `probe.method` only accepts `GET, HEAD, JSON-RPC, WSS-RPC` — every query-param/path-param/auth-gated/POST surface here is `probe.enabled:false`; the 12 fixed no-auth GETs keep live probes.
- Path-param URLs use the percent-encoded brace form (`%7Bbrief_id%7D`, `%7Boutlet_id%7D`, `%7Bcontact_id%7D`).
- Registered `provider: "herald"` — matches the file's existing first-party surfaces and the registered `registry/providers/herald.json` entry, checked before generating.
- The auth-gated surfaces use `auth.scheme:"custom"` with the literal `x-*-token` header name — these are per-operation header parameters in the schema, not a formal `securitySchemes` entry; no `value_format` is asserted since the token format isn't publicly documented.
- Strictly append-only into `surfaces[]`: **+900/−0**, top-level `notes`/`curation` untouched. (The file's `gap_notes` still carry a now-stale "no verified first-party API/OpenAPI schema" line — left alone as maintainer-owned metadata; flagged here in prose instead.)
- `public/metagraph/operational-surfaces.json` changed on `npm run build` but is **not** in this diff — committed-but-excluded from the freshness gate per `reference.md`.

- [x] `npm run validate:surface -- registry/subnets/ain.json` — 41 surfaces, passed
- [x] `npm run scan:public-safety` — passed
- [x] `npm run build && npm run validate` — 129 subnets, 2634 total surfaces, clean

author: uny
body:
Keep construction-time disk I/O off the caller thread (#55)

Closes #55.

## Problem

`Autograph { }` runs on the caller thread — frequently the Android/iOS main thread (a Compose
`LaunchedEffect`) — and did synchronous disk I/O during construction:

- `platformSeqStore()` → `FileSeqStore(dir)` read the JSON state file in its constructor (`load()`).
- `Stamper`'s `init{}` read the store and, on a **cold start** (no stored session, or an expired one),
  called `startNewSession()` → `store.flush()` — a file **write**, not just a read. Under
  `SeqPersistence.Chunked` it additionally reserved the current block with two `putLong`s + a `flush()`.

So even the default (EveryEvent) configuration read *and wrote* the state file on the caller thread the
first time a tracker was built. This can trip StrictMode and cause main-thread jank.

## Fix

Defer that I/O to the first operation, which for a core-stamping tracker runs on the serial dispatcher
— off the caller thread — without weakening the sequence-uniqueness guarantee:

- `FileSeqStore` loads its map lazily (`by lazy { load() }`, SYNCHRONIZED); the constructor does no read.
- `Stamper`'s `init{}` work moves into `ensureStarted(now)`, guarded by a `started` flag under the
  existing lock and invoked at the top of every operation (`stamp`, `notifyForeground`,
  `notifyBackground`, `reset`). Construction touches the store zero times.

No `AutographConfig`/public-API change; `checkKotlinAbi` is unchanged on both dumps.

### Why the sequence-uniqueness guarantee still holds

A sequence number only escapes through `stamp()`, and `ensureStarted()` completes the chunk
reservation *within the same lock, before* the first number is handed out — it moved from
construction-time to first-operation-time, but is still ordered before any number it protects.
`reset()` calls `ensureStarted()` first on purpose: `startNewSession()` preserves the device-lifetime
`globalSeq`, so a reset that is the very first operation must load the persisted counter before
rotating, or it would re-hand-out already-emitted numbers.

### Behavior notes (deliberate, not silent)

- **`session_start` is now the first *operation's* time, not construction time.** The first `stamp`
  opens its session at its own `event_timestamp`, which *preserves* the `event_timestamp >= session.start`
  ordering a downstream consumer might rely on. (An earlier draft eagerly "warmed up" the stamper on the
  dispatcher at construction; that was dropped because it opened the session at warm-up-execution time and
  could put `session.start` a hair *after* an already-queued event's timestamp — a new inversion for no
  real gain.)
- **A lifecycle call (`notifyForeground`/`notifyBackground`) or `reset` that precedes any event performs
  the one-time load on its own (synchronous) caller thread** — the same place `notifyBackground` already
  does its session flush today. #55 targets *construction*; both are unchanged from the existing
  lifecycle-I/O contract.
- **Failure timing shifts.** A store I/O failure (e.g. a disk-full reservation `flush()`) used to crash
  `Autograph { }` synchronously; it now surfaces on the first operation instead — swallowed by the
  delivery `CoroutineExceptionHandler` on the stamping path (the event is dropped and the next operation
  retries, since `started` is only set after a full pass), or thrown on the lifecycle thread as
  `notifyBackground`'s flush already could. Uniqueness is intact throughout (nothing escapes before
  `started`).

## Tests

- New `constructionDoesNoStoreWritesUntilFirstOperation` — asserts the store is neither read nor written
  at construction, and both happen on the first operation. **Fault-injected**: restoring an eager
  `init{ ensureStarted() }` reddens exactly this test (verified) and nothing else. `NonDurableSeqStore`
  gained a `readCount` so the detector catches a restored eager *read* (the heaviest I/O), not only a write.
- `chunkedSingleCounterModePersistsOnlyAtBoundaries` rewritten to capture the write count *after* the
  first stamp (construction no longer writes), still guarding non-boundary batching.
- Stale "reserved and flushed to disk at construction" comment in `FileSeqStoreDurabilityTest` updated.
- All existing Stamper / FileSeqStore / durability / tracker tests pass unchanged (JVM + iosSimulatorArm64).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
  * Deferred loading of persisted sequence and session state until the first operation, reducing work during initialization.
  * Avoided disk access when creating a store or stamper.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Preserved sequence counters and session state across resets and delayed initialization.
  * Maintained reliable persistence at chunk boundaries while preventing unnecessary writes between boundaries.

author: costajohnt
body:
## Summary

Two coupled grading defects, now unblocked by `@oss-scout/core@1.5.0` (which supplies the repo-intrinsic merge signal).

**#248** - the success grade derived `mergeRate` only from the viewer's own merged/closed counts, so a healthy repo we'd never contributed to had a null merge signal and collapsed to the bottom band (F). `deriveGradeSignals` now prefers scout's `projectHealth.recentMergeRate` and falls back to the relationship-derived rate only when scout didn't supply one, preserving prior behavior for repos with contribution history.

**#1575 defect 2** - scout emits `recommendation: approve` without consulting the grade, so `approve` could coexist with a bottom-band grade. `reconcileRecommendation` downgrades such an `approve` to `needs_review` (never a hard skip). Applied only on the `vet` / `vet-list` surfaces, where the grade is computed from freshly fetched health; `search` and `features` grade from history alone (a `checkFailed` sentinel), so reconciling there would wrongly downgrade well-vetted new repos.

## Changes

- `core/issue-grading.ts` - prefer `recentMergeRate` in `deriveGradeSignals`; add `reconcileRecommendation` + `KEEP_GRADE_THRESHOLD`.
- `commands/vet.ts`, `commands/vet-list.ts` - reconcile the recommendation against the grade.
- `packages/core/package.json` - bump `@oss-scout/core` to `^1.5.0` (supplies `recentMergeRate`).

## Related Issues

Closes #1575
Closes costajohnt/oss-scout#248

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass (`pnpm test`) - 3015 core tests; new tests cover the `recentMergeRate` preference, the new-repo-no-longer-F case, and the reconcile thresholds.
- [x] Commits follow conventional format
- [x] No manual version bumps or CHANGELOG edits (release-please)

author: fortizfe
body:
## Summary
- Collapses the three existing workflows (`ci.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `deploy.yml`) into a single `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Pipeline order: `[analyze (CodeQL), checks, e2e]` → deploy (`deploy-preview` on PR, `deploy-production` on push to `main`) → `version` (semantic-release)
- Each stage is gated on the previous one via native `needs:`/`if:` job dependencies, replacing the old cross-workflow `wait-on-check-action` polling
- `deploy-production` (and `version`) continue to skip on the release's own `[version bump]` commit, preventing a redeploy/re-release loop
- Job/check `name:` values are preserved verbatim so branch protection's required status checks keep matching with no reconfiguration
- CodeQL's own severity-based merge blocking (High/Critical findings) is untouched — it remains the separate branch-protection code-scanning check's responsibility, not this pipeline's job graph (see spec Clarifications)

Full spec, plan, research, and task breakdown are in `specs/007-unified-ci-workflow/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml` passes with zero errors
- [x] Confirmed exactly one workflow file remains in `.github/workflows/`
- [ ] Watch this PR's own Actions run: `analyze`/`checks`/`e2e` run in parallel, `deploy-preview` only starts after all three succeed, preview URL is commented on this PR
- [ ] After merge to `main`: confirm `deploy-production` runs after checks, then `version` runs after `deploy-production` succeeds and produces a release commit
- [ ] Confirm branch protection's required status checks (`Type-check, lint, and test with coverage`, `Playwright E2E (Firebase Emulator Suite)`, `CodeQL`) still report correctly with no manual reconfiguration
